Sports.title: Ex-Fulham player tied up by armed robbers in terrifying incident
Sports.content:
Ex-Fulham player tied up by armed robbers in terrifying incident

Former Fulham goalkeeper Sergio Rico was the victim of an armed robbery at his family home on Monday night.

The terrifying attack took place whilst the 33-year-old was having dinner with his wife and two children, including their baby son.

3 Rico and his wife were the victims of a violent attack at their family home Credit: instagram

According to reports, Rico was tied up after five masked raiders forced their way into the family's property near Seville.

His wife, influencer Alba Silva, was also threatened during the violent break-in.

Details of break-in at Rico's family home

Reports also claim Alba's mother had a gun put to her head by one of the intruders.

Meanwhile, accomplices ransacked the house, taking valuables including cash, jewellery and designer handbags.

The family had been at the dinner table at their home in Bollullos de la Mitacion when the attack occurred.

As well as Rico, Alba, their two children and Alba's mother, the family's maid was also present at the time of the break-in.

Police are now investigating the incident, but no arrests are understood to have been made as of yet.

Alba took to Instagram on Tuesday, revealing she remained traumatised by the ordeal.

In a post shared to her 255,000 followers, she wrote: "I’m still in shock after what happened, I am without words.

"But the only really important thing is that thanks to God our family is safe. Thank you to everyone for your concern."

3 The couple's children as well as Alba's mother and the family maid were present when the attack occurred Credit: instagram @ albasilvat

Rico has yet to address the incident on social media, but contacted Spanish reporters to admit the attackers were extremely violent.

However, he refuted reports which had claimed he was badly beaten during the attack.

It comes after Villarreal goalkeeper Peter Gulacsi and his wife were targeted whilst they slept ahead of his side's Champions League clash with Napoli last week.

The former Liverpool stopper was subsequently ruled out of the match following the ordeal.

Burnley's Largie Ramazani also had his home burgled in May whilst playing for Valencia during a previous loan spell from Leeds United.

Who is Sergio Rico?

Rico spent the 2018/19 season in the Premier League after joining Fulham on loan from Sevilla.

3 Rico spent the 2018/19 season on loan at Fulham from Sevilla Credit: Getty

The former Spain international made 29 league appearances for the Cottagers as they were relegated from the top-flight.

He later joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won six trophies including two Ligue 1 titles.

Following spells with Mallorca and Qatari side Al Gharafa, Rico retired at the end of last season aged 32.

The two-time Europa League winner was also left in a coma for nearly three weeks after being hit by a mule cart and runaway horse in May 2023.

Rico spent 36 days in intensive care following the accident, which occurred during an annual pilgrimage in south-west Spain.

He was ultimately discharged from hospital almost three months later in August 2023.

Sports.title: Phil Foden warned uncapped star and three other players still ahead of him before England recall
Sports.content:
Phil Foden warned uncapped star and three other players still ahead of him before England recall

Phil Foden has been told an uncapped Premier League star is more deserving of an England call-up than the in-form midfielder.

It follows calls for Foden to be handed a Three Lions return following his hat-trick for Manchester City on Tuesday night.

3 Foden's recent City form does not warrant an England recall, says Gabby Agbonlahor Credit: Getty

The 26-year-old scored three goals and added an assist in a 5-1 home win over AEK Athens in the Champions League.

Having also scored against Ipswich Town at the weekend, Foden now has four goals and three assists in eight appearances across all competitions.

Despite a recent suspension for a red card in the Manchester derby, he has started all but one of his outings under Enzo Maresca so far this term.

However, talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor remains unconvinced Foden is far enough up the England pecking order to receive a recall.

Thomas Tuchel has not included him since the March friendlies against Uruguay and Japan.

As well as missing out on a place in the World Cup squad, Foden was also left out for the recent Nations League matches against Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia.

Does Foden deserve an England recall?

Following Foden's display against AEK, Agbonlahor was asked by Alan Brazil on Breakfast if he would grant Foden an England recall.

The former Aston Villa striker responded by explaining: "No, not yet. For the reasons of, Jude Belingham, let’s just forget about him, he’s out there on his own as our No.1 choice No.10.

"Then the manager loves Morgan Rogers, rightly so, fantastic player, he can do it on the left or right, but he does love that No.10 position.

"And also I’ll put Cole Palmer still ahead of Phil Foden, fantastic hat-trick last night, but Cole Palmer started off the season well."

3 Josh King is the latest promising Premier League youngster tipped for an England call-up Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

As for who could earn a call-up next month, he added: "You’ve got Palmer there, he’s got two goals, three assists in the Premier League so far this season.

"But after Palmer, before (Morgan) Gibbs-White, before (Eberechi) Eze, before Foden, before (James) Maddison, who’s coming back now and who’s looking to get back into it, I would go with Josh King.

"He’s got two goals in the Premier League this season, if I watch him for Fulham, and obviously it’s harder for Fulham, they haven’t got the players like Chelsea, Manchester City and Real Madrid. Whenever I watch him, he’s some player."

Josh King has yet to make his senior international debut but has already featured nine times for England's Under-21s.

The 19-year-old was also called up for the World Cup warm-up matches against New Zealand and Costa Rica in June.

King has started each of Fulham's opening seven Premier League matches this season, scoring twice.

3 Foden has scored four goals and added three assists for City so far this season Credit: Getty

England's No.10 options

Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer were all included by Tuchel for the September and October internationals along with Arsenal's Eberechi Eze.

However, Palmer later withdrew from the squad and was replaced by Morgan Gibbs-White.

It leaves Foden stranded on 49 senior caps for the Three Lions since making his debut aged 20 under Gareth Southgate back in 2020.

He has since scored four goals for England as well as featuring at Euro 2020, the 2022 World Cup and Euro 2024.

Tuchel will name his next squad at the start of November ahead of the conclusion to the Nations League league phase.

England host Croatia on November 12 before a trip to Madrid to face Spain three days later.

Sports.title: New development in Man City case as another regulator makes fresh inquiries
Sports.content:
The UK audit regulator is making inquiries into alleged accounting irregularities at Man City.

Dame Jayne-Anne Gadhia, chair of the Financial Reporting Council [FRC], said in a letter the watchdog was making preliminary enquiries to assess whether there are formal grounds to open an investigation.

2 Foden scored a hat-trick as Man City beat AEK Athens in the Champions League Credit: Getty

Man City were found guilty in September on all charges relating to Premier League financial rule breaches from 2009 to 2018, and have since launched an appeal.

City were adjudged to have artificially inflated their revenue by £900million via 'sham' contracts.

City launched an appeal on October 2, and claim they are backed by a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence'.

A wide range of sanctions are available, including huge fines, points deductions, and stripping of titles.

City auditors under microscope

The FRC can look into the conduct of BDO, City's auditors, to assess whether the audit was in line with the rules.

City is not classified as a 'public interest entity', a designation given to listed companies, banks and insurers.

The responsibility for overseeing the quality of its accounting and audits initially fell to the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales.

The FRC can apply sanctions if it finds any evidence of wrongdoing.

It can also apply sanctions to individuals such as directors or employees of the club, if they are members of professional accountancy bodies.

BDO advises a number of Premier League and Championship clubs on their accounts, and is the fifth-largest accountancy firm in the UK.

2 City have appealed against the findings of an independent commission Credit: Getty

Two of BDO’s most senior partners led its audits of City.

Liam Byrne, chair of the business select committee, called for greater powers for the FRC to look into similar cases.

He wrote on X: "The regulator's letter exposes gaps in its ability to compel evidence from the club and pursue directors who fall outside its disciplinary rules.

"This raises serious questions about the powers available to hold companies and directors to account.

"The government has a responsibility to explain why reforms to close these gaps were abandoned - and what will now be done to strengthen accountability."

Sports.title: Tottenham urged to make immediate move for €18m-rated star outscoring Harry Kane
Sports.content:
Younes Ebnoutalib is not ready to take Tottenham to the next level - but that shouldn't stop the club from making a move for him now.

That is the verdict of European football expert Andy Brassell, who believes Spurs should capitalise on the chaos at Eintracht Frankfurt.



7 Ebnoutalib has enjoyed a meteoric rise to the top of German football Credit: AFP

Who is Younes Ebnoutalib?

The 23-year-old, who is valued at around €18m, has scored six goals and provided two assists in seven games across all competitions this season.

The most recent of which was the winner against FC Koln on Friday, in which Tottenham scouts were reported to have been in attendance.

Spurs loanee Mikey Moore appeared off the bench for the visitors in that fixture, but it was Ebnoutalib who made the difference.



The latter recently won his first two caps for Germany under Jurgen Klopp last month as a reward for his meteoric rise to the Bundesliga.

Ebnoutalib was playing in the fourth-tier in his homeland as recently as December 2024 before he joined Elversburg a month later.



The striker netted 12 goals in 17 games at the start of last season for the newly-promoted Bundesliga team, who were then residing in the second division.

His form meant Ebnoutalib jumped to the top level of the German pyramid six months earlier than Elversburg after he completed a £6.9m move to Frankfurt, his hometown club, last December.



Frankfurt's No.11 has now hit the ground running this campaign, after an injury-hit first half-season to attract interest from abroad.

And Brassell explained exclusively to talkSPORT.com why it might be a shrewd move for suitors to make an early play for his services.

Bundesliga top scorers 2026/27 Patrik Schick (Bayer Leverkusen) - 6 goals Niclas Füllkrug (Werder Bremen) - 6 goals Younes Ebnoutalib (Frankfurt) - 5 goals Michael Olise (Bayern Munich) - 5 goals Phillip Tietz (Mainz) - 5 goals Harry Kane (Bayern Munich) - 4 goals

7 Ebnoutalib, who played for Morocco's under-15, is now a fully fledged Germany international under Klopp Credit: Getty

Ebnoutalib to Tottenham?

Tottenham spent more than £200million in the summer after only just surviving Premier League relegation last term.



Sandro Tonali was signed from Newcastle for £100m, Mateus Fernandes joined from West Ham for £85m, and Jan Paul van Hecke arrived in North London from Brighton for £52m.

However, Spurs still look light in attack, having sold Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough and exiled Richarlison from the senior squad.

Dominic Solanke has managed just one Premier League goal this term, with Omar Marmoush finally breaking his duck on Monday.

Marmoush's successor at Frankfurt, Ebnoutalib, may still be a work in progress - but the departure of the club's no-nonsense sporting director, Markus Krösche, may land Spurs a bargain.



7 Marmoush scored his first Tottenham goal on his sixth Premier League appearance for the club to help secure a crucial 3-1 victory over Coventry City Credit: Getty

Brassell told talkSPORT: "I really like Younes Ebnoutalib, because he's come through, like a few players have, through Elversburg.

"Ebnoutalib is a player who has great movement; he's a really good finisher. He's also inexperienced at the top level.

"So he's been brought into the Germany squad by Jürgen Klopp, and I think it's great that Klopp is getting a look at younger players.



"Younes Ebnoutalib has been held up by injury, which has spoiled a lot of the back of last season for him.

"He signed for Eintracht Frankfurt, scored straight away and then got injured straight away after that.

"So the fact that he's been called into the Germany squad shows you that people really believe in his potential. Hat-trick on the first day of the season at Union as well, the winner on Friday against Koln.

7 Ebnoutalib’s style of play has been likened to Germany legend Miroslav Klose Credit: Getty



"The good thing about trying to buy him now, I think, would be a potential power vacuum for Eintracht Frankfurt."

Why Krösche's exit will help Spurs

Krösche went to Eintracht in 2021; in that time, they went from a club that was ballast in the Bundesliga to a team that won the Europa League, which qualified for the Champions League twice.

"They developed coaches and players at a great rate," Brassell added. "You look at some of the sales under him, like big money sales.

"Willian Pacho, Randal Kolo Muani, Hugo Ekitike, who I remember came as a sort of PSG flop really, to all intents and purposes.



"Now he's playing for one of the biggest clubs in the world - he was in the France squad before the injury.

"Omar Marmoush has been another one, of course. They took him on to the next level.

"Firstly, you think, okay, maybe there is a bit of a power vacuum at Eintracht Frankfurt at the moment.

7 Kroesche, who built a reputation for selling players at significant profit during his Frankfurt tenure, has since been linked with Milan Credit: Getty



"So maybe, if I make my offer for this star of tomorrow, and that's what he is. He's not a guarantee of a ton of goals yet in the Premier League at a meaningful level. At least not yet.

"He might be in the future, but he's not yet. So you think, maybe I'll make my offer and I won't be completely held feet to the fire by Krösche, who's very good at extracting maximum value for some of those players.

"The other thing is, when you have such an immense figure move on from the club, people do talk. I think it does create a little bit of uneasiness.

"So I think there will be players going, 'Is Eintracht still the place for me to develop?' I think not only do you look at the players who have gone there and developed, but you look at how they've tried to get to the next level.



"I suppose it was a bit of a frustration for Krösche and for the club in general. The players that have nearly signed there over the last year and a half or so."

7 "I saw his first game of the season for Eintracht and said to myself, ‘What a player! Where did they find him?’" Klopp said after calling up Ebnoutalib Credit: AFP

Jobe Bellingham held talks with Frankfurt over a move from Sunderland before he joined Bundesliga rivals Borussia Dortmund.

His English compatriot James McAtee also snubbed Adi Hutter's men in the same summer of 2025 in favour of Nottingham Forest.



Brassell told talkSPORT: "I think it must have been tough for Krösche, the fact that we're really close to getting these players who could turn into absolutely world-class players. But we can't quite get it over the line.

"And that feeling that Eintracht Frankfurt could be the next Dortmund, or the next Monaco; that finishing school for elite players. Play here, have one and a half or two good years, and you'll be headed for absolutely elite stardom. They weren't quite there.

7 Ebnoutalib has worked his way up through the German pyramid and has scored more Bundesliga goals this season than Harry Kane Credit: Getty

"I guess the question I would like to know the answer to, and we're going to find out in the next six to twelve months, is once Krösche's out the door, do players still have that feeling about them?



"So I think for those reasons, even if he's not ready, even if he's like a prospect for the future, even if he's a stash pick or whatever, maybe this is the right time for Tottenham to make a move.

"In terms of him being the finished article, Ebnoutalib, to help them now, or to help them in January, to take them to that next level, I don't think he's ready.

"Maybe though, the deal makes some sort of financial and sporting sense in the sense that, right, get him now, while the club's in this sort of transitional period, and maybe we get a slightly better deal than we normally would.

"And then maybe, whether we bring him on and use him in the squad, or whether we loan him somewhere and then bring him in later, you know, sort of Luka Vuskovic situation. I think that's a fair question to ask.

Sports.title: EFL strugglers sack manager just two hours after game amid dreadful run
Sports.content:
EFL strugglers sack manager just two hours after game amid dreadful run

Crawley Town have sacked head coach Colin Kazim-Richards following their 3-2 defeat to Shrewsbury on Tuesday night.

The club made the announcement shortly after midnight, barely two hours after their League Two clash.



2 Kazim-Richards was appointed Crawley head coach in March Credit: Getty

Crawley are rooted to the bottom of the table with just five points from 10 games.

They remain six points from safety with the very real threat of dropping down to the National League.

In a statement, the club said: "Crawley Town Football Club can confirm that Head Coach Colin Kazim-Richards and Assistant Head Coach Julian Gray have been relieved of their duties with immediate effect.



"Director of Football Erdem Konyar will also be leaving the club.

"The club would like to place on record its sincere thanks to Colin and Julian, who joined during a challenging period and played an important role in securing the club’s EFL status at the end of last season.

"We would also like to thank Erdem for his hard work and commitment since returning to the club last year.



"All three depart with the best wishes of everyone at Crawley Town, and we wish them every success in their future endeavours. The club will make no further comment at this time."

Kazim-Richards at Crawley

The former Premier League forward was a coach in Arsenal's academy before landing his first head coach job at Crawley.



He was appointed in March 2026 with the club facing relegation to the National League.

They were just a point above the drop when he was hired, but managed to keep them in League Two on the final day.

2 Kazim-Richards kept Crawley in the football league just five months ago Credit: Getty

Kazim-Richards signed a new contract shortly after, but 10 games into the new season he has been axed.



Kazim-Richards' career

Kazim-Richards had an extensive career that saw him play in every English professional league: from League Two to the Premier League.

He started his professional career at Bury before moving to Brighton and then playing in the top flight with Sheffield United.

His extensive career also saw him travel across the world, featuring for clubs in Turkey, France, Greece, Netherlands, Mexico and Brazil.

This included huge teams such as Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, Feyenoord and Corinthians.



He eventually hung up his boots in 2023.

Johan Manzambi bagged the winner against Newcastle on Saturday and still looks overpriced in the anytime scorer market against the Eliteserien champions.

The Stavanger side claimed an unlikely point in their 3-3 home draw against Bayern Munich last week, but it was a one-sided affair.

The Bundesliga champions fired off 28 shots and had 15 corners but wasted several chances to clinch the victory.

Viking's brave attacking approach often leaves space for opponents to exploit on the break, which could play directly into Manzambi's strengths, with the youngster thriving when games become stretched.

The 19-year-old has shown a real eye for goal despite operating from midfield, regularly making late runs into the penalty area and finding dangerous positions between opposition defenders.

Manzambi has scored in three of his last four appearances for club and country and looks tremendous value to notch against the Norwegians.

As ever, Harry Kane is the obvious candidate to get on the scoresheet. The England captain remains Bayern's focal point in the final third and continues to deliver in the biggest matches. Whether from open play, a set-piece or the penalty spot, Kane is rarely short of opportunities.

For Wednesday's accumulator, three strong home favourites stand out.

Como are capable of causing Michael Carrick’s Manchester United plenty of problems in one of the two early games.

Cesc Fabregas' side have tasted defeat only once in their last 11 at home stretching back to last season, while the Red Devils remain winless in six across all competitions.

Lille are picked to send Galatasaray packing in the other 5.45pm kick-off. The French outfit score goals at home and should extend a miserable run for the travelling Turks, who have lost eight of their last nine European trips.

Club Brugge complete the treble as they take on inconsistent Ligue 1 Lens.

The Belgian champions upset Inter Milan at the San Siro last week and are full of confidence right now on the back of a five-match winning streak.

Combining Como, Lille and Club Brugge to win at home creates a strong-looking midweek accumulator and rounds off Wednesday's football betting card nicely.

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha breaks Liverpool record and is a major England threat to Bukayo Saka
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha dazzled for Liverpool in their 4-3 victory over Villarreal - and Bukayo Saka should be worried about his England spot.

It's a suggestion made by Jason Cundy after the teenager picked up two assists in the Champions League thriller at Anfield on Tuesday.

3 Ngumoha arguably had his best Liverpool performance to date as he assisted two goals in their comeback win over Villarreal Credit: Getty

Player-of-the-match Ngumoha provided for Ronald Araujo with a floating cross and then teed up Alexis Mac Allister as Liverpool came from behind to win their third European match of the season.

The teenager has started in all of their Champions League ties and is becoming an integral part of Andoni Iraola's squad, with a new deal also a possibility.

He featured in England's pre-World Cup training camp, and made his debut during the 1-0 friendly win over New Zealand.

Thomas Tuchel did not select him as part of his final 26-man squad but, with Euro 2028 the next major tournament, and Cundy believes the starlet is capable of battling Saka for a starting spot on the right.

Ngumoha v Saka for England starting role

When asked if Ngumoha should play right-wing for England, Cundy said on The Sports Bar: "After that performance, you have to be seriously looking at him. He was involved in the last squad.

Cundy added: "He has caught the eye. Every time he plays, he catches the eye. And there are very few players that can do that at his age. But the thing that he's got, he has the ability because he's so young.

"There's no fear of failure. You get this with young players. They don't know what it's like. Failure doesn't exist in their lives. They've always been the best.

"They just go out and just go and showcase what you've got. Go on, do a step over. Who cares if I get it? And more often than not, because he's so full of confidence…

"There will be a moment in his career where there will be a dip, he will drop in form. It inevitably happens with most young kids but wow, what a performance, what a player."

Cundy then claimed that Saka, who is the consistent starter at right-wing for England, may be wary of Ngumoha's rise as he said: "Saka's had a lot of injuries, but he's England's starter right now in England's best team.

3 With 59 caps, Saka has been the long-term go-to choice on the right for England - but Cundy thinks Ngumoha can rival him for the starting role Credit: Getty

"But, when you're watching young players come through, and even though Saka's still got to reach the peak of his powers...

"When you're looking over your shoulder, you're going, 'Wow, this kid has got something'. Liverpool fans should be very excited, England fans should be very excited."

Ngumoha with a record-breaking display

Ngumoha and Barcelona star Lamine Yamal are the only two teens in this season's Champions League to bag two assists in one match.

The cross for Araujo also made Ngumoha the youngest ever player to score or assist in the competition for Liverpool, doing so aged 18 years and 52 days.

In addition, he is the third-youngest Englishman to provide an assist after Jude Bellingham, Lewis Miley and Theo Walcott.

Ngumoha has now made seven Champions League appearances for Liverpool, although he is still waiting for his first competition goal.

3 Ngumoha broke a club record on what was a night to remember in Liverpool colours on the Champions League stage Credit: Getty

"Tonight is up there with one of the best I've played I think," he said in his post-match interview with Amazon Prime. "I enjoyed myself out there, the team helped me a lot…

"Whenever I get the ball and have the opportunity to go one v one, or sometimes two v one, I'll by all means go for it.

"I believe in myself to do that and the more chances we get the more we can worry the opposition and be ruthless."

Ngumoha added: "To hear my name being chanted by the crowd is a dream. We have the best fans in the world."

Sports.title: EFL managers separated at full time in furious touchline spat
Sports.content:
Wolves and Portsmouth managers Cesar Peixoto and John Mousinho were involved in a heated altercation at full-time of their Championship clash.

Emotions boiled over at the final whistle following the 1-1 draw at Molineux, as Terry Devlin's 86th-minute equaliser snatched a point for Pompey.

5 Cesar Peixoto angrily approached Mousinho at full-time

5 The two managers began to bicker and had to be separated as things threatened to boil over

Wolves had taken the lead through Jordan James, before being made to settle for a draw as Mousinho's side grabbed a late goal.

The result appeared to leave Peixoto frustrated, as footage shows him angrily approaching Mousinho as the full-time whistle blows.

He can be seen making a talking gesture with his hands whilst walking towards his Portsmouth counterpart, who responds by putting his hands on Peixoto and attempting to move him away.

But this only appeared to anger the Wolves boss more, as he continued to appear animated whilst gesticulating at Mousinho.

Other members of staff soon became involved in the heated altercation with players also appearing on the scene to separate the two.

With others beginning to push and shove each other, Mousinho walked away from his opposite number as things calmed down.

It isn't clear what sparked the touchline spat, with Peixoto clearly the more angry of the two managers.

The draw leaves Wolves - who were relegated last season - seventh in the table on 18 points, while Portsmouth are 13th, three points behind them with a tally of 15.

Mousinho reveals Peixoto anger

Speaking after the heated full-time scenes, Mousinho revealed that Peixoto had been angered by his vocal manner on the touchline.

He told The News: "I shook the manager’s hand and then he said I talk too much. So I very politely told him that that’s probably what I do, that’s my job as head coach.

5 Peixoto cut a frustrated figure at full time at Molineux Credit: Getty

5 Mousinho has been Portsmouth head coach since 2023 Credit: Getty

"It was just handbags, absolutely nothing, it’s just one of those, shake hands and walk off.

"I didn’t quite understand it, but it’s fine, no worries."

Stressing that the altercation was nothing serious, Mousinho explained that his questions for the fourth official during the game had annoyed Peixoto.

He continued: "During the game, I got up to talk to the fourth official, I don’t know if you aren’t allowed to any more, I was told in no uncertain terms, quite a rude way, that I needed to sit down and not talk to the fourth.

"I tried to point out that I didn’t know there had been a law change where I wasn’t allowed to speak to the fourth any more, that was it.

"You know what I’m like, just let each manager speak to the fourth, just get on with your own job.

5 Terry Devlin's second goal of the season grabbed a point for Portsmouth at Wolves Credit: Getty

"My job is quite difficult, I’m sure his job is quite difficult as well, let them get on with it. Let the staff do their own thing, stop interfering."

This wasn't Mousinho's first touchline altercation, having also been involved in a spat with Coventry boss Frank Lampard last season.

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag takes on the pundits: Ex-Man United boss insists club legends 'don't know what's going on' inside Old Trafford and are trying to 'protect their legacies'
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag takes on the pundits: Ex-Man United boss insists club legends 'don't know what's going on' inside Old Trafford and are trying to 'protect their legacies'

Erik ten Hag has insisted former Manchester United stars turned pundits 'don't always know what's going on' at the club and believes their criticism can have an impact on players.

Ten Hag served as the Red Devils boss for two-and-a-half years, before he was sacked in October 2024.

The Dutchman had come under fire from pundits during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, with Gary Neville and Rio Ferdinand among former Man United stars speaking out about events at the club.

The pair continue to be vocal with Sky Sports pundit Neville having recently expanded his Overlap podcast empire, while Ferdinand has a well-established YouTube channel.

Former Man United captain Roy Keane and Wayne Rooney are also among prominent pundits, as well as Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt.

Speaking to the Athletic, Ten Hag said he had respect for the achievements of Man United legends but stressed that their comments can have an impact on players and that they 'don't always know what's going on' at the club.

Erik ten Hag insisted he has respect for former Man United stars turned pundits for their achievements, but stressed they 'don't always know what's going on' at the club

Ten Hag admitted the words of high-profile former stars can have an impact on players

'It's everywhere the same, they always want to protect their legacies,' Ten Hag said. 'It's no different than Bayern Munich or Ajax; they do the same. But they are history, and they do not always know what's going on. Football evolves.

'For United, it's clear: they had great contributions, they achieved massive results, trophies for the club and for themselves, so I respect them.

'I have to say, I had a very good relationship with them all, with Gary Neville, Rio Ferdinand. I did nice interviews with them both, so it didn't hurt me.

'Of course, they have podcasts, they have their models. Sometimes it's difficult for players. Some of them get affected by it, get annoyed by it.

'They achieved massive successes. But also, they can help the club more, help the players more. There should be two ways that they support it. But I think always the thing you most love, you most criticise.'

Ten Hag led Man United to the Carabao Cup in 2023 and the FA Cup in 2024, while he oversaw third and eighth place league finishes in his two completed seasons.

He hit out at pundits prior to Man United's FA Cup triumph against rivals Man City, which proved key to the Dutchman keeping his job at the end of the 2023-24 season.

'The pundits in England want to score, they want to show they are worth the money, and for that Manchester United is an easy prey,' Ten Hag said prior to the match.

Rio Ferdinand and Paul Scholes were among Man United legends Ten Hag dealt with during his time in the Old Trafford dugout

'It’s the biggest club in England and possibly in the world. The club is either loved or hated, there is no in-between.

'So when things go bad, they all start talking and talking with very big words. All this negativity from these so-called experts who don’t have the capability to analyse something with facts, but who prefer to attack people to make themselves look better.

'And these same people were the ones who gave me a pat on the back last year. Last year I was able to walk on water, this year I am the worst manager in the Premier League.'

Ten Hag had jokingly poked fun at Roy Keane's managerial record after overseeing Man United's FA Cup victory, while he also had a tense exchange with Gary Lineker and Alan Shearer on the BBC post-match.

The FA Cup triumph had led to Ten Hag's contract being extended, but the Dutchman was sacked in October 2024 with Man United languishing in 14th in the Premier League.

Broken promises and nobody taking responsibility: Erik ten Hag is right - Man United are addicted to going around in circles, writes NATHAN SALT, and Michael Carrick is learning the hard way

Sports.title: Arsenal's meeting with Bayern Munich and Harry Kane is a litmus test in Europe for a team playing ugly football, writes IAN LADYMAN - as David Raya fires back at 'boring' critics
Sports.content:
Arsenal's meeting with Bayern Munich and Harry Kane is a litmus test in Europe for a team playing ugly football, writes IAN LADYMAN - as David Raya fires back at 'boring' critics

It is 144 days since Arsenal came within a couple of bad penalties of winning the Champions League Final in Budapest.

Manager Mikel Arteta still hasn’t got over it.

‘I have tried but when I see the ball and the music I realise how much I still want it so badly,’ he said here last night.

In terms of his players, perhaps the biggest test since that early summer defeat to PSG comes on Wednesday in Bavaria. Bayern Munich have lost just once at home since last April and not anywhere so far this season.

A meeting with Bayern and Harry Kane rightly stands as some kind of litmus test of progress. Arteta said after last season’s disappointment that his team had to evolve yet here we are in mid-autumn with similar themes at play.

Sunday’s win at Nottingham Forest in the Premier League came courtesy of one shot on target and that in itself a deflection. It was a dreary and rather ugly way to win. Arsenal are our English champions but don’t always seem to play like them.

Mikel Arteta will look to impress against Bayern Munich after Arsenal's stodgier start to the domestic season

On Tuesday he admitted that he is still haunted by losing the Champions League final in May

Arteta made light of it all as he sat and talked at the Allianz Arena on Tuesday evening but his goalkeeper David Raya did not.

Does – he was asked by Daily Mail Sport – the criticism of Arsenal’s style irritate the dressing room or not?

‘No it doesn’t,’ Raya said.

‘People have their own opinions. We have our own opinion.

‘At the end of the day, we have lost one game in eleven this season and if you call that boring or irritating, I don’t know what to say.

‘We enjoy playing football. We enjoy going out there every single day to win football matches and that’s the most important thing.’

That game in Budapest last May ended with Arsenal having seen only 25 per cent of the ball. That’s the kind of number we expect to see when, say, Manchester City face Burnley at home.

Again Raya was happy to engage on the subject and the argument he presented was not without its merits.

Asked whether Arsenal are confident of imposing themselves more successfully on the best European teams this season, he said: ‘I think so. But you have to see that in perspective as well.

‘It was our first Champions League final in so many years and we score in the fifth minute and sit back a little bit knowing how good they are offensively. We didn’t want to give anything away.

‘It is different now. I think you can see the way we play, you can see the different ways of playing that we have.

‘I think we are more prepared this year than last year so hopefully we can keep that going.’

David Raya brushed off criticism of Arsenal's playing style this season, stressing that the players had their own opinions

On Wednesday in Bavaria, Arsenal will face an opponent that at least wishes to play in their opponents’ half of the field. In the Premier League it is not always the way.

Equally, Arteta’s players have a European memory bank containing more than images of just one game against just one team. Arsenal beat Bayern at home last season. The season before they ran all over Real Madrid at the Emirates and then beat them in Spain, too.

When the mood takes them, they can run hot. The puzzle is – given the attacking talent at their disposal – why it doesn’t happen more often.

Wednesday may well be informative from that point of view while exactly what Arteta really feels about it is hard to know. The Spaniard is as inscrutable as they come in public but if he wasn’t motivated by the noise that tends to follow his team around then he wouldn’t be human.

On this occasion, he chose to approach the issue with a hint of deadpan and a little sarcasm.

‘I heard our style was incredible,’ he said.

‘Because we scored so many goals, we have had more possession, more shots, different players participating, no goals from set-pieces.

‘So the story is completely different to last year.

‘I think we are talking about a very small minority [who criticise] and the other ones they know they have enjoyed a lot the way we have played and dominated games this year.

‘I think we have proven that so that’s my opinion.

‘If you analyse all the top teams in England they all have a list [of criticism]. We all have a list because none of us are perfect.

‘Thank God that we are not perfect. Thank God that we can still improve even though we have won the amount of games that we have done because otherwise the next day, what do you do?

‘You just expect to be better than the opponent and that’s it. Especially in the Premier League we know that is very far from the reality.

‘I think on Sunday [at Forest], we could have done things better. And that's in our hands. We need to recognise that openly as well.

‘But we did a lot of great things as well against a really tough opponent. Very, very well coached as well. And we did something that we didn't manage to do two years in a row. So that's another step. A really positive one. And then we're done from it and we're okay.’

Arsenal will face a Bayern team on Wednesday expected to be without coach Vincent Kompany on the sidelines. The former City defender has been struck by a virus that is impacting on his ability to walk and has been ordered by his doctors to rest.

Raya opened his part of the media proceedings by offering Kompany his best wishes and that was a nice and clearly pre-meditated touch.

In terms of the game, the nature of the competition’s league format makes these match-ups feel marginally less significant than they once did. But there is a bigger picture at play for this Arsenal team.

Opportunities for statement performances don’t come round very often in a Premier League where the low block is king. In Europe – at places like this – it is different. A win on Wednesday for Arsenal would mean more than Arteta is perhaps willing to admit.

Sports.title: Revealed: How Lord's is taking drastic action to sort pitch problems for 2027 Ashes Test after 'unsatisfactory' surface against New Zealand
Sports.content:
Lord’s will not host any cricket for 18 days during the build-up to the 2027 Ashes Test in a bid to avoid a repeat of the pitch problems that made headlines over the summer.

The groundstaff had only a clear 10 days before the first Test against New Zealand in June, when a surface of variable bounce was rated ‘unsatisfactory’ by the ICC, prompting a public apology from MCC and earning the venue an unprecedented demerit point.

There were also 10 days between finals day of the Hundred and the second Test against Pakistan in August, when the surface was rated ‘satisfactory’ – the second-highest of the four ratings.

The ECB want to ensure venues have between seven and nine clear days before hosting a Test next summer.

But Lord’s officials are taking no chances when it comes to next summer’s high-profile second Test against Australia starting on June 30, and have given head groundsman Karl McDermott and his team what Rob Lynch, MCC’s director of cricket and operations, called ‘the best chance of producing the best pitch’.

MCC’s determination to deal with the slowness and inconsistency of their surfaces has produced a raft of bold measures, including the recent decision to dig up Pitch 9 – which hosted the New Zealand Test.

Lord’s will not host any cricket for 18 days during the build-up to the 2027 Ashes Test in a bid to avoid a repeat of the pitch problems that made headlines over the summer

The pitch for June's Test against New Zealand was rated 'unsatisfactory' amid variable bounce

It is the first time in over 25 years that the home of cricket has taken such drastic action, taking the pitch out of action until 2029. The process involved digging down 12 inches, and replacing it with four inches of stabilising crushed granite, 20mm of porous matter and nearly eight inches of Ongar loam.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this year, MCC are also moving ahead with plans to instal three permanent drop-in pitches over the next few years, with a view to staging a domestic match on one of them in 2029, and international cricket the following summer. Each pitch should have a lifespan of 10-15 years.

With the Wormsley ground, an hour’s drive away up the M40, now bearing some of the Lord’s load, MCC plan to reduce the number of days’ cricket they host in 2027 from this year’s 63 to 55 or 56.

Sports.title: Villa Park... get ready for a Viking invasion! How spirited Champions League minnows plan to topple Aston Villa after stunning Bayern Munich - with TWO managers at the helm
Sports.content:
The Vikings are plotting another European raid and this time, it's Prince William who has reason to worry. Tonight, Norwegian minnows Viking FK head to Villa Park with the wind in their sails, fresh from holding German giants Bayern Munich to a pulsating 3-3 draw in the Champions League last week. Despite hosting Bayern on home soil, Viking were given little hope of upsetting the Bundesliga champions, whose £878.7million squad is worth more than 18 times that of the Stavanger-based outfit. Viking did more than spring a surprise against Bayern Munich. The underdogs carved out a stunning 2-0 half-time lead and then showed real character to snatch a last-gasp equaliser after Harry Kane and Co had fought their way back into the game. Aston Villa, meanwhile, have made an impressive start to their own European campaign. Unai Emery's side edged past Club Brugge 3-2 in their opening Champions League clash before thumping Fenerbahce by six goals last week, establishing themselves as a force to be reckoned with after lifting the Europa League trophy last season. First up, Villa will have to contend with Viking's indomitable spirit, fuelled by a fervent travelling support. Aston Villa host Norwegian minnows Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday night Viking stunned Harry Kane and Bayern Munich last week, holding the giants to a 3-3 draw Viking have two managers at the helm with shared responsibility - Morten Jensen (right) and Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim (left) - and it has proved hugely successful since their arrival in 2021

Your browser does not support iframes.

After waiting 34 years to see their side back among Europe's elite, the Norwegian faithful had barely settled before erupting in celebration as Viking took a shock lead after just 72 seconds. Bayern's sluggish start may have been compounded by reports that Viking fans set off fireworks outside the German side's hotel at around 1.30am on the morning of the match, in an attempt to stop Vincent Kompany's side from sleeping. With Gianni Stensness having fired them in front, the home fans kept up their deafening support throughout the match, roaring the team on through every twist and turn of a thrilling contest. 'That was the moment', Viking's chief executive Eirik Bjorno told Sky Sports, reflecting on the opening goal. 'You are preparing for wave after wave, maybe having a counter-attack or two, and then you score from the first corner.' Erik Nevland, the club's sporting director, was left even more impressed by the second goal, which came in the 38th minute courtesy of Peter Christiansen. 'You can always score early,' he said. 'But that was something that we had never dreamed of. It was crazy. More than we could expect. It was just a night for the history books.' In many ways, Viking's remarkable rise began with a simple dream – two great friends joining forces to lead the club as joint head coaches. Viking uniquely have two managers steering their ship, with Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim and Morten Jensen sharing equal charge of the team since their appointment in January 2021. When they first floated the idea, Aarsheim worked in banking and Jensen was employed in the oil and gas industry, both coaching separate local teams on the side. The Norwegian minnows are competing in their first Champions League campaign since 1992 They will hope to wipe the smile off Aston Villa's most famous fan Prince William (pictured during his team's 6-0 thumping over Fenerbahce last week) when they head to Villa Park Speaking of their partnership, Aarsheim told The Guardian earlier this month: 'We were talking on the phone one evening, it must have been around 2012 or 2013. I remember us saying: "Hey, one day we should coach a team together." 'What’s impressive with Morten is how big he thinks and that he dares to tell it out loud. He talks about winning the league, the Champions League, everything, while I’m thinking: "Let’s just get a good team first". But it transmits. 'We put dreams to the players and put that flame inside for them to dream bigger. We don’t want players simply to be satisfied to play here.' The two-boss setup has been hugely successful since Aarsheim and Jensen's arrival, culminating in the club winning their first Eliteserien title in 34 years in 2025. Despite missing out on the title last campaign, losing out to Bodo/Glimt on goal difference, Viking triumphed over Dinamo Zagreb to qualify for this season's Champions League through the playoffs, marking their first appearance in the elite competition since 1992. Viking captain Zlatko Tripic acts as the crucial glue between the two managers during matches, tasked with executing the shared tactical vision on the pitch while Aarsheim and Jensen coach in tandem. They also split matchday and media duties equally, resisting the temptation to divide responsibilities into separate areas of expertise. Ranked as one of the leading youth academies in Norway, Viking have profited hugely from homegrown talent, but they keep their eyes out for a certain type of youngster. The academy’s strapline, displayed on the club’s website, is simple: 'We are looking for potential, and looking for those who want it the most!' Hard work, passion and dedication are at the heart of Viking's youth set-up, with those values expected to carry through to the first team when young players earn their chance at senior level. Just as important is a strong connection to the club and the Stavanger region it represents. For sporting director Nevland, success is about more than recruitment – it is about having players who genuinely care about Viking, its identity and what it means to the local community. Unai Emery pictured in training as Villa prepare to play host to the Vikings on Wednesday night Homegrown midfielder Simen Kvia-Egeskog is a natural embodiment of that philosophy, following in the footsteps of his grandfather Svein Kvia, who made almost 300 appearances for Viking and remains a much-loved club legend. As Turkish giants Fenerbahce will tell you, travelling to Villa Park is no easy feat. But Viking have already shown they are capable of unsettling a European giant, and their remarkable performance against Bayern Munich suggests they will not be overawed by the occasion.

Sports.title: How two tobacco tycoons, Cesc Fabregas' unique link, a former England hardman and the 'Disney model' inspired Como's remarkable rise ahead of Manchester United clash
Sports.content:
When Michael Carrick arrives in the tranquil surroundings of Lake Como for Wednesday night's Champions League clash against the Italian side, he may find little respite from Manchester United's troubles. For all its picturesque beauty, Como is home to one of European football's most ambitious and remarkable footballing projects. Just seven years ago, they were playing in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football, having suffered three bankruptcies between 2004 and 2017. Now, they are rubbing shoulders with Europe's elite. The transformation began in 2019, when Indonesian billionaire brothers Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono, who originally made their fortune in the tobacco industry, bought the club for $850,000 (£644,427) through their Djarum Group. With a combined net worth then estimated at $48billion (£36.4billion), they instantly made Como the richest club in Italian football. The money mattered, but so did the strategy. Rather than pursue instant success through lavish spending, Como built steadily, investing in infrastructure, recruitment and a clear footballing identity. Manchester United take on high-flying Italian side Como in the Champions League tonight Como are managed by Cesc Fabregas, who has become one of Europe's top young coaches 'They didn't just do an Abramovich and buy anything that would move on two legs,' Italian football expert Daniele Verri tells Daily Mail Sport. 'They just went step-by-step and they’ve done it really well... they are still doing it well. 'They climbed the ladder of Italian football pretty quickly, but they never overspent. It’s not like they bought Roberto Baggio or mega-fancy names.' The results have been striking. Promotion from Serie D in 2019 was followed by a Serie C title in 2021, before a second-place finish in Serie B three years later secured Como's return to Serie A after a 21-year absence. Having come tenth in 2024-25, they finished fourth last time out to qualify for the Champions League. After a rapid summer renovation of their Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, which sits on the shores of Lake Como and will have a capacity of around 11,000 for the United game, they are now welcoming one of the biggest clubs in the world. The fact they were able to complete the necessary stadium improvements to ensure they could host Champions League games sums up their efficient management, with renovation of grounds typically difficult in Italy due to bureaucratic issues. At the heart of the project is Cesc Fabregas, the former Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea midfielder who has emerged as one of Europe's brightest young coaches. Also a minority shareholder, he has developed a side built around possession, intensity and an attractive style of play. His connections to Spanish football have proved particularly valuable in the transfer market. Although significant investment has helped Como's journey, they have always spent smartly and brought in top young talents. That is best reflected in Nico Paz, who joined from Real Madrid aged 19 but is now an Argentina international and one of the most exciting young players on the continent. Greek forward Anastasios Douvikas, a 2025 arrival from Celta Vigo, is another good example. Como's current squad includes other young stars like Maximo Perrone and Jacobo Ramon, while summer additions that included Moise Kean, Robert Sanchez and Trevoh Chalobah underlined the club's growing appeal. 'The idea of being part of a rising club with big-money involved and young players under a former champion like Fabregas is very attractive,' Verri adds. 'Everyone recognises they play a nice brand of football, and they've done it step-by-step up the ladder. They never bought a title and have always brought in players who were pivotal for the project. Como is a small city, but they are competing.' Behind that recruitment is a data-led approach, with Como drawing on Jamestown Analytics, the sports analytics company best known for its work with Brighton. Their Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia sits on the shores of the luxurious and beautiful Lake Como Como (pictured after being promoted from Serie B in 2024) have had an incredible rise Argentina star Nico Paz is a superb example of Como's impressive data-driven recruitment Fabregas and the owners take a lot of credit in Como's rise yet there are several unsung heroes. That includes former Wimbledon and Chelsea hardman Dennis Wise, who was instrumental in laying the foundations for the club's modern success. Initially acting as a technical consultant, he became CEO in 2021 and helped build crucial infrastructure and drive on-pitch success. This included developing a new training facility and rebuilding the youth academy. He was also central to persuading Fabregas to join as a player and minority shareholder in 2022. Wise left in July 2024 amid a reported power struggle. Thierry Henry is another minority shareholder. Although he isn't involved in the day-to-day running of things, his presence has brought global prestige and focus to the project. Perhaps that attention is not needed for a football team in one of the most luxurious and beautiful settings in the world, a factor the club have made central to a wider strategy to turn themselves into a international fashion and lifestyle brand. This has included launching their own streetwear and formal wear collections, helping the club to significantly grow their off-pitch revenue and global visibility, while celebrity visitors have brought additional attention. Keira Knightley, Hugh Grant, Michael Fassbender and Benedict Cumberbatch have all attended games, while Chalobah recently revealed he was a neighbour of George Clooney. ’Funnily enough, I went on a boat, and I drove past his house,’ Chalobah said. ‘It’s a really nice place, by the lake, the food is great, the weather is nice, and the people and the club have really helped me settle in. I suggest you guys should go there.' For club president Mirwan Suwarso, the ambition extends well beyond the pitch. He has previously likened Como's business model to Disney, with football serving as the centrepiece to a much broader commercial network. 'The parallel is between Disney and Como,' he said. 'For Disney, Disneyland represents its theme park division; for us, the football club and the matchday experience is our theme park division.' Alongside that, Suwarso has described a network of complementary businesses spanning merchandising, licensing, clothing, footwear, hospitality, travel and tourism, all built around the identity and international appeal of Lake Como. He added: 'The team from a small city - 80,000 inhabitants - now sells jerseys in London, Paris, Milan, and New York as if it were Inter, Juventus, or AC Milan. Only 14 per cent of our commercial revenue comes from Como and its province. 'We are building a broader ecosystem, drawing on the lake's identity, its global appeal, and the aspirations associated with it. This creates opportunities in merchandising, hospitality, travel, and tourism, beyond traditional football revenues. 'We want to play good football and win, but Como is also a lifestyle destination. Ignoring this would be a mistake.' Verri believes that international positioning is central to the club's long-term appeal. 'They are one of these new global projects,' he says. 'AC Milan have fans all over the world because of their successful eras, but Como cannot rely on that. 'They are doing one of those new chic and trendy projects where they have a nice shirt, invite actors to games, and Como is a luxury place. 'But the owners are also putting money into the city, creating something of real value to help the club grow as quick as possible.' Arsenal, Barcelona and France legend Thierry Henry (centre) is a minority shareholder Several celebrities have attended games, including (left to right) Michael Fassbender, Keira Knightley and James Righton The question is whether Como can sustain their extraordinary progress and eventually challenge Italy’s established elite. 'Why not?' Verri says. 'They've got the money to do so. In the summer people were saying Como were a title contender this season, but I believe it's too early because of their squad depth and European commitments. 'It takes time to be consistent at a certain level, but you have seen how quickly they’ve climbed from Serie D to the Champions League so the sky's the limit.' For United, meanwhile, the trip represents another demanding test. Sunday's draw at Leeds may have slightly dampened the noise around Carrick after another difficult week, yet Como's recent progress suggests they will not be straightforward opponents. They thrashed Leipzig 4-1 in their Champions League opener before they suffered a disappointing 3-2 defeat by Feyenoord in which key man Assane Diao, another recruit from Spain, got injured. 'Most of the Como players aren’t used to this level of football every three days so it will be difficult for them,' Verri concludes. 'They will respect Man United, but Fabregas will not change his approach and will go for the win. 'It will be a good game, Como are an attractive team and they run a lot, which is not that typical for Italian clubs although it might suit Manchester United.'

Sports.title: The night Rio Ngumoha cemented his status as a future world-beater: Liverpool had a £400m attack at their disposal but it was the 18-year-old who shone brightest in chaotic comeback win, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
They used to call it 'Pep roulette' at Manchester City. A phrase coined by fantasy football nerds about Pep Guardiola's tendency to chop and change his front line every week to devastating effect. We haven't refined our snazzy phrase for Andoni Iraola yet – the working drafts are 'AI Bingo' or 'Iraola tombola' – but the Liverpool boss has a devastating depth of attacking talent that, if they all fulfil their potential, can lead this team to dizzying heights. That is caveated with a reminder that Iraola's Reds are simultaneously plagued by many teething problems in other areas and are far from complete. We will discuss that in due course but first, a word on Iraola's deck of cards that contains multiple aces and jokers. With the best part of half a billion pounds worth of attackers not starting this comeback victory against VIllarreal, it was left to others to step up and no one caught the eye more than the potential world-beater but lesser-heralded Rio Ngumoha. At just 18, Ngumoha already has three England caps and is well on the radar of Thomas Tuchel, but he is not yet guaranteed a starting berth at Liverpool and has had to bide his time due to competition and having been asked to swap wings by Iraola after the arrival of left-winger Bradley Barcola. The teenager, who was poached from Chelsea in 2024 to much fury at Stamford Bridge, will cost a maximum of £6.8million but his ceiling is just as high as £125m Alexander Isak, £123m Barcola or £116m Florian Wirtz. Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 in a chaotic Champions League encounter at Anfield on Tuesday Alexis Mac Allister was Liverpool's hero, scoring twice as the Reds came from behind to win But it was Rio Ngumoha's display that was most impressive as he showed all of his quality Ngumoha is yet to score this season but was the shining light here with two assists in a spell-binding performance that helped tilt the game in Liverpool's favour. That was far from guaranteed after a shoddy, uncharacteristic and worrying first half an hour. Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: MATCH FACTS LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 6; Araujo 7 (Wirtz 46, 7), Jacquet 6 (Gomez 74, 6), Van Dijk 5, Tsimikas 6; Nyoni 7 (McConnell 81), Mac Allister 8; Ngumoha 8 (Barcola 74, 6), Gravenberch 6; Gakpo 6; Koumas 6. Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Kerkez, Isak, Chambers, Danns, Laffey. Booked: None. Scorers: Mac Allister 36, 65, Araujo 45+2, Wirtz 68. Manager: Andoni Iraola 7. VILLARREAL (4-2-3-1): Gulacsi 5; Mourino 5, Navarro 5, Veiga 6, Cardona 6; Saliba 7 (Oluwaseyi 46, 7), Gueye 6; Buchanan 5 (Freeman 60, 6), Comesana 6 (Moreno 78), Moleiro 6 (Foyth 54, 6); Mikautadze 7 (Perez 60, 6). Subs not used: Luiz Junior, Akhomach, Costa, Diatta, El Jmili, Gaitan, Macia. Booked: Moleiro, Mourino. Scorers: Mikautadze 4, Cardona 29, Oluwaseyi 87. Manager: Inigo Perez 7. Referee: Szymon Marciniak (Pol) 7. Attendance: not provided. Alexis Mac Allister is also worthy of vast praise as the Argentine struck a brace to continue his resurgence and stellar season after a year-long dip, while Ronald Araujo and substitute Wirtz also scored. As the scoreline suggests, Liverpool's defence was all at sea and that will provide a headache for Iraola in the coming days, especially given they have conceded 10 in their last four games, also shipping three to Manchester City and Austrian side LASK. But while the boss agonises over fixing the defence, he knows he has cracked it at the other end. Ngumoha can trouble any defence, Isak can win any game with his instinctive poacher-like finishing, Wirtz and Barcola are starting to show signs they can unlock stubborn sides. Then there is Cody Gakpo, who returned from injury and showed signs he is picking up where he left off, and the energetic Victor Munoz, who missed this game but was described as a 'Formula One car' in these pages yesterday. And don't forget £79m injured striker Hugo Ekitike. Liverpool's array of weapons in attack were needed to help them get over the mess of the first half an hour, as Iraola was being taught a lesson by his former right-hand man, Inigo Perez, who was the No 2 during the Basque's formative years at Rayo Vallecano. Perez could not move to England when Iraola did because some wise cracks at the Home Office said he was not skilled enough for a work permit. The 38-year-old has made a mockery of that since, leading Rayo to the Conference League final after taking over from Iraola as head coach and now managing in the Champions League, where, for 35 minutes at least, his team played six-time European kings Liverpool off the park. Liverpool fought back after a dreadful first 30 minutes that saw Villarreal go 2-0 ahead Ronald Araujo scored his second goal in a week and celebrated by jumping into the stands Florian Wirtz (right) was also on the scoresheet to cap off a good few days for the German RIO: ONE OF THE BEST I'VE PLAYED Rio Ngumoha said his virtuoso performance against Villarreal was up there with the best in his budding career. The 18-year-old registered two assists and was the star man as Liverpool put a worrying start behind them to come from 2-0 down to beat their Spanish opposition. And the three-time England cap said: 'It's up there with one of the best I've played, I think. I enjoyed myself out there. The team helped me as well a lot. I enjoyed today. 'Like I always say, we have the best fans in the world. To hear my name being chanted is a dream.' Boss Andoni Iraola added: 'The good thing with Rio is he is still 18, he is not the full package, he can add things fortunately for us. 'Hopefully he can continue in the same way. He's not always going to be like this, he will have ups and downs in the process. 'But I'm happy because attitude-wise I think he's in a great place.' Alexis Mac Allister was also a shining light and scored twice. The Argentine said: 'Look at Rio, he was amazing tonight. He made the difference. He was really important and I'm glad for him. 'It's clear the quality Rio has. Everyone knows. It's easy to say he's a really good player but he needs to focus on other things. He worked really hard off the ball.' On his fine headed goal, Mac Allister added: 'It's not something I really practice. My dad is a bit smaller than me but he was quite good in the air so maybe it's something I got from him. 'Last year was a really difficult year for all of us. It was clear I was not at the level and I am the first one to say. Something wasn't right in the group and this manager changed it. The way we play is different, I don't like to compare. I'm feeling good.' By Lewis Steele Villarreal were magic, Liverpool tragic. This was by far the worst half hour of the Iraola era, more worrying than the capitulation against Manchester City. At least that time they had the defence of going down to 10 men. No excuse on this occasion, apprentice Perez was simply schooling master Iraola. Villarreal, nicknamed El Submarino Amarillo or The Yellow Submarine, were enjoying themselves in the land of the Beatles – whose song inspired that tag and is played before games at Estadio de la Ceramica. They were ahead after just four minutes. Virgil van Dijk made a honking error to head a long ball straight to the path of Georges Mikautadze, who could not believe his luck and scored. Van Dijk barely makes one wrong step, never mind a catastrophic mistake like this, and everyone at Anfield looked shellshocked. The 1,500 or so away fans and sea of vibrant yellow shirts were soon jumping for joy again on 29 minutes when Sergi Cardona sprung through a shoddy offside trap and waltzed through on goal to slot past a helpless Alisson for 2-0. Iraola was left scratching his head and probably regretting the six changes he made from the team that fought from behind to beat Brentford on Saturday. But out of nowhere, his team found something and started the comeback, through a Mac Allister header on 36 minutes. The Argentine may be small but is as good as most in the air and connected well with Kostas Tsimikas's corner to score. Anfield found its voice and the Reds responded. Ngumoha made the equaliser with a fine ball that was headed home by Ronald Araujo for his second goal in a week after scoring at LASK. The Uruguayan loanee, here for the season from Barcelona, is quickly becoming a cult hero and is being affectionately referred to as 'Big Ron'. He jumped into the Anfield Road End and made the night of one lucky lady, who received a bear hug. There was never any looking back from there, and Mac Allister put Liverpool ahead on 65 minutes after a dancing run from Ngumoha, before Wirtz came on and put gloss on the victory with a fine finish to continue an eye-catching week for the much-criticised German. Tani Oluwaseyi made it a nervy finish with an 87th-minute goal which highlighted Liverpool's defensive issues once more, but at least they can follow the old mantra of 'you can score, we will just score more'. How long that will last, who knows, but it is certainly not going to be boring this year.
