Sports.title: Formula 1’s move to shorter grands prix in 2027 will not be permanent | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 will reinstate full grand prix distances in 2028 after shortening the races this year, the FIA has confirmed.

The championship announced last month it will cut 15 kilometres from the standard grand prix distance next year as a result of the new fuel flow limits which will come into force. Shortening the grand prix distances will reduce the number of components teams need to redesign next year.

The shortened distance of 290 kilometres will apply for all grands prix except Monaco, which has run to a shorter distance of 260km for many years and will continue to.

However the first edition of the 2027 Formula 1 Sporting Regulations published by the FIA notes the previous distance will apply again from 2028. “The distance of the race [i.e. grand prix], from the start signal referred to in Article B5.7.2 to the end-of-session signal referred to in Article B5.16.1, shall be equal to the least number of complete laps which exceed a distance of 305km,” it states.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Backs Tyson Fury To Stop Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Frank Warren is convinced Tyson Fury stops Anthony Joshua inside the distance, pinpointing AJ’s defensive lapses during his own offensive bursts as the decisive flaw.

Fury’s timing and counterpunching remain central to Warren’s prediction. The promoter views the dynamic much like he viewed Daniel Dubois’s upset win over Joshua, even while admitting neither man is operating at their athletic peak.

“Styles make fights. I believe the same as I believed Daniel, when he fought AJ, he would knock him out and beat him. I think Tyson would do the same thing,” Warren said to Sky Sports Boxing. “I just feel that Tyson has his number, in my opinion. Maybe wrong. The one thing about AJ, as we all know, he can whack.”

Warren’s logic involves the split second Joshua commits to his combinations. While Joshua’s power creates danger whenever he fires, his delayed guard gives an elite counterpuncher clear targets before his hands return home.

“When he throws his shots, he leaves himself very vulnerable, and Tyson’s a good counterpuncher,” Warren added.

Capitalizing on those windows requires sharp reflexes, something that naturally diminishes with age. Warren admitted the bout will look different than it would have years ago, predicting a tighter, less mobile collision where neither heavyweight retreats.

“I think they’ll both be a little bit slower than they were,” Warren said. “I think it’ll be very exciting whilst it lasts.”

Warren dresses it up with complex talk about technical openings and counter angles, but the fundamental flaw is Joshua’s punch resistance. Once a heavyweight’s chin cracks, no amount of technical adjustment can compensate for it.

The warning signs were impossible to miss against Kristian Prenga. Surviving Dubois is one thing because Daniel hits with concussive force, but getting buzzed and nearly closed out by a fringe guy like Prenga signals that Joshua’s internal alarm system is permanently compromised. Every time clean contact lands, his legs betray him immediately.

Fury does not possess one-punch power, yet that makes little difference when the target crumples under ordinary pressure. With his towering frame and natural bulk, Fury merely needs to absorb the initial storm, step into the pocket, and let his hands go until something connects flush. A clean tap on a ruined chin does the exact same job as an explosive shot.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Aims To Become Undisputed Champion
Sports.content:
Las Vegas, Nevada – On Saturday night, Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) defended his WBC junior middleweight championship at The Chelsea inside the Cosmopolitan Casino against the very tough and gritty Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs).

It was a much more challenging match than many expected; Hadribeaj tested Fundora on the inside by making him miss and countering him with an efficient attack. The Albanian Sniper’s total connect rate of 32.3 percent was more effective than The Towering Inferno’s 25.9

percent.

However, Sebastian did outland Ermal in total punches 202 to 144, outlanding him8 of the 12 rounds(Compubox). Fundora was able to score the finishing blow in the last second of the twelve-round fight, winning the fight by controversial knockout.

After the fight, Sebastian said, “It was an interesting fight. I had to go back and fight on the inside and show everyone again that I can still do that. It was dramatic to knock him out at the last second, but we’ll go back to the gym and fix some things.”

He added whom he’ll like to fight next by saying, “I want to go for undisputed in this division. We’ll break either Jaron Ennis or Josh Kelly down just like the last guy and the guy before that. We’ll keep breaking them down. When asked of the two whom he expects to win, Fundora answered, “I do favor Boots.” Meaning him and promoter Sampson Lewkowicz believe it will be Boots whom they’ll have to negotiate for the undisputed crown, but they appear they’ll be playing hardball in negotiations.

Lewkowicz told the media after the fight what he expects the terms of the contract to be, “It doesn’t make any difference…because we need each other. We need 50-50 because we want to unify. It doesn’t matter how many titles. I see so many st**d guys saying on the internet saying he has three belts. You have only two. People already saying he has three.

So many people saying he have three belts. Who’s he fighting? A bum? I respect boxing, and I tell you Kelly can fight.” Sampson went on to state he had already spoken to Jaron’s advisor on the expectations of terms, making it known it should be a 50-50 fight, and hopes they don’t deviate from it by requesting a higher percentage for themselves.

However, if the fight for undisputed does happen next year, the winner of the Boots-Kelly fight will be a three-belt holder bringing the WBA, WBO, and IBF titles to the table, with Fundora holding the single WBC belt. The undisputed showdown is a fight fans will want to see and will truly crown the junior middleweight king.

Hopefully both sides can come to an amicable agreement, and the fight won’t get derailed as were the contract negotiations between Boots and Vergil Ortiz Jr. For now, Sebastian will rest and wait for the Boots-Kelly winner and prepare for his next goal of becoming undisputed junior middleweight king.

Sports.title: Chris Algieri Doubts An 80% Canelo Alvarez Beats Christian Mbilli
Sports.content:
Chris Algieri argues that Canelo Alvarez must bring his absolute best to get past Christian Mbilli. His claim that Mbilli’s style naturally plays into Canelo’s hands doesn’t hold up, especially given the challenger’s relentless engine.

Algieri does give Canelo credit for stepping right into danger following surgery and significant time away, acknowledging the grueling physical test awaiting him.

“Can we give him a little respect for coming off a layoff and a surgery right into Mbilli?” Algieri pointed out to DAZN Boxing. “Yes, he has his faults. I think he falls right into Canelo’s style, but what Canelo are we getting? If Canelo is at all degraded, an 80% Canelo probably doesn’t beat Mbilli. He’s got to be top-notch for that fight.”

Even a peak version of Canelo might have struggled with this matchup. While aggressive fighters give Canelo plenty of targets, Mbilli refuses to give up the breathing room Canelo usually buys with crisp counterpunches.

Gennadiy Golovkin applied pressure behind a stiff jab, leaning on heavy single shots. Miguel Cotto relied on movement during the twilight of his prime. Neither fighter swarmed with the sustained, multi-punch bursts that define Mbilli’s game.

Canelo typically hurts opponents until they freeze. They back off, rethink their strategy, let him rest, and wait for his next opening. Mbilli simply ignores that script.

Mbilli isn’t invincible, of course. Charging forward recklessly leaves massive openings, and eating flush counter hooks could quickly check his enthusiasm. Canelo has the precision to make him pay for being aggressive. Yet landing clean shots is vastly different from dictating the tempo. If Mbilli walks through fire and keeps throwing, Canelo has to scramble back into a defensive shell before his lungs catch up with the previous exchange.

Managing that volume would test any elite fighter in his prime. Asking a 36-year-old coming off major surgery and ring rust to endure it is an entirely different proposition. Algieri is spot on about the danger here. His warning that an 80% Canelo falls short might ring true, but treating an ultra-high-volume brawler as tailor-made for him severely understates the threat.

If Canelo cannot discourage Mbilli inside the first four rounds, the math turns ugly very quickly. By round six, when Canelo’s output routinely dips and his feet go flat, he will be forced to shell up against the ropes while Mbilli pounds away at his arms, shoulders, and ribs. Heavy volume wears down legs just as fast as clean headshots, especially for an aging fighter carrying thirteen months of inactivity and repaired joints.

Surviving that kind of physical tax requires supreme conditioning and fluid defensive pivots. If Canelo is stuck playing defense just to survive the onslaught, he will not have the legs or the gas tank left to mount a mid-fight rescue. When a fighter relies strictly on finding one perfect counter shot to bail himself out, every missed swing empties the reserve that much faster.

In 2019, Canelo capitalized on a faded, battle-worn Sergey Kovalev, whose gas tank was depleted, waiting out Kovalev’s tired arm punches until round eleven to land the finishing blow. Now, the dynamic has flipped, and Canelo finds himself occupying the aging fighter’s corner against a younger, relentless pressure puncher.

Kovalev came into the fight at 36 with heavy miles and well-documented physical wear, and Canelo is carrying an even larger cumulative toll. With more than two decades in the professional ranks, chronic joint issues, and elbow surgery following a year on the shelf, the engine simply cannot turn over the way it once did.

The pattern across the Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga, William Scull, and Terence Crawford bouts showed a fighter relying almost entirely on bursts, resting for extended stretches, and depending on defensive posturing to steal rounds on ring generalship. Against Crawford, the inability to sustain offense or dictate the terms of engagement laid bare what happens when elite opposition refuses to grant Canelo those customary rest periods.

Against Mbilli, relying on selective counterpunching becomes a dangerous gamble. Landing a crisp left hook or a sharp uppercut only helps if it forces the incoming fighter to step back, reset, and second-guess their entry. If Mbilli treats every clean counter as a cue to unload another four-punch salvo to the body, Canelo will never get the pauses he needs to recharge.

Sports.title: Abdullah Mason Targets William Zepeda Or Joe Cordina
Sports.content:
Abdullah Mason is targeting a December return against William Zepeda or Joe Cordina, with a lightweight unification fight or another defense of his WBO title under consideration.

Mason says nothing is signed, but those are the two names emerging for his next appearance. He is also willing to travel to the UK to face Cordina after being told visa issues prevented the British fighter from meeting him in the summer.

“Right now it’s looking like it could be a unification with Zepeda or a defense with Cordina,” Mason said to Brian Custer’s channel. “That’s what it’s looking like it could be. So I’m definitely ready to face anybody in that position.”

Zepeda would give Mason the opportunity to add the WBC belt and test himself against a pressure fighter who believes he can wear the young champion down. Asked about Zepeda’s claim that he would struggle to last 12 rounds, Mason declined to make a counterprediction.

“Two fighters got to step in the ring to really see how it’s going to go down,” he said.

That would be the harder physical test. Zepeda’s volume would force Mason to decide when to trade and when to use his feet. Mason’s willingness to fight aggressively could make it an action fight, but he would need to avoid letting Zepeda dictate how much work he does every round.

The Cordina option offers a different route, and Mason has no objection to defending on the challenger’s side of the Atlantic.

“If he’s had visa issues in the summer, I’m ready to go over there,” Mason said. “It’s a huge fight card in December in the UK. Why don’t I fight him over there if they can’t come over here?”

Mason did not identify the event or confirm a place on it. His December plans remain a target rather than a completed deal.

“Nothing confirmed, nothing signed off on, but that’s what it’s looking like, and that’s what we’re pushing for.”

Mason’s promoters at Top Rank rarely throw a young fighter into a risky fight when they can take an easier route to build an international footprint. Zepeda represents pure peril right now. His punch output breaks people down, and Top Rank knows Mason is far too young to be taking that sort of physical punishment if it can be delayed.

Letting Zepeda put more miles on the odometer before signing off on a unification makes total promotional sense.

Cordina is the soft landing spot. He gives Mason a recognizable British name to put on the record, introduces the young champion to UK fans on a big DAZN card, and presents minimal stylistic danger. Cordina likes to pick his spots from the outside and does not push a blistering pace, which plays right into Mason’s hands.

It would be a low-risk voluntary defense disguised as a big overseas trip, keeping Mason active, winning, and out of harm’s way while Zepeda’s prime ticks down.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Departure Brings Relief Within Zuffa
Sports.content:
Some inside Zuffa Boxing actually welcomed Shakur Stevenson walking away. When the planned Devin Haney matchup collapsed, the company found itself staring down massive financial obligations with zero marquee headliner to show for it.

Dan Rafael noted that parting ways worked out for both camps, despite the optics sting of Zuffa dropping a prized marquee acquisition right out of the gate.

“There are some people that are sort of relieved that they’re not going to, you know, go down that pit of that money,” Rafael said to Total Boxing.

The broadcast setup explains plenty about why Zuffa executives felt that way. Per Rafael, even if Haney versus Stevenson crossed the finish line, the US broadcast rights belonged to DAZN instead of Zuffa’s domestic partner Paramount+. Zuffa faced bankrolling an enormous purse just to drive its biggest potential viewership straight to a competing network.

Rafael pointed out that securing both men in the ring demanded north of $20 million just for the main event. Spending that kind of cash to cement Shakur as the promotion’s central figure, while asking Paramount+ subscribers to tune in elsewhere, looked like bad business.

When the Haney talks cratered, backup plans looked rough. Zuffa put a hold on Newark’s Prudential Center for January 23, but finding a credible dance rival for a hometown showcase proved tough. Footing an astronomical bill for a soft touch would leave Zuffa paying elite rates without the blockbuster that validated signing Shakur initially.

“I don’t think that everybody involved with Zuffa Boxing and/or their parent company TKO was that upset that they were able to separate because I think they might have had some buyer’s remorse,” Rafael said.

Shakur exiting before ever fighting under the banner definitely hurts Zuffa’s reputation, especially after hyping up the Haney clash. Still, the numbers explain the decision. Retaining Shakur only worked if Zuffa locked down the right opponents alongside favorable platform deals to balance the books. Once Haney slipped away, cutting ties cost far less than trying to patch up an expensive mistake.

Shakur commands elite, eight-figure purses, but his track record does not show independent pay-per-view drawing power or the ability to move tickets outside of a localized Newark gate. When a promoter guarantees that kind of money, the fighter has to generate massive subscription spikes, sell out neutral venues, or command major foreign site fees. Shakur has not done any of that on his own.

His safety-first, low-volume style makes that financial gap impossible to bridge. Fans want drama, sustained action, and knockouts. Shakur is technically brilliant, but his emphasis on distance control and minimal engagement often draws boos from casual crowds and turns off broadcast executives looking for viral, highlight-reel content. Promoting a fighter with that approach is an uphill battle, especially for an outfit tied to the UFC and TKO brand, where audiences expect relentless pressure and decisive finishes.

Paying top-dollar purses for Shakur to out-point mismatched opponents in tactical dull contests would have eroded fan interest and bled capital fast. Zuffa avoided footing the bill for an expensive, low-entertainment asset who brings little commercial leverage to the table.

Sports.title: Rafael Espinoza Wants Naoya Inoue Before Moving Up
Sports.content:
Rafael Espinoza has his sights set on Naoya Inoue, citing the Japanese superstar as his main reason to stay at 126 pounds. The WBO featherweight champion is also realistic, keeping the door open to move up to super featherweight if elite opportunities don’t materialize.

At 6’1″, the Mexican titlist wants unification honors at featherweight, knowing a win over Inoue punches his ticket straight into pound-for-pound conversations. He is even game to travel to Tokyo to make it happen.

“There’s also a big fight, the Inoue fight, and I think that’s the fight that would launch me into the world pound-for-pound rankings. That’s my dream,” Espinoza said to The Ring.

Landing the bout is another story. Espinoza presents an awkward, grueling test for anyone stepping up in weight. His height, wingspan, and relentless motor demand total focus. While Inoue possesses the timing and precision to exploit defensive holes, getting inside on Espinoza means walking through fire against a much bigger fighter.

Espinoza feels fully equipped to take the victory, even if he avoids bold knockout predictions.

“I have the qualities, the desire, and I have the reach, the height. I think I have power,” Espinoza said. “I’m not saying I’m going to knock him out. I’ve never liked talking that way, but I have a lot of hope that I can win that fight.”

Under the guidance of trainer Eddy Reynoso, Espinoza has spent recent camps dialing in his fundamentals. Rather than crowding opponents and absorbing needless shots, he has been drilling range control, leaning hard into straight punches from the outside.

The risk-to-reward ratio is completely tilted against Espinoza. Inoue gets credit for daring to be great no matter who he faces, but taking on a tall physical anomaly in his first outing at 126 offers minimal extra reward compared to the extreme stylistic danger.

Instead of Espinoza getting rewarded for ruling the division, Top Rank and Inoue’s team have plenty of reason to look elsewhere. Whether that means targeting a more conventionally sized titlist like Leo Angelo or Bruce Carrington, or grabbing the newly stripped WBA belt against an opponent with fewer stylistic advantages, Espinoza could find out the hard way that being the most dangerous man in the room often leaves you standing alone.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis Signs Seven-Fight Extension With Matchroom
Sports.content:
Jaron “Boots” Ennis is locked in for the long haul after signing a massive seven-fight extension with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom. His eyes remain squarely set on collecting every piece of hardware at 154 pounds.

The timing couldn’t be better since IBF champion Josh Kelly signed fresh terms with the promoter on the exact same day. Because both champions share a promotional home, Hearn holds the inside track to set up an in-house unification clash. Whoever walks away with those three belts would then need only Sebastian Fundora’s WBC title to crown an undisputed king.

Ennis, now 29, picked up the WBA alongside the WBO belt after stopping Xander Zayas in Brooklyn this past July. Matchroom hasn’t announced a date or next rival just yet, but the mission statement is clear.

“I’m excited for my extended partnership with Matchroom,” Ennis stated. “Together we have aligned ourselves in all the right positions to get what I want, and that’s undisputed!” A seven-fight commitment gives Hearn plenty of runway. Still, locking down every title means hammering out contracts with rival camps, and Kelly’s signature alone doesn’t automatically settle fight terms.

Fundora brings another challenge to the bargaining table. His team wants an even split for any clash with Boots. If Ennis handles Kelly first to claim the IBF strap, he enters negotiations holding three belts, giving him total leverage to demand the lion’s share. Yet Fundora would still hold the final piece of the puzzle Ennis desires.

Ennis originally teamed up with Matchroom back in April 2024. That run saw him defend his turf in Philadelphia against David Avanesyan, beat Karen Chukhadzhian, then unify at welterweight by taking down Eimantas Stanionis in Atlantic City. Since jumping up to light middleweight, he obliterated Uisma Lima inside a single round before outclassing Zayas to become a two-division unified champ.

Hearn made his intentions clear, stating the entire Matchroom team plans to honor that loyalty by delivering undisputed opportunities on boxing’s premier stages.

Now comes the real work: turning contract ink into confirmed fight dates. Locking down Kelly gets the ball rolling toward three belts, setting up a clash with Fundora to finish the undisputed sweep.

Hearn had no choice but to lock Ennis down with a massive commitment, because letting him walk into Zuffa’s open arms would have been catastrophic for Matchroom’s stable. Dana White and the Zuffa operation are hungry for legitimate, elite names with actual substance, not smoke and mirrors. Losing Boots to that machine right when Anthony Joshua is clearly nearing the final bell would have stripped Matchroom of its true crown jewel in the United States.

The reality is that Hearn’s roster of genuine, division-ruling stars is paper thin. Ben Whittaker was hyped up as a generational sensation, but the matchmaking quickly exposed the ceiling there. When a promoter has to spoon-feed a 29-year-old fighter soft touches like Richard Rivera just to keep the show on the road, everyone sees through the packaging. Whittaker needs careful stage management and manufactured protection to stay afloat.

Ennis is the exact opposite. Boots does not need protective matchmaking or promotional smoke screens to look elite because the skill set is real. He can fight on the inside, switch stances seamlessly, punch with spite, and wipe out titleholders without Hearn having to hold his hand. While British promoters naturally lean toward homegrown cash cows, Ennis possesses the pedigree to carry the Matchroom banner globally and clean out an entire division on merit alone. Locking him in for seven bouts ensures Hearn stays relevant in the US market instead of watching Zuffa build their boxing empire around Philadelphia’s best fighter.

Sports.title: David Haye Urges Fabio Wardley To Take Year Off
Sports.content:
David Haye thinks Fabio Wardley needs to step away from the ring for an entire year to rebuild his mechanics from the ground up following another brutal second-round TKO loss to Daniel Dubois.

While Haye still sees a path forward for Wardley, he doubts a standard eight-week training camp offers enough runway to fix the technical flaws Dubois repeatedly punished. His advice is simple: take an extended break to master the fundamental skills Wardley missed by turning pro without an amateur background.

“He should take a year out. But not a year out partying, holiday. No, just working on the basic fundamentals,” Haye said to talkSPORT Boxing about Wardley. “Go get a good Cuban coach, someone who just gets your legs right, gets your balance.”

Haye is assuming a lot if he thinks a year off in a Cuban school of boxing is going to rewire a 31-year-old brawler who learned his trade on the white-collar circuit. Fighters do not magically develop fluid footwork, ring IQ, and nuanced balance at this stage of life in an empty gym. Those instincts are drilled into kids through hundreds of amateur bouts between the ages of twelve and twenty.

If Wardley steps away for twelve months with millions already sitting in the bank, he will not return as Guillermo Rigondeaux. He will return as an older, heavier, rustier version of the exact same guy, minus whatever sharp edge kept him dangerous.

Taking a year off ignores human nature, especially for a fighter who just cashed massive checks. Inactivity dulls timing and slows reflexes, and when a fighter relies almost entirely on explosive athleticism and punching power, ring rust is lethal.

“In the heat of the battle, you do what you do,” Haye explained. “He hasn’t done the correct thing, enough reps.” “He could continue in this division, and we’ll have some great fights, but it’s not going to be good for his health.”

The blueprint to keep his career alive is obvious: step down levels immediately. Wardley needs active reps under the lights against beatable, mid-tier opposition. He needs guys who will test him for six to eight rounds without having the world-class power or technical precision of a Daniel Dubois or Joseph Parker to punish every fundamental mistake.

The punishment he absorbed across those three elite fights is the kind that takes chunks out of a fighter’s prime. Throwing him into gym purgatory will only make him think too much in the ring, and a hesitant brawler gets knocked out twice as fast.

Ghana News.title: From Potential to Practice: Africa’s AI decade has begun
Ghana News.content:
A month after PAAIS 2026, the summit's convenor reflects on what the room revealed and what leaders in boardrooms and ministries must do now.

Watching the highlights film from this year's Pan African AI & Innovation Summit, I was struck less by the stage than by the people in the audience. Bankers beside students. Regulators beside founders. Civil servants taking notes next to engineers who build the very systems those civil servants will one day have to govern. For two days in Accra, people who rarely shared a room faced a shared problem and treated it as their own.

That, in a sentence, is why the Pan African AI & Innovation Summit exists.

The audience no longer

For too long, the global story of artificial intelligence may have cast Africa as the audience. Models are trained elsewhere on data that rarely reflects our languages, markets, or people, then arrive here as finished products to be adopted, priced, and regulated after the fact. The risk is that we live inside it on terms that are written by someone else.

What I heard across the keynotes and corridor conversations this September was a refusal of that role. Africa will not wait to see how AI unfolds globally. We are deciding how it will serve our economies, our institutions and our people.

The gap we must name

Ambition is often perceived by many as readiness, but it’s not, and honesty demands that we say so.

Ahead of the summit, PAAIS surveyed 100 professionals from 89 institutions in preparation for our AI masterclass in partnership with the Chartered Institute of Bankers Ghana. 65% said their organisations were still at the pre-pilot stage. 68% had no AI governance committee. Most strikingly, 18 of the 35 organisations already piloting or scaling AI were doing so without one.

Read that again. Half of the institutions already putting AI in front of customers have no formal body asking who is accountable when it goes wrong. And the outcome respondents wanted most, chosen by 50%, was a governance framework their boards could use.

This is not a story of reluctance. It is a story of people moving faster than the structures meant to protect them and the public they serve. Closing that gap is precisely the work a convening like ours is built for.

Why the room matters

Policy developed without industry input can never be truly complete. Likewise, an industry that advances without policy rests on a fragile foundation. And when both are shaped without young people at the table, they risk building a future for a generation they never consulted. In Africa, home to the youngest population in the world, the voices, ideas, and aspirations of young people are essential to creating sustainable and inclusive progress.

PAAIS rests on four commitments: equipping young people with skills, strengthening policy and digital sovereignty, unlocking partnership and investment, and insisting that AI be applied ethically in the sectors closest to daily life, namely health, agriculture, education and finance. None of these works alone. A skilled graduate without an investor stalls. A brilliant regulation that no one in industry understands gathers dust. Investment without ethical guardrails eventually costs more trust than it earns. The summit's purpose is to hold these forces in the same room long enough for them to discover they need each other.

What I ask of leaders

To business leaders: establish AI governance before your next pilot, not after your first incident. Your board deserves a framework, and your customers deserve to know that someone is accountable.

To technology leaders: build for the user in Kumasi as seriously as the user in London. Local language, local data and local context. They are the product.

To government institutions: We are grateful that our leaders are increasingly recognising convening as critical infrastructure. The regulators who engage founders, innovators, and industry leaders before drafting policy invariably create stronger, more practical, and future-ready frameworks. As several Ministers highlighted during the summit, digital sovereignty is about where data is stored. Equally, it is also about whether we possess the capability, expertise, and confidence to make strategic decisions for ourselves. True sovereignty is built on infrastructure, competence, ownership, and the capacity to shape our own technological destiny.

The human reality

It would be easy to write about AI entirely in numbers. But the energy in that hall was not statistical. It was hope, carefully tested. People did not come to be dazzled by technology. They came to find out whether it could be made to work for the nurse, the farmer, the bank teller and the young person they know by name.

The summit lasted two days. The work it began will take a generation. No one will hand Africa an AI future that fits us. We are building it together, in rooms like that one, to solve our own challenges and then carry it back into our boardrooms, ministries and classrooms.

The conversation continues toward PAAIS 2027. I invite every leader reading this to take a seat at the table.

Ghana News.title: Finance Ministry to meet maritime stakeholders over Tema Port clearance delays
Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson

The Ministry of Finance will meet key stakeholders in Ghana’s maritime and logistics sectors on Wednesday, October 21, to discuss proposed changes to customs clearance procedures amid concerns about persistent delays and rising costs at Tema Port.

The meeting will review existing cargo clearance processes and consider proposed amendments aimed at addressing operational challenges affecting the smooth and timely movement of goods.

The engagement follows calls by the Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana (IEAG) for urgent intervention over delays in shipping invoices, payment processing and container releases.

The Association says the bottlenecks are increasing demurrage, rent and storage charges for businesses operating through the port.

IEAG has also raised concerns about reported disruptions at Meridian Port Services (MPS) Terminal 3, where more than 120 trucks scheduled to transfer containers were reportedly delayed.

It warned that the situation could extend truck turnaround times, disrupt haulage schedules and increase operating costs for importers and other port users, calling for an investigation to establish the causes and determine responsibility.

In an invitation signed by Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Nyarko Ampem on behalf of the Finance Minister, the Ministry said its Revenue Policy Division had conducted a preliminary assessment of existing customs clearance procedures and identified operational challenges affecting cargo movement.

The Ministry said the stakeholder meeting would provide an opportunity to discuss and review proposed amendments. Expected participants include the Ghana Revenue Authority, Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority, Ghana Shippers’ Authority, Ghana Link Network Services, Meridian Port Services Limited, industry associations and other maritime sector stakeholders.

Ghana News.title: NDPC DG urges action on existing policies to boost Ghana’s human capital
Ghana News.content:
The Director-General of the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), Dr Audrey Smock Amoah, has called on stakeholders to focus on implementing existing policies and commitments to build a productive human capital ecosystem in Ghana.

She said the country already had policies, institutions and legislative frameworks to support human capital development, stressing that the priority should be to translate these commitments into practical outcomes rather than continually developing new policy documents.

Dr Amoah made the remarks at the sixth annual Precision Policy Conference on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, under the theme “Human Capital at Work.”

“Please, let us work with what we have and translate these existing commitments into tangible change,” she said.

She explained that human capital development required coordinated action across health, early childhood development, education, skills training, employment and enterprise development to ensure that people acquired relevant skills and applied them productively.

The NDPC Director-General also emphasised the need for adequate financing, monitoring, evaluation and learning to ensure that policies translated into measurable improvements in people's lives.

“Let us move from policy to plans, from plans to budgets, and from commitments to implementation,” she said.

Dr Amoah expressed hope that the conference would generate practical recommendations to strengthen the proposed Human Capital Development Strategy and connect the various policy areas into a coherent and productive ecosystem.

The Founder and President of the Design and Technology Institute (DTI), Constance Swaniker, said Ghana’s ambition to become a high-income nation by 2057 would depend on the productivity and capabilities of its people.

She cited the World Bank’s Human Capital Index, noting that a child born in Ghana today was expected to attain about 45 per cent of the productivity potential associated with full health and quality education.

Ms Swaniker urged stakeholders to view human capital as a productive asset, arguing that development efforts must consider not only educational qualifications but also people's ability to contribute meaningfully to the economy.

“Human capital is built by all of us, or it is not built at all,” she said, highlighting the shared responsibility of government, industry, academia, development partners and young people.

Ghana News.title: NDPC boss urges greater use of evaluation evidence in national development planning
Ghana News.content:
The Director-General of the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), Dr Audrey Smock Amoah, has called for greater use of evaluation evidence in national development planning to improve policy implementation, resource allocation and accountability.

She made the call at the 2026 Ghana Evaluation Week (GEW) Conference at the University of Ghana, Legon, held under the theme, “Strengthening Evidence Use for Inclusive Development: Bridging Policy, Practice and Innovation.”

Dr Amoah said evaluation should go beyond collecting data and producing reports to directly informing policy decisions and delivering measurable development outcomes.

“Evaluation must help us identify what works, understand implementation gaps and determine what needs to change to deliver better outcomes for all,” she said.

She explained that evidence from the evaluation of the 2022–2025 Medium-Term National Development Policy Framework had informed four strategic shifts in the 2026–2029 framework.

These include strengthening institutional and human capital, advancing regulatory and legal reforms, ensuring predictable financing and promoting data-driven coordination.

According to Dr Amoah, incorporating evaluation findings into planning processes is essential to ensuring that development policies respond to identified challenges and achieve their intended objectives.

Lakeside Estate has reaffirmed its commitment to quality housing, customer satisfaction and innovation in Ghana’s real estate sector.

For prospective homeowners, LAKESIDE ESTATES remain your number choice in the real estate industry. Ghana News.title: Bekwai MP distributes 450 streetlights, 2,500 LED bulbs across constituency
Ghana News.content:
The Member of Parliament for Bekwai, Ralph Poku-Adusei, has distributed 450 streetlights and 2,500 LED bulbs across the constituency under his “Let Bekwai Shine” initiative.

The distribution, which took place on Sunday, October 18, covered all 34 electoral areas and schools, while the LED bulbs were allocated to tertiary and second-cycle institutions, hospitals, health centres and other key institutions.

Mr Poku-Adusei said the initiative was in response to calls from constituents for additional streetlights and LED bulbs to improve visibility and security in their communities.

He explained that the installation of the lighting facilities was intended to brighten the constituency and reduce incidents of crime and attacks carried out under the cover of darkness.

According to the MP, improved lighting would also help residents and businesses carry out their activities more safely, while supporting economic activity across the constituency.

“Bekwai must shine!” he said, describing the initiative as part of his broader vision to make the constituency self-sufficient.

The intervention is expected to improve lighting in public spaces and key institutions, with the distribution of streetlights across all 34 electoral areas aimed at extending the benefits to communities throughout the constituency.

Ghana News.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Aligning Resources with Strategic Ambition.
Ghana News.content:
Insight

An organisation cannot achieve its strategic ambitions if its resources remain tied to outdated priorities. CEOs must ensure that budgets, talent, technology, and operational capacity are aligned with the results the organisation intends to deliver.

Resource allocation is not simply an annual budgeting exercise. It is an ongoing leadership responsibility that requires difficult choices, regular performance reviews, and a willingness to redirect resources when circumstances change.

Key Strategies:

1. Map available resources against the organization’s strategic priorities.

2. Identify capability gaps that could prevent successful execution.

3. Prioritize investments based on strategic value and expected returns.

4. Reduce spending on activities that no longer justify their resource requirements.

5. Review resource allocation as performance, risks, and opportunities evolve.

CEO Leadership Actions.

✅ Require each major strategic initiative to have a realistic resource plan.

✅ Identify areas where investment is insufficient or resources are being underused.

✅ Ensure that resource allocation decisions reflect strategic priorities rather than historical budgets alone.

Actionable Tip.

* Ask: “If we were allocating our resources from scratch today, would we distribute them in the same way?”

Why This Matters?

Strategic ambition without appropriate resources remains an aspiration. When CEOs align investment and organizational capacity with priorities, they improve execution, strengthen financial discipline, and increase the likelihood of achieving meaningful results.

About the Author

Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

Ghana News.title: FDA orders 14-day recall of Franko Herbal Mixture over drug contamination
Ghana News.content:
The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) has ordered Franko Herbal Centre to recall its Franko Herbal Mixture from the market within 14 days after laboratory tests detected diazepam and paracetamol in the product.

The Authority has also shut down the company’s manufacturing facility at Jacobu in the Ashanti Region, warning that failure to comply with the directives could lead to further regulatory sanctions, including criminal prosecution.

In a statement, the FDA said laboratory analysis found that the product, registered as a herbal medicinal preparation containing Carica papaya, Alstonei boonei and Tetrapleura tetraptera, had been adulterated with diazepam, a prescription-only medicine, and paracetamol, commonly used to relieve pain and reduce fever.

The FDA said the presence of the two pharmaceutical substances in a product registered strictly as a herbal medicine violated regulatory requirements and posed serious health risks to consumers. It added that it would supervise the safe disposal of all recalled products to ensure they were completely removed from circulation.

The Authority explained that diazepam, a benzodiazepine, is prescribed for conditions including anxiety disorders, acute alcohol withdrawal, muscle spasms and certain types of seizures.

However, it warned that its presence in an unapproved herbal formulation could expose consumers to dangerous effects, particularly when taken with other medicines.

According to the FDA, interactions involving diazepam can increase the risk of severe sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death.

The Authority has urged compliance with its recall directive to protect public health and ensure the safety of medicinal products on the Ghanaian market.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Attack on Australian MP Haines: How threats against legislators have soared
World.content:
Abuse and threats against Australian lawmakers are rising in a country where political violence has historically been rare.

Share Attack on Australian MP: How threats against legislators have soared on social media

An Australian independent lawmaker, Helen Haines, has had both legs amputated after ⁠being struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria state, in what Prime Minister ⁠Anthony Albanese called “a deliberate attack”.

The MP’s right leg was amputated on Wednesday, two days after her left leg was amputated at a hospital in Melbourne, where the 65-year-old politician has been receiving treatment after being flown by helicopter.

Recommended Stories list of 1 item list 1 of 1 Australian MP Helen Haines critically injured in ‘deliberate’ car ramming end of list

“The good news in all this is that Helen is alive and she’s stable. That is the most important thing for our family,” her husband, Phil Haines, told reporters outside the Melbourne hospital.

“We are grateful and thankful that, at this stage, both her heart and her mind are in good shape,” he said.

The Australian police said it was a “targeted attack” and warned of growing “online extremism” and recorded a rise in abuse, threats and intimidation targeting lawmakers – steadily growing in a country where political violence has been rare.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has led an outpouring of support for Haines. “It’s a reminder that the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago,” Albanese told ABC Radio on Wednesday.

“I think that Australians do want to see their politicians be able to go about their business, to be able to get something from the back of their car, for goodness sake.”

So, why have threats against Australian lawmakers risen?

What do we know about the alleged attack?

On Monday, Haines, who entered parliament in 2019, was struck by an SUV in Wangaratta in the afternoon, sending the rural Australian town into a mix of horror and disbelief.



Haines was getting something from the boot of her car when her alleged attacker drove past in a Toyota Land Cruiser. Authorities said the 43-year-old man turned the car around before veering at Haines and pinning her against her vehicle. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said the driver then reversed before ramming her again.

Police named the suspect in the attack as Brendan Nugent, who appeared in court on Wednesday but did not apply for bail or enter a plea.

He was charged with three offences: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a public official. Additional charges of cannabis cultivation and possession have also been laid against him.

Nugent will remain in custody until his next court appearance in February.

The Australian Federal Police received no warning of any imminent danger from the alleged attacker, Commissioner Krissy Barrett told reporters.

“What I can ⁠say is we didn’t have any specific intelligence that would have indicated something as atrocious as happened on Monday afternoon,” she said.

Victoria Police Chief Mike Bush said the state police could not find any direct past contact ⁠between Haines and the accused.

“Motivation is one of ⁠these things that we absolutely need to explore. His motivation for this, what we allege is a deliberate attack, is very much a centrepiece of the investigation,” Bush said.

Who is Helen Haines?

Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife, becoming known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action. She retained the rural seat of Indi in 2022 and 2025.

She was widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption.

“My background in nursing guides my work. As a nurse and a midwife, you’re with people in their most joyous and difficult moments. It’s taught me that life is precious, that everyone deserves dignity and respect, that good policy starts with listening, and – as a health researcher – that facts matter,” she describes herself on her website.

“Every day, I work to be a strong, independent voice – guided by common sense, decency and a commitment to delivering for our community and your family.”

In parliament, she pushed for a national anticorruption body. She introduced a bill in 2021 for a federal integrity commission, but it was defeated.

A year later, the Australian Parliament passed the National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022, leading to the formation of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC).



Haines, who played a major role in the passing of the bill, served as the deputy chair of the parliamentary committee on the NACC.

Why are threats against lawmakers rising?

The Australian Human Rights Commission said the attack happened “against a backdrop of increasing polarisation and threats against politicians” that could undermine democracy.

Threats against Australian lawmakers and electorate offices doubled between 2021 and 2025, with 1,067 incidents reported to police last year.

The police also charged 41 people with offences relating to threats against parliamentarians last year, after the Australian federal police formed a National Security Investigations team described by police commissioner Barrett as a “flying squad of hate disruptors”.

In the 2025 election, threats to candidates jumped 17 percent from the previous campaign.

Earlier this month, police charged three men over separate threats to politicians and government officials, and three others were sentenced by courts.

Senior opposition politician James Paterson on Wednesday called for a review of personal security in response to the alleged crime. “The reality is that Australian parliamentarians by global standards are uniquely accessible to the public and that’s a good thing,” Paterson told the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.

“But we can’t have a situation where shocking attacks like this take place because that will fundamentally change our democracy forever if it becomes a serious risk to your life to be a member of parliament,” he added.

Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Director-General Mike Burgess warned last year that politically motivated violence was among the agency’s fastest-growing security concerns, driven by “grievance narratives, conspiracies and online echo chambers”.

Antiterrorism police are among the agencies investigating the attack on Haines, but the police maintain that they believe it was an isolated incident and there was “no intelligence to suggest any threat to Haines”.

What do we know about the attacker?

Nugent, a 43-year-old resident of the rural town of Tarrawingee within Haines’s electorate, has been charged with offences that carry a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.

The motive remains unknown, and authorities have refused to speculate while the investigation takes place.

But police said on Wednesday they were examining all possible leads, including that Nugent may have held radical antigovernment views.

“Like everyone, we’re examining social media associations, talking to witnesses, friends and colleagues,” Bush, the Victoria police commissioner, told journalists.

During the brief court appearance on Wednesday, Nugent’s lawyer said his client suffers from a rare neurological condition called idiopathic transverse myelitis and that it was his first time in custody.

Meanwhile, Wangaratta’s Mayor Irene Grant said a sombre mood has settled over the town of about 30,000 people, a regional hub about 250km (155 miles) northeast of state capital Melbourne.



“What has happened to Helen has caused the community to step back in utter disbelief. We can’t believe it; people are horrified by what has happened,” she told AFP news agency.
