World.title: Liberian Senate’s Own Papers Bury Its Denial
World.content:
MONROVIA – On Monday, the Liberian Senate under the leadership of Pro Temp Nyonblee Karnga-Lawrence, called FrontPageAfrica’s reporting on a staff salary plan “false,” “misleading” and “fabricated,” and demanded a retraction. What the Senate did not do is more telling. It did not dispute a single figure, did not challenge the authenticity of a single page, and did not say the plan does not exist.

By Rodney D. Sieh

It could not. The plan is on Senate letterhead.



What the documents say

On October 7, 2026, the Senate Committee on Rules, Order and Administration signed a “Proposal for the Standardization of Remuneration for Civil Servants and Personal Staffers of the Senate.” Six of the seven committee members signed it, including Chairman J. Gbleh-bo Brown of Maryland County and Vice-Chairman Johnathan B. Sogbe. On October 12, Senator Brown sent it to President Pro Tempore Nyonblee Karnga-Lawrence. He asked for leadership’s endorsement and for the plan to be included in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget.

The numbers are the committee’s own:

* The Legal Counsel’s monthly pay rises from US$1,704 to US$2,920, an increase of US$1,216, or 71 percent.

* The HR Director rises from US$1,500 to US$2,000, and the Deputy Legal Counsel from US$1,500 to US$1,991.

* Senators’ chiefs of office staff rise from US$1,021 to US$1,500.

* The total annual cost is US$792,552. The covered payroll grows from US$1,830,648 to US$2,623,200, an increase of 43 percent.

The committee’s final recommendation asks the Senate leadership and plenary to approve US$792,552 for the 2027 budget. That is not a rumor. It is a funding request.

A denial that answers a different question

The Senate’s statement rests on one claim: the plenary never voted. That is true, and it is beside the point.

A proposal that six senators have signed, that the Pro Tempore commissioned, and that is formally headed for the national budget is news. Proposals are exactly when the public should hear about them, before the money is spent rather than after.

The statement also confirms the most important fact. It says the review was “mandated by the President Pro Tempore.” By the Senate’s own account, this plan began in the Pro Tempore’s office.

The fine print the statement leaves out

The statement describes the plan as a review “across the three branches of Government.” The documents cover only Senate staff. The other branches appear only as benchmarks for raising Senate pay.

The statement says the plan has not been “acted upon.” Yet section 2.0 of the committee’s report, titled “What Has Been Accomplished,” says the committee “has completed” standardizing fuel and gas benefits for directors, deputy directors, assistant directors, secretaries, drivers and other staff. The Senate should explain whether those benefits are already being paid.

The statement also accuses this newspaper of failing to verify the facts “through the Senate official spokesperson.” The verification is the documents themselves: the Senate’s letterhead, its committee’s signatures and its own arithmetic.

“Harmony” for whom?

The committee says the 2019 National Remuneration and Standardization Act requires the plan. It quotes the Act’s goal of narrowing “the inequality gap in government.” The tables point the other way.

The Legal Counsel’s raise alone, US$1,216 a month, is larger than the entire current salary of nine of the twelve central administration positions listed. At the bottom of the scale, the Executive Secretary gets US$96.

Today the Legal Counsel earns about three times as much as the Executive Secretary. Under the proposal, that would rise to about four and a half times. In dollar terms, the gap between them nearly doubles, from US$1,153 to US$2,273 a month.

A plan written to narrow inequality would widen it.

The comparison the Senate calls “emotional”

The Senate objects to comparisons with the national minimum wage and calls them “emotional.” They are arithmetic. Labour Minister Cooper W. Kruah has reminded employers that Liberia’s Decent Work Act sets a minimum monthly wage of US$143, and he has warned firms caught paying less.

The proposed raise for the Legal Counsel is roughly eight and a half times that minimum wage. The proposed salary is about twenty times it. That is not the language of emotion. It is the reality of a country where many families decide daily between food, school fees and medicine.

The staff have a case, and that is not the issue

Fairness requires saying this clearly: many Senate employees are underpaid, and their complaints are real. In December, staff spokesperson Roosevelt Tulay told reporters there had been no salary increment for Senate staff since 2015. He pointed out that the Senate’s own budget had grown from US$14.6 million to a proposed US$16.4 million for Fiscal Year 2026, while staff salaries stayed flat, and he warned of civil disobedience.

A serious reform would start at the bottom, with the clerks, secretaries and drivers. This plan gives its biggest dollars to the top. And the Senate’s answer to public scrutiny has been to call accurate reporting “fabricated.”

What the Senate should do

If the Senate believes the plan is sound, it should defend it in public. It should publish the full proposal and the attached spreadsheet, explain the 71 percent raise for its Legal Counsel, disclose whether the fuel benefits are already being paid, and commit to a recorded plenary vote.

What it should not do is demand that a newspaper retract a story built on the Senate’s own signed pages. FrontPageAfrica stands by its reporting.

World.title: Liberia: MCSS Students Storm Capitol Hill, Petition House Over Teacher Crisis and ‘Administrative Lapses’
World.content:
MONROVIA — Frustrated by prolonged school disruptions, students of the Monrovia Consolidated School System (MCSS) on Tuesday took their grievances to Capitol Hill, demanding urgent government intervention in the crisis affecting their teachers and schools.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

Chanting, “We want to learn too,” the students petitioned the House of Representatives to enforce the implementation of a March 27 agreement between the government and MCSS, investigate allegations of intimidation and administrative interference, and increase funding for public schools.



The protest came as a 24-hour ultimatum issued by the Monrovia Consolidated School System Students Union (MCSS-SU) expired on October 20. Hours after the demonstration, the government announced that 201 outstanding volunteer teachers would be enrolled on the national payroll effective October 2026 and that eligible teachers would receive retroactive salaries following the October salary payment.

The government’s announcement marks a response to one of the central grievances underlying the dispute, but questions remain over the implementation of the agreement, outstanding teacher welfare concerns, and the broader administrative problems students say continue to disrupt their education.

Students Take Grievances to Capitol Hill

Thousands of students gathered between the University of Liberia and the Capitol Building, where lawmakers were conducting legislative business, to draw attention to the prolonged challenges confronting the public school system.

The demonstration, which lasted more than two hours, was organized under the banner of the MCSS Students Union. The students said unresolved teacher welfare issues and administrative disputes had deprived them of valuable instructional time.

In a formal petition signed at William V. S. Tubman High School on 12th Street, the union outlined four major demands and warned that it would proceed with peaceful protest action if authorities failed to respond.

The petition was received by several lawmakers, including Nimba County District No. 2 Representative Nyan Flomo, Montserrado County District No. 8 Representative Prince A. Toles, who chairs the House Committee on Claims and Petitions; River Cess County District No. 2 Representative Steve Tequah, chairman of the House Committee on Youth and Sports; and Montserrado County District No. 4 Representative Michael Thomas.

The petition was ultimately handed to Representative Flomo after the students initially rejected presenting it to Representative Toles.

Following its receipt, the petition was read during Tuesday’s plenary session of the House and referred to the Committees on Education and Claims and Petitions. The committees were instructed to report back to the plenary within one week.

Students Demand Implementation of March Agreement

At the center of the students’ demands is the full implementation of the Memorandum of Understanding signed between the government and MCSS on March 27, 2026.

The union said unresolved teacher welfare issues under the agreement continue to threaten the delivery of education across public schools in Monrovia and its environs.

The students are calling on the government to fulfill its commitments, arguing that continued delays have placed an unfair burden on learners who depend on public education.

They warned that their patience should not be interpreted as acceptance of prolonged school disruptions.

“Our patience must not be mistaken for weakness, and our commitment to peace must not be used to justify continued inaction while students’ education remains at risk,” the union stated in its petition.

Union Seeks Dismissal of MCSS Official

The students are also demanding the dismissal of MCSS Assistant Superintendent Emmanuel Kyne Robertson, accusing him of inciting students, disrupting classes and threatening learners.

The petition further alleged that individuals had been sent to attack the president of the MCSS Students Union.

The union called for an investigation into the alleged incident and measures to protect student leaders from intimidation.

The allegations against Robertson have not been independently established in the information provided for this report. He should be given an opportunity to respond to the claims.

The union also accused some school administrators of involving students in personal, administrative and political disputes within the education system.

“Students must not be used as instruments to advance anyone’s personal, administrative, or political interests,” the petition stated.

The students called for greater respect for legitimate student leadership and urged authorities to resolve internal disagreements without disrupting classes or compromising students’ safety.

Budget Increase, Better School Facilities Demanded

Beyond the teacher crisis, the union is calling for an increase in the MCSS budget and greater transparency in the use of public education funds.

While acknowledging ongoing renovations at Boatswain Junior and Senior High School, G.W. Gibson Senior High School and Matilda Newport Junior High School, the students said numerous other schools continue to face poor infrastructure, inadequate classrooms, insufficient furniture and unsanitary conditions.

They argued that addressing teacher welfare alone would not resolve the challenges confronting public education without corresponding investments in school facilities and learning resources.

The union said its demands are intended to restore teaching and learning, protect students, strengthen accountability and improve conditions across the school system.

It formally notified authorities of its intention to organize peaceful protests if its concerns remain unresolved.

Government Moves to Enroll 201 Volunteer Teachers

Hours after the students’ demonstration, the Government of Liberia issued a statement acknowledging concerns raised by MCSS teachers over employment regularization, outstanding salaries and compensation adjustments.

The government said consultations involving the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning, the Civil Service Agency and MCSS had resulted in a decision to enroll the remaining 201 volunteer teachers on the national payroll effective October 2026.

According to the statement, the affected teachers will receive their October salaries as formally employed government teachers, ending their volunteer status.

The decision will bring the total number of verified MCSS volunteer teachers enrolled on the national payroll to 409.

“The Government recognizes the teachers’ invaluable contributions to the country’s educational system and remains committed to addressing their concerns through concrete administrative decisions, responsible financial measures and reforms,” the statement said.

The government also announced that retroactive salaries owed to eligible teachers would be paid one week after the October salary payment, in accordance with their respective eligibility categories.

It described the decision as evidence of its commitment to fulfilling its obligations and ensuring that affected teachers receive their compensation.

Salary Adjustments Still Under Review

On demands for salary adjustments by currently employed MCSS teachers, the government said the concerns would be addressed through an ongoing government-wide salary structure reform.

According to the statement, the proposed reform is intended to correct existing salary disparities, promote fairness and equity, and establish a transparent and sustainable compensation system across the public service.

However, the government did not provide a specific implementation date for the broader salary reform in the statement.

It appealed to public school teachers to remain calm and return to their classrooms while the relevant institutions implement the agreed measures.

The government also urged MCSS students to remain in school and continue their academic activities without interruption, reaffirming its commitment to constructive engagement with teachers and strengthening the country’s education system.

Questions Remain Over Implementation

Although the government’s announcement addresses the employment status of the 201 outstanding volunteer teachers and provides for the settlement of eligible retroactive salaries, the broader dispute involves additional concerns raised by teachers, students and school administrators.

The students’ petition places responsibility on the government and education authorities to ensure that commitments are implemented and that administrative disagreements do not continue to deprive learners of classroom instruction.

The House committees’ one-week deadline to report back to plenary could provide an opportunity for lawmakers to examine the students’ allegations, assess the implementation of the March 27 agreement and determine what further action may be necessary.

For the students who took their demands to Capitol Hill, the immediate concern remains the restoration of uninterrupted teaching and learning.

Their message was direct: while government officials and school administrators negotiate over salaries, employment status and administrative control, students should not continue to pay the price through lost instructional time.

World.title: Liberia: Partisans Allege Push to Hand Party to Koung as Howard-Taylor Faces Drug Charges
World.content:
MONROVIA – The National Patriotic Party (NPP) may be heading into another leadership crisis. Former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor is facing drug charges, and a group of partisans is now openly fighting the party leadership over plans to hold a convention in December. Some party insiders say the dispute is about more than the calendar.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

“I think a few at the top want to use this impasse to sell the NPP to Vice President Jeremiah Koung,” a senior party source told FrontPageAfrica. The source asked not to be named because of how sensitive the internal talks are.



Vice President Koung’s office had not responded to FrontPageAfrica’s request for comment by press time.

Call for postponement

A group calling itself the Concerned Partisans of the National Patriotic Party (CP-NPP) wants the party to postpone the convention planned for December 2026. The group says it is made up of members of the party’s National Executive Committee and longtime stalwarts. In a press release signed by its chairman, Emmanuel Goll, the group said the timing “demonstrates a lack of sensitivity” to the arrest, detention and indictment of Howard-Taylor, the party’s Standard Bearer.

The group warned that going ahead with the convention now “could reinforce growing public perceptions that the arrest and indictment of its Standard Bearer are politically motivated.”

Howard-Taylor was Vice President from 2018 to 2024. She was arrested at Roberts International Airport on August 19, 2026. A Montserrado County grand jury indicted her and others on October 7 over an alleged US$317 million cocaine trafficking operation. The case is linked to the seizure of about four metric tons of cocaine in Duazon in July. The charges include drug trafficking, criminal conspiracy, and money laundering. Reports say she was later placed under house arrest on medical grounds while the case continues. She is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Biney in the crosshairs

The CP-NPP’s sharpest criticism is aimed at Senator James Biney, who chairs the Senate Committee on Executive. The group pointed to what it called his “proximity to the ruling establishment” and accused him of allegedly influencing a faction of the party’s executive committee to push for “a contentious convention.”

The group said thisraises concerns that Biney is trying “to advance his ambition to become Political Leader” in a way that, in its view, goes against Articles III and V of the party’s 2004 Constitution.

Biney and Howard-Taylor have fought before over who controls the NPP. Their earlier struggles split the party and ended up before the National Elections Commission.

Senator Biney did not respond to FPA’s inquiry up to press time.

‘Unexpected’ timetable

According to the CP-NPP, consultations about moving the convention to a later date were still going on among executive committee members, the Advisory Council and party stalwarts when the Party Secretariat “unexpectedly released a timetable of convention activities.” The group said it issued its release as “a caution against actions that could deepen existing divisions and generate further crises.”

Constitutional questions

The group’s legal argument is built on the party constitution, which provides for two kinds of convention:

• Biennial Convention (Section 3.2(b)): held every other year on the second Saturday of December

• National Convention (Section 3.2(a)): held every six years or in a national election year

Article V, Section 5.22(VII) says the Standard Bearer stays in office until the next National Convention. By the CP-NPP’s reading, that is not due until 2029.

Because the leadership has fixed the date on the second Saturday of December, the group says the gathering is a Biennial Convention. It asked: “If the proposed gathering is a Biennial Convention, why did the Party’s leadership reportedly present it to the National Elections Commission as a National Convention?”

It also questioned why the December meeting “appear[s] to be aimed at replacing the sitting Standard Bearer with a Political Leader through a process that CP-NPP considers unconstitutional.”

“An indictment does not constitute a conviction or establish guilt,” the group said. “The Party must not disregard constitutional safeguards or treat allegations against its Standard Bearer as proof of wrongdoing.”

The CP-NPP wants the leadership to revisit the group’s July 20, 2026 letter to the National Elections Commission and the Commission’s reply dated September 17, 2026.

The group admitted that the party’s long internal crisis has left many officials serving after their terms expired. It argued that if those officials can stay in office until a proper convention elects their successors, the Standard Bearer should be allowed to do the same.

“The Constitution must remain the supreme authority in the affairs of the Party,” the release concluded, “and no individual ambition should take precedence over its provisions.”

The NPP Secretariat had not responded to questions about the convention timetable by press time.

World.title: Liberia: Snowe Seeks Audit Over Alleged Kickbacks in Bomi, Presses Education Ministry on School Closed Three Years
World.content:
Monrovia – Bomi County Senator Edwin Melvin Snowe, Jr. has called for an urgent, independent audit of local government spending in the county, citing allegations that some officials are spending county resources without adequate accountability and inflating contract values to facilitate possible kickbacks.

By Rodney D. Sieh

Speaking as the Liberian Senate resumed its legislative duties, Sen. Snowe told his colleagues that the implementation of the Local Government Act, passed by the Legislature, “raises serious concerns requiring our urgent attention.” He said the allegations warrant an audit “to establish the facts and ensure appropriate action where wrongdoing is found.”



The senator also urged the Legislature to revisit provisions governing the qualifications, selection and responsibilities of County Council members, saying lawmakers must address weaknesses that undermine competent representation, transparency and accountability.

School Closed for More Than Three Years

Sen. Snowe drew particular attention to Bomi Junior High School, which he said has been closed for more than three years because of a damaged roof. Its students are currently being accommodated at C. H. Dewey High School.

He told the Senate that when the Minister of Education appeared before the body, she made a firm commitment to intervene urgently. “Regrettably, that commitment remains unfulfilled,” he said.

According to the senator, he wrote to the Minister offering to use his legislative project funds to repair the roof. The Minister, he said, asked him to hold off, explaining that funding was available and that the repairs were awaiting approval from the Public Procurement and Concessions Commission (PPCC), along with works at other schools across the country.

“Our students cannot continue to bear the consequences of these delays,” Sen. Snowe said, calling on the plenary to require the Minister to explain the outstanding procurement issues and provide a definite timetable for the repairs.

He also asked the relevant Senate committee to examine concerns about the Western Region University’s compliance with its Charter, particularly the constitution of its governing Board and the recruitment of its leadership. The university, he said, is now fully operational.

Development Projects and Student Support

Sen. Snowe listed ongoing projects in the county, including a public clinic in Weajour, an auditorium for the Sess Town High School and a town hall in Lower Zor. He said he continues to provide full scholarships for 100 students at the Western Region University and, during the period under review, gave short-term vacation jobs to 536 students. Each student worked two hours daily for four days and received LRD 5,000 toward returning to school.

He noted that, despite political differences, he and his Bomi colleague, Senator Alex Tyler, maintain a cordial working relationship.

“Follow the Money”

Turning to national matters, the senator acknowledged that Liberia’s budget has crossed the billion-dollar mark, describing it as a significant milestone. But he warned that the Senate “cannot continue to celebrate increased revenues or reported budget surpluses while our communities struggle to see the benefits.”

“Our oversight must follow the money from allocation to release, expenditure, and results,” he said, adding that institutions falling behind on implementation must explain the delays.

As Chairman of the Senate Committee on Hydrocarbon, Energy and Environment, Sen. Snowe said his committee continues oversight of electricity generation and distribution, tariffs, petroleum-sector governance and environmental protection, working with institutions including the LEC, LERC, EPA and NIC.

He also called for sustained legislative and budgetary support for the fight against drugs, covering prevention, enforcement, treatment and rehabilitation.

US$17.5 Million Owed to ECOWAS

Sen. Snowe raised alarm over Liberia’s reported US$17.5 million in arrears to ECOWAS, recommending that the relevant committees engage the Ministries of Finance and Development Planning and Foreign Affairs to establish the status of the debt and secure a practical payment plan.

He said the arrears must be addressed as Liberia eyes major regional roles, including the possibility of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai chairing the ECOWAS Authority of Heads of State and Government, and the presidency of the ECOWAS Commission, allocated to Liberia for 2030–2034 subject to meeting the applicable criteria.

He recognized three Liberians serving in regional institutions: Hon. Dehpue Yenpea Zuo, ECOWAS Commissioner for Economic Affairs and Agriculture; Hon. Boima S. Kamara, Director General of the West African Monetary Agency; and Justice Charlyne M. Brumskine, President of the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice, whom he described as the first Liberian to head an ECOWAS institution.

Africa CDC Appointment, Diaspora Voting

The senator announced his appointment to the Continental Immunization Advisory Council of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC). He said the council’s new 15-member configuration includes three parliamentarians from across the continent, and he is one of them.

He also recommended that the Legislature begin a structured examination of diaspora voting, saying the continued inability of Liberians in the United States and elsewhere to vote from abroad “deserves serious legislative consideration.”

Sen. Snowe thanked President Boakai for inviting him to development discussions in the United States with American inventor Dr. Lonnie Johnson, and said a formal report on those talks will be submitted to the Senate.

World.title: Liberia: U.S. Embassy Officials Visit Leading War Crimes Investigators in Show of Support, Investigators Say
World.content:
Liberia’s leading war crimes investigation group says a visit by U.S. Embassy officials was intended to reassure its staff about their security. From left: Hassan Bility, director of the Global Justice and Research Project; Christopher M. Hofmann, political officer; and Thomas Quaye, political and human rights assistant at the U.S. Embassy in Liberia. Credit: Anthony Stephens/New Narratives.

Summary:

Two U.S. Embassy officials visited Liberia’s leading war crimes investigation group following death threats against its director of investigations, who was subsequently relocated for security reasons.

Hassan Bility, the group’s director, described the visit as a show of American solidarity while the officials declined to comment on the visit.

The visit comes amid security concerns linked to investigations involving alleged Liberian war criminals, including former senior army commander Moses Wright, whose U.S. trial has been postponed until February 2027.

By Anthony Stephens, senior justice correspondent with New Narratives

Two officials from the U.S. Embassy in Monrovia visited the Global Justice and Research Project, Liberia’s leading war crimes investigation group, two weeks after it relocated its director of investigations following repeated death threats . The group’s director said the visit was an expression of American solidarity with his organization.



Christopher M. Hofmann, a political officer at the Embassy, and Thomas Quaye, a political and human rights assistant, visited the organization earlier this month. They allowed this reporter to photograph their visit but declined to comment on the discussions, referring questions to Hassan Bility, the group’s director.

“The U.S. had come to listen to some of our security concerns,” Bility said in an interview after the meeting. “Their coming was a solidarity of support to indicate that the United States stands with us, and the United States will not stand by idly to allow somebody to do harm to the Global Justice and Research Project.”

The visit comes amid growing security concerns involving the Global Justice and Research Project, whose investigations have contributed to convictions of former rebel commanders over their Liberia war-related crimes, in the United States and Europe. The organization has repeatedly faced threats and attacks.

The latest threats were directed at an investigator working on cases involving alleged wartime perpetrators, including Moses Wright, 73, a former senior Liberian army commander accused of concealing his wartime activities when applying for U.S. immigration benefits. Survivors have accused Wright of involvement in the 1990 St. Peter’s Lutheran Church massacre, in which an estimated 600 civilians were killed. He faces federal immigration fraud and perjury charges in Pennsylvania and has denied the charges.

Bility said his organization had sought security assistance from the two-member U.S. Embassy delegation but declined to share what they said. Nevertheless he said he was comforted by the visit.

“I feel more secure,” Bility said of the embassy’s visit. “Every time U.S. embassy officials visit this office, for us, it becomes an expression of solidarity with our works and our belief, what we stand for. And we know what they can do.”

In 2021, Michael McCarthy, then the U.S. ambassador to Liberia, visited the group’s offices and publicly expressed support for Bility’s work amid threats against the organization.

The organization has faced other security incidents. Earlier this year, armed men broke into its Monrovia offices , assaulted a security guard and threatened Bility, prompting renewed concerns about the safety of those investigating wartime atrocities.

A portion of the 16-foot fence surrounding the offices of the Global Justice and Research Project, which the group says were recently broken into by armed men.Credit: Global Justice and Research Project.

Bility said the Liberia National Police had not provided updates on complaints the organization filed concerning the threats. Gregory Coleman, Liberia’s police inspector general, did not respond to the latest request for comment.

The Global Justice and Research Project and its Swiss partner, Civitas Maxima, have helped document atrocities committed during Liberia’s civil wars, gathering evidence and identifying witnesses for investigations and prosecutions in the United States and Europe.

Their work has contributed to several convictions. In the United States, Mohammed Jabateh, a former rebel commander known as “Jungle Jabbah,” was sentenced to 30 years in prison for immigration fraud and perjury. In Switzerland, Alieu Kosiah, another former rebel commander, received a 20-year sentence for war crimes . In France, Kunti Kamara, a former commander of the same rebel group, was sentenced to 30 years imprisonment in 2022 for complicity in crimes against humanity, torture and acts of barbarism.

The organizations’ work has also drawn accusations of witness coaching and bribery from defendants and their supporters, allegations they, investigators and prosecutors in every case have rejected.

In 2022, Beth Van Schaack, then the U.S. ambassador-at-large for global criminal justice, publicly backed Bility and his organization , praising their contribution to international prosecutions.

“These cases would not be possible without the amazing work of the Global Justice and Research Project and other Liberian and international civil society actors who have rigorously, reliably, and with unwavering integrity worked to keep the dream of justice alive,” she said.

Van Schaack also expressed concern about threats and intimidation against the organization’s staff.

Threats against Global Justice have fueled concerns about security for witnesses and officials of Liberia’s proposed war and economic crimes court. The country’s Witness Protection Agency recently unveiled a US$20.54 million plan they said would be needed to support the activities of the court.

World.title: Liberia Ready for Scrabble Nations Cup as 16th Africa Championship Draws Near
World.content:
MONROVIA — Liberia is set to host the 16th Africa Scrabble Championship (ASC) as national delegations from across the continent begin arriving in Monrovia for the four-day event, scheduled to run from October 22 to 25.

By Christopher C. Walker, [email protected]

The tournament will feature players from 24 African nations at the Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Ministerial Complex in Congo Town, positioning Liberia at the center of the continent’s competitive Scrabble landscape.



Anticipation is building ahead of Thursday’s official kickoff. Defending champion Nigeria is eyeing another continental title, Kenya is sending a massive contingent, and neighboring Sierra Leone is making its journey by road.

Participating athletes will compete for both individual and national honors in a sport that requires vocabulary mastery, spatial strategy, board management, and mental stamina.

Contingents Arrive as Nigeria Targets Title Defense

Kenya began its arrivals on Tuesday evening, with an initial group landing at Roberts International Airport aboard ASKY Airlines at 5:50 p.m.

While 15 members of the delegation received government sponsorship, the total Kenyan contingent is expected to be substantially larger, with team officials indicating up to 32 players could represent the East African power.

Meanwhile, Nigeria’s national team officially departed for Monrovia on Tuesday, intent on defending its continental crown against top-tier contenders and emerging nations.

Sierra Leone is also scheduled to enter Liberia by road via the Bo Waterside border crossing, adding a strong West African regional presence.

Association President: “Liberia Is Prepared”

Addressing journalists at the Ministry of Information, Liberian Scrabble Association (LSA) President Lester Morris confirmed that all hosting arrangements are complete and urged Liberians to attend in large numbers.

“Liberia is fully prepared to host this championship,” Morris said, encouraging the public to support local players and witness high-level intellectual sport firsthand.

Liberia, hosting the ASC represents both a test of its sports management capabilities and a major opportunity for local players to test their skills against the continent’s best.

Four Days of High-Stakes Strategy

The championship officially opens on Thursday, October 22, and concludes on Sunday, October 25.

Over ninety-six hours of continuous play, competitors will battle through a grueling schedule where dynamic word knowledge, board control, and quick decision-making will decide the ultimate winners.

By Thursday morning, administrative preparations will yield to live play as Monrovia welcomes Africa’s elite Scrabble community for four days of strategic competition.

World.title: Liberia: Koulibaly Shines on Borough FC Return With Goal and Crucial Saves
World.content:
MONROVIA — Goalkeeper Abdulai Koulibaly marked his return to Borough FC in dramatic fashion on Sunday, scoring a second-half penalty and making a series of crucial saves in a 1-1 draw against Heaven Eleven in the opening fixture of the 2026/27 Liberia Football Association (LFA) First Division season.

By Christopher C. Walker, [email protected]

Playing at the D. Twe Sports Pitch in New Kru Town, Koulibaly who recently rejoined Borough on a two-year deal following his departure from LPRC Oilers proved decisive at both ends of the pitch.



The shot-stopper broke the deadlock in the 70th minute, calmly step-stepping up to convert from the penalty spot to give the hosts a 1-0 lead.

Beyond his goal, Koulibaly produced a commanding display between the posts, turning away several dangerous efforts from Heaven Eleven to preserve Borough’s advantage.

However, Borough’s bid for all three points was thwarted in the 84th minute when Heaven Eleven’s Moses Cooper rose above the defense to head home the equalizer.

Experienced Head Back in New Kru Town

Despite conceding late, Koulibaly’s individual performance provided a major highlight for Borough as the club aims to build momentum in the new campaign.

Koulibaly brings a rich legacy back to the club, having featured prominently across its previous names from Monrovia Club Breweries to Global Pharma FC and now Borough FC.

During his previous stint, he helped the club secure two Orange FA Cups and two Second Division titles.

After departing at the end of the 2024/25 season for LPRC Oilers, Koulibaly mutually terminated his contract with Oilers to pave the way for his return to New Kru Town.

Borough FC will look to claim its first victory of the new season on Thursday, October 22, when they travel to Tusa Field to face Gardnersville FC.

World.title: UPEZZA digital platform launched
World.content:
Government says technology should not be viewed as a threat to existing jobs but as an opportunity to create new jobs, improve productivity and generate economic opportunities.

Ministry of Technology and Science Permanent Secretary, Brilliant Habeenzu has further called for increased collaboration among the government, the private sector, financial institutions and academic institutions to support local innovators through financing, mentorship and business development services.

He has reaffirmed the government’s commitment to creating an enabling environment for science, technology and innovation to contribute to national development, job creation and economic growth.

Dr Habeenzu said this in a speech delivered on his behalf by the Ministry’s Assistant Director for ICT and Postal Services, Khumbuzo Nkunika, during the launch of Upezza digital platform in Lusaka today.

He noted that Upezza digital platform helps connect landlords, estate agents and prospective tenants, while providing reliable property information to Zambians living abroad who wish to invest in the country.

Dr Habeenzu noted that applications such as Upezza, demonstrate how local innovation can address real challenges while contributing to the country’s broader economic transformation aspirations.

He also said digital platforms could improve tax compliance in the property sector by promoting transparency among landlords and estate agents.

Meanwhile, Upezza Founder and Director, Nchimunya Ndiili, says the digital platform is aimed at making property discovery easier, faster and more convenient for Zambians seeking accommodation and commercial properties.

Dr Ndiili explained that the application connects property seekers with landlords, property owners, developers and real estate agents through digital technology.

She added that the platform is expected to reduce the time, cost and inconvenience associated with searching for accommodation, as many people spend money travelling from one location to another in search of suitable properties.

Dr Ndiili said Upezza also seeks to address challenges associated with misleading addresses and unverified property listings, which can expose unsuspecting property seekers to exploitation.

She also stated that the application would contribute to economic growth by improving access to property information in both established and emerging economic centres.

Dr Ndiili said the initiative aligns with the government’s development agenda, as economic growth is expected to increase demand for accommodation and commercial properties.

World.title: Cybersecurity agency advises the public against online scams
World.content:
The Zambia Cyber Security Agency (ZCSA) has urged members of the public to adopt safe online practices and report suspected cybercrimes, as investigations continue into the alleged murder of two young women of Kabwe by a 17-year-old boy in pursuit of wealth.

Speaking in a telephone interview with ZANIS in Lusaka today, ZCSA Research, Awareness and Education Director, Edgar Mlauzi, said the public should adopt the Stop, Think, Verify and Act (STVA) approach to protect themselves against cybercrime and online scams.

Mr Mlauzi further highlighted that suspected cybercrime incidents, including scam messages and fraudulent activities, should be reported to relevant authorities, while related messages and conversations should be preserved as evidence.

And, Mr Mlauzi indicated that the agency conducts awareness programmes beyond Cybersecurity Awareness Month of October, including sensitisation activities during the 16 Days of Gender Activism in November, to promote safer digital spaces.

He explained that during this awareness month, the agency planned to conduct radio programmes, visit shopping malls and engage schools and other institutions to educate the public on online safety.

“There is a need to partner with the media in disseminating cybersecurity information and educating the public on how to identify and respond to online threats,” said Mr Mlauzi.

He also encouraged young people to explore opportunities in cybersecurity and digital innovation through education, training and innovation programmes.

Mr Mlauzi further urged young people to engage in productive online activities, saying responsible use of digital platforms is essential to promoting a safer cyberspace and contributing to national digital development.

Meanwhile, Bishop of the Anglican Diocese of Central Zambia, Emmanuel Chikoya, said wealth creation requires hard and smart work, adding that alternative means of acquiring wealth are unsustainable and unacceptable.

“There should be zero tolerance towards individuals promoting such practices,” Reverend Chikoya said.

He urged members of the public to report such individuals to the relevant authorities and called for thorough investigations into the murder of the two young women to ensure that anyone suspected of influencing or facilitating the crime was held accountable.

Rev Chikoya also urged young people to develop their skills, establish businesses and find innovative ways of addressing community needs, saying creativity, invention and hard work are sustainable pathways to financial independence.

Psychologist, Darlington Mwendabai, said the 17-year-old boy could have been influenced by his family background, upbringing and environment, noting that parental absence, family conflicts and neglect could contribute to behavioural challenges among young people.

Mr Mwendabai noted that adolescents are still developing decision-making and impulse-control skills, making them vulnerable to peer pressure, manipulation, economic desperation and harmful beliefs that rituals could bring wealth.

He urged young people facing difficult circumstances to seek psychological support and confide in trusted people rather than resorting to harmful actions.

World.title: African leaders call for increased local value addition in mining sector
World.content:
African leaders have called for increased local value addition, faster implementation of mining policies and investment in the Lobito Corridor to create jobs and ensure Africa benefits more from its mineral resources.

Speaking during a plenary session at the Zambia mining and Investment Insaka in Lusaka, Zambia’s Acting Minister of Mines and Minerals Development, Gilbert Siame, said Africa must move from discussing mining reforms to implementing them.

Dr Siame noted that coordination with other countries on the Lobito Corridor will unlock opportunities for Zambia.

“We are intentional on making value addition an important aspect,” Dr Siame said.

He further stated that the government is also committed to promoting registered and legally compliant small scale mining.

Dr Siame added that small scale mining is an important part of the journey to meeting the three million metric tonnes of copper.

“We want organised, efficient and small-scale artisan mining that will contribute to meeting the target,” he said.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Minister of Mines, Louis Kabamba has called for the implementation of policies in the region.

Mr Kabamba said Africa has had enough talks and it is now time to implement the policies.

“We need action, enough said, talk is cheap, it’s time to implement,” he said.

He further noted Zambia has local manufacturing capabilities and called for collaboration with the DRC.

Meanwhile, Nigeria Ministry of Steel Development Director, Metallurgical Raw Materials Development and Investment Promotion, Ime Ekrikpo, has called on Africa to take control of its mineral wealth and benefit from it.

“Africa should take control of its mineral wealth instead of exporting raw materials and allowing other countries to capture most of the economic benefit,” Mr Ekrikpo said.

He added that to attain value addition, mining has to benefit the communities first.

“Mining has to benefit the communities first, because the moment the communities are made to understand their role and also benefit from it, value addition will be attained,” he said.

World.title: Gender Division, NGOCC track health, agriculture budgets
World.content:
The Gender Division, in collaboration with the Non-Governmental Gender Organisations Coordinating Council (NGOCC), is conducting a budget tracking exercise in the health and agriculture sectors in Chinsali and Isoka districts.

NGOCC Communications Lead Matthews Musokotwane explained that the budget tracking exercise will help to examine the allocation, release, utilisation and implementation of public resources to establish whether government expenditure is responding to community needs, particularly those of women, girls and other vulnerable groups.

Mr Musokotwane said the exercise will strengthen public accountability and promote evidence-based advocacy.

He said this when he, accompanied by other NGOCC officials, paid a courtesy call on Muchinga Province Permanent Secretary, Dr Tuesday Bwalya, at his office.

Mr Musokotwane said the exercise will involve consultations with relevant stakeholders, including District Health Office representatives, local government officials, health facility staff, district agriculture officers and beneficiaries.

He further said that stakeholders are expected to provide budgetary and expenditure information, share progress on implementation, highlight challenges affecting service delivery and identify opportunities for improving the utilisation of public resources.

Mr Musokotwane said the team will also visit selected projects and service delivery facilities to verify implementation progress, where applicable.

Meanwhile, Muchinga Province Permanent Secretary Tuesday Bwalya has urged stakeholders to use budget tracking findings to strengthen the inclusion of gender issues in government planning and resource allocation.

Dr Bwalya has encouraged NGOCC and other relevant stakeholders to raise gender-related concerns during the budget preparation process, noting that the current budget has already been consolidated ahead of its final presentation in Parliament.

“Bring up your tracking reports and show how the Province and the nation at large fared particularly on mainstreaming women’s issues into the national budget,” Dr Bwalya said.

Dr Bwalya said the exercise will help stakeholders assess whether budget allocations are gender sensitive by examining issues such as recruitment, the representation of women and men, and funding for training and skills upgrading.

He said such assessments will help establish whether public expenditure is responding fairly to the different needs of vulnerable women, girls and men.

While in the district, the team is expected to visit the One-Stop Centre and Chief Nkula’s One Stop centre to appreciate their operations.

World.title: Phase 2 Urea plant to boost local fertiliser production – President Hichilema
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema today officiated at a groundbreaking ceremony for the construction of United Capital Fertilizer (UCF) $1.6 billion Urea Plant Phase 2 project, describing the investment as a major milestone in Zambia’s quest for industrialisation, food security and job creation.

The President said the plant will significantly boost local fertiliser production, reduce dependence on imports and lower the cost of inputs for farmers.

President Hichilema commended UCF and its partners for their additional investment in the production of urea, ammonia and ammonium nitrate at the 2,000-hectare site in Chilanga which he said was once full of rocks but is now a city on its own.

“This is a clear demonstration of what a serious investment can do to turn around a place defined as a rocky plant, but now an industrial site. Congratulations to UCF,” President Hichilema said.

The Head of State also commended the company for its continued confidence in Zambia, saying his administration will continue to market Zambia ferociously and aggressively as an investment destination.

He disclosed that UCF has pledged to invest up to $5 billion by 2030 and has already invested heavily, expressing optimism that the target will be achieved even before 2030.

President Hichilema singled out the company’s wastewater recycling system as exemplary, noting that raw water is extracted from underground, used, treated and reused, a practice he said other industries must emulate under climate change.

The President also called for accelerated investment in the chemical industry, noting that coal from Maamba is now being used to produce explosives for mining and other industrial uses.

“What we have seen around here tells us that coal can produce us white stuff that will lead to production of explosives. This is value addition,” he said.

The President said the project is a Zambian company employing Zambians, with a target of 10,000 direct jobs and thousands more indirect jobs for transporters, dealers and traders.

“This is a Zambian company employing Zambians directly and indirectly. 10,000 families multiplied by eight is 80,000 plus people feeding every day because a family member works here,” he said.

President Hichilema said the investment is key to the country’s food security agenda and the target of producing 10 million tonnes of maize, noting that UCF is providing quality, correctly weighed 50kg fertilizer tailored to soil types.

He said the development aligns with Government’s mantra of economic growth through investment and trade and other things will fall in place, adding that there are no shortcuts to development.

The President also conveyed gratitude to Chinese President Xi Jinping for the comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership between Zambia and China, which he said is delivering mutual benefits.

He urged Zambians to support and protect investments, stating that increased local production will reduce dependence on imports and position Zambia as a producer, processor and trader for the region.

Chinese Ambassador to Zambia, Han Jing, said the groundbreaking is tangible proof of commitments taking root and grand visions transforming into a growing industry.

Ambassador Jing extended gratitude to President Hichilema for honouring the ceremony twice in a year first for the launch of trial production of Phase 1 and now Phase 2, saying his presence gives the strongest endorsement to China-Zambia practical cooperation.

He said the industrial park where the ceremony was held represents a total investment of over $3 billion and in just 5 years has grown into a comprehensive manufacturing hub producing compound fertilizers, ammonia and urea, integrating energy supply and logistics, and providing over 10,000 jobs.

The Ambassador said Phase 2 will drive coordinated growth across upstream and downstream sectors, foster local SMEs, strengthen industrial supply chains and significantly reduce import dependence, conserve foreign exchange and strengthen national food security.

He said Zambia is now actively strengthening its competitiveness in fertilizer, energy and logistics while Chinese enterprises provide capital, technology and expertise, noting that the two countries’ strengths complement each other perfectly.

Ambassador Han said President Hichilema’s reelection has greatly strengthened confidence among international investors and disclosed that President Xi Jinping has extended warm congratulations, with both Heads of State reaffirming commitment to deepen cooperation.

World.title: Mining expert calls for deliberate government sector policies and  targeted financing
World.content:
Mining Expert, Norman Mbazima, has called for deliberate government policies and targeted financing to accelerate mineral processing and manufacturing in Zambia and across Africa.

Mr Mbazima says African countries must intentionally develop downstream industries by investing in electricity, technology, infrastructure and financing mechanisms that support local mineral processing and manufacturing.

He was speaking today during a panel discussion on the sidelines of the 2026 Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka (ZAMII) being held in Lusaka, under the theme: Transforming Africa’s Mining Landscape: Regional Value Chains, Shared Prosperity and Empowering Communities.

Mr Mbazima cited Japan, South Korea and China as countries that had successfully established smelting and refining industries despite having limited mineral resources, through deliberate government support and investment.

“African countries should adopt similar strategies to ensure more minerals are processed locally instead of being transported over long distances for refining elsewhere,” he added.

Mr Mbazima stressed that developing industries beyond mineral extraction requires governments to identify potential investment barriers and implement measures to address them.

And, Mining Consultant, David Ng’andu, called for increased access to foreign investment and international capital markets to finance mineral exploration and mine development in Zambia.

Mr Ng’andu pointed out that Zambia needs to strengthen pathways through which local mining companies, particularly junior explorers, can access international financing to reduce the financial barriers associated with mineral exploration.

He cited the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Peru as examples of countries that have significantly increased copper production through foreign direct investment (FDI) and international mining partnerships.

Mr Ng’andu said improving access to international capital markets and strengthening investor confidence could help Zambia unlock its mineral potential and increase copper production.

Meanwhile, Botswana’s Presidential Projects Advisor, Jerry Chitube, has urged Zambia to use public resources strategically to attract private investment in the mining sector without exposing government to excessive financial risks.

“Government participation should focus on creating an enabling environment for investment rather than using public funds to absorb risks that should be borne by private investors,” he added.

Mr Chitube explained that government should prioritise geological studies and other project preparation activities that improve the bankability of mining projects and attract investors.

“Institutions such as the Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) could consider carefully structured minority equity investments alongside Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) to support viable mining projects,” he added.

Mr Chitube also called for a more disciplined approach to government guarantees, saying these should be partial, appropriately priced, time-bound and restricted to clearly identified risks.

He further said fiscal incentives should be linked to actual investments in mineral exploration, processing and manufacturing rather than blanket tax holidays that may not deliver meaningful economic benefits.

Ghanaian Chief Technical and Operations Officer for Mineral Income and Investment Fund, Kwabena Barning, also called on Zambia to adopt innovative financing models and long-term investment strategies to unlock the full potential of its mining industry.

Mr Barning said Zambia should explore alternative financing mechanisms, including royalty streaming, staged project financing and equity markets, to support mining projects from exploration through to production.

“Despite Zambia’s established position as a mining jurisdiction, relatively few mining companies were listed on the local stock exchange or accessed innovative financing arrangements,” he added.

He said Zambia should consider financing models that allow mining companies to secure funding in stages, beginning with exploration and progressing to advanced exploration before accessing debt financing when projects become bankable.

Meanwhile, United States Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) Representative, Sonja Horgen, said innovative financing structures and project preparation support is key to attracting investment into Zambia’s critical minerals sector.

Ms Morgan said such interventions help reduce investment risks and increase the appetite of banks and other financial institutions to finance projects.

“USTDA works with various financial institutions and development partners, including the United States International Development Finance Corporation, the World Bank and the African Development Bank, to facilitate long-term financing opportunities,” she said.

She said financing options could also include public-private partnerships (PPPs), offtake agreements and blended finance arrangements to support infrastructure development and critical minerals projects.

Ms Morgan said the agency remains open to different financing models, depending on the needs and requirements of individual projects.

World.title: Chisamba Magistrate set judgment date for defilement case
World.content:
The Chisamba Magistrates’ Court has set October 30, 2026, for judgement in a case in which a 28-year-old man is accused of defiling an 11-year-old girl.

Resident Magistrate, Susan Magalashi, set the date after the defence concluded its case, with the accused maintaining his innocence.

Cornwell Nchimunya, of Chawama Compound in Chisamba is charged with one count of defilement, contrary to Section 138 (1) of the Penal Code.

It is alleged that between 2025 and July 18, 2026, on an unknown date in Chisamba, Nchimunya had unlawful carnal knowledge of a girl under the age of 16.

In his defence, Nchimunya told the court that he was surprised when police officers apprehended him on July 24, 2026, while he was working at Lupapula’s Farm, where he was employed as a general worker.

He explained that he had been sent to collect a pig from Mr Sakala’s farm in the Mutoyo area and he was returning to his workplace when the incident happened.

“On 24 July, 2026, I was sent to pick a pig at Mr Sakala’s farm in the Mutoyo area. On my way back closer to the farm, I called Mr Kapapula to find out if there was a piggery where I could put the pig. I could hear some voices in the background but I didn’t know that it was the police,” he said.

Nchimunya told the court that an approaching police stopped and the officers informed him that they were looking for him.

“I was coming from the piggery towards my workplace when I saw a police vehicle parked. Later it started moving towards my direction and stopped after reaching where I was and the officers said they were looking for me,” he explained.

He also recalled that his workmate, Costa Sikabondo, once told him that a girl in the neighbourhood had been defiled, but did not identify the victim or the person responsible.

Sikabondo, 25, who testified as a defence witness, told the court that he only learnt about the case after Nchimunya had been taken into custody.

Meanwhile, a Clinical Officer, Derris Chiyesu, who testified at the request of the accused, identified the medical report he had signed and said his findings supported the allegation that the girl had been sexually abused, noting that her hymen was perforated.

Earlier, four prosecution witnesses, including the victim, testified and identified Nchimunya in court, while a signed medical report and an affidavit were also presented as evidence.

The court heard from the victim that the alleged abuse first occurred in a poultry house and on another occasion at the home of the accused’s relative.

Magistrate Magalashi adjourned the matter to October 30, 2026, for judgement, with Nchimunya remaining in custody.

World.title: Isoka Council urges youths to utilize skills training
World.content:
Isoka Town Council has urged youths in the area to take an active role in national development by utilizing government-supported skills training programmes to create employment and contribute to community growth.

Council Chairperson, Bright Siame, said the call is in line with Zambia’s 62nd Independence Anniversary theme; which highlights the country’s development journey and the importance of building a sustainable future through the participation of all citizens.

Mr Siame said youths have a critical role to play in shaping the country’s future and should take advantage of government initiatives, particularly skills bursaries, to acquire practical skills and venture into entrepreneurship.

Mr Siame said it was concerning that some beneficiaries abandoned their training before completion, resulting in the wastage of public resources invested in their education.

“It is actually disheartening that some youths are running away from skills. When somebody is enrolled at an institution, you find that maybe up to half of the training period of youth disappears, and the government will continue pumping in money for the same youth,” Mr Siame said.

He urged young people to apply the knowledge and skills acquired through training to productive activities that would benefit their communities and contribute to the country’s development.

Mr Siame said the Independence Anniversary theme should inspire youths to recognize their responsibility in sustaining Zambia’s progress by becoming proactive citizens who identify opportunities to improve their communities.

He said young people should move away from unproductive activities and instead focus on initiatives that promote self-reliance, entrepreneurship and national development.

Mr Siame further encouraged youths to take advantage of opportunities for representation in decision-making structures, including Parliament and local councils, to articulate issues affecting their peers.

He said the inclusion of youths through proportional representation provided an opportunity for young people to participate in governance and influence decisions that shape their future.

Mr Siame said Zambia’s future depended on a generation of responsible, innovative and development-oriented youths who would sustain the gains made since independence.

He appealed to young people in Isoka, in particular, to take ownership of the district’s development by making productive use of available government support and actively participating in community initiatives.

The 2026 Independence Anniversary will be held under the theme: “Zambia @62: Our Journey, Our Growth, Our Future,”

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 21, 2026
World.content:
Nigeria Confirms First Ebola Case as Outbreak Spreads

Nigeria has confirmed one case of Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) after a woman who recently travelled from Uganda tested positive. The patient is in isolation and receiving treatment at a private hospital. The authorities have begun tracing 44 people identified as contacts of the patient. The government has called on health facilities to step up surveillance, isolate suspected cases and implement infection prevention measures. It also advised the public to maintain good hand hygiene and avoid contact with bodily fluids from suspected cases. Nigeria has become the latest country to report an Ebola case as the virus spreads across the region. Kenya has recorded nine infections. Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases, but it later declared itself free of the virus.



UN Warns Pulling Peacekeepers From CAR Will Fuel Regional Chaos

The United Nations has warned against a premature withdrawal of peacekeepers from the Central African Republic (CAR) as Sudan's war fuels instability along the country's eastern borders. UN Special Representative Valentine Rugwabiza told the Security Council that an attack on Am-Dafock on June 30 killed civilians and security personnel, displaced 17,000 people and injured six UN peacekeepers. She said the rapid response by the UN peacekeeping mission, MINUSCA, helped restore state authority and prevent further casualties. Between June and September, suspected Lord's Resistance Army fighters were linked to 26 serious incidents in the southeast, including sexual violence and the abduction of 68 civilians, about 40 of them children. Despite progress in disarming 1,907 fighters since July 2025 and establishing municipal councils in 127 of 177 municipalities, large areas remain unstable. Nearly two million people faced acute food insecurity between April and August, while the UN humanitarian plan was less than half funded. As the Security Council considers renewing MINUSCA's mandate, members remain divided over troop reductions, with the UN Secretary-General recommending a one-year extension that preserves the mission's capacity to respond rapidly to violence.

15 Years After Gaddafi's Fall, His Legacy Still Haunts Libya and the Sahel

Fifteen years after Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi was captured and killed in 2011, his political legacy continues to influence debates about Libya's instability and security across the Sahel. Libya specialist Virginie Collombier says Kadhafism combined the Green Book's proposed alternative to capitalism and communism with centralised rule, Arab and African nationalism, anti-imperialism and the redistribution of oil wealth. However, the regime was also marked by severe repression, restrictions on political opposition and policies that alienated sections of the population. Kadhafi's overthrow, following an uprising and Western-backed military intervention, left Libya divided between rival political and military factions, with insecurity spreading across the region. Some African leaders and political elites remain nostalgic for his investment and support for African development, while criticising foreign powers for removing him without a clear plan for the country's future. The assassination of his son Saif al-Islam in February 2026 has further weakened the movement, leaving supporters without a prominent leader or a clear political project. Collombier argues that Kadhafi's legacy reflects both his personalised rule and Libya's complex history.

South African Woman Dies in Shark Attack Off Eastern Cape Coast

A 65-year-old South African woman, Janine Lochrenberg, has died following a shark attack while swimming off Orient Beach in KuGompo City, formerly East London. Lochrenberg was swimming with her local open-water swimming club at about 08:00 when she was bitten on her thigh and upper arm. Fellow swimmers brought her towards shore, but she is believed to have died before reaching it. Her sister, Margot, said Lochrenberg had a deep love of the ocean despite being aware of the elevated shark presence in the area. Her partner, Barbara Briceland, described her as an experienced swimmer who regularly ventured into the breakers. The retired medical physicist was reportedly wearing a magnetic shark-repellent band when the attack occurred. Authorities have closed Orient Beach and another nearby beach following the incident. According to the Florida Museum's International Shark Attack File, fatal shark attacks in South Africa are rare, with about 10 recorded since 2012.

Morocco's First Female Prime Minister Faces Test on Women's Rights

Morocco's appointment of Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as its first female prime minister has been welcomed as a historic milestone but has also reignited debate over women's leadership and gender equality in the Muslim-majority country. Former justice minister Mustafa Ramid questioned whether a woman should lead the government, citing a religious saying that countries led by women will not succeed. Many younger Moroccans welcomed El Mansouri's appointment. However, conservative views remain influential, particularly on inheritance, polygamy, marriage and divorce. Women's rights advocates say reform of the country's family code, known as the Moudawana, will be a key test of whether the new government can deliver meaningful change. Education is another concern, with official figures showing that only 55% of girls aged 15 to 17 in rural areas attended school in 2025, compared with 100% in urban areas. However, analysts said that El Mansouri's ability to drive reform is constrained by the king's extensive powers and the influence of religious authorities. But critics also question whether her appointment is a true step forward, or simply an attempt to bolster the monarchy's image at a time of low voter turnout. Advocates argue that her record in office, rather than her gender alone, will determine whether the appointment translates into lasting improvements for Moroccan women.

World.title: South Africa: Madlanga Commission Weighs In-Camera Hearing Request - South African News Briefs - October 21, 2026
World.content:
press review

Madlanga Commission to Hear Arguments on Secret Testimony

The Madlanga Commission will resume from recess to hear arguments on an application for National Intelligence Coordinating Committee head Dr Ntandazo Sifolo to testify in camera, reports EWN. Evidence leaders want Sifolo to present classified information about the committee's internal operations, accountability and current and future threat assessments, which would be declassified for the commission's viewing but withheld from the public. Media organisations, including amaBhungane Centre for Investigative Journalism, Daily Maverick and Media24, oppose the application, arguing that intelligence structures are matters of significant public interest and that closed-door proceedings could undermine the commission's public accountability mandate.

Alleged Triple Murder Suspect Ndodana Tshuma Returns to Court



Zimbabwean national Ndodana Tshuma is set to appear at the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court in connection with the alleged murders of his wife, Zandile, and their two daughters, Natalie and Nala, in the United Kingdom, reports SABC News. Tshuma was arrested in Kensington, Johannesburg, in July during a joint operation involving the South African Police Service and Interpol after an international red notice was issued for him. He has pleaded guilty to firearm and immigration-related charges in South Africa. The court previously postponed the case to allow the state and defence to finalise a plea and sentencing agreement and resolve documentation discrepancies. He remains in custody without bail as the UK murder case proceeds.

Prosecutors Consider Further Arrests in Shadrack Sibiya Rape Case

The National Prosecuting Authority has not ruled out further arrests in the case involving former Deputy National Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya, who remains in custody at Kgosi Mampuru Prison after being denied bail by the Randburg Magistrate’s Court, reports EWN. Sibiya is accused of sexually grooming a minor and raping an 18-year-old woman. NPA spokesperson Kaizer Kganyago said prosecutors would decide whether to pursue charges against alleged accomplices, adding that further arrests were possible if additional investigations uncovered evidence against other individuals.
