World.title: Colombia’s Congress approves De la Espriella’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia’s Congress agreed to increase the government’s 2027 budget despite promises by President Abelardo de la Espriella to reduce public spending.

Next year’s budget will be COP634.9 trillion, almost $204 billion, which is 16% more than last year’s budget and 10% higher than the proposal made by former President Gustavo Petro.

According to Finance Minister Miguel Gomez, the budget seeks to bring the State’s finances in line with reality.

The budget was approved in both the Senate and the House of Representatives with the support of De la Espriella’s government coalition.

The Historic Pact, the only leftist opposition party, rejected the budget and boycotted the vote.

On behalf of the national government, I would like to thank you all for your work over the past few months in passing the budget. I would also like to thank the opposition for the strength with which they defended their views. The message that Congress has sent today regarding the government’s economic policy is very important. It is the first step toward putting the country’s economy back on track toward growth, fiscal responsibility, and addressing the nation’s needs. Finance Minister Miguel Gomez

The budget seeks to reimpose the neoliberal model that had been abandoned by Petro and reduce public debt.

According to Green Party representative Jaime Raul Salamanca, who opposed the budget, funding for free higher education was cut in half from COP800 billion ($254 million) to COP400 billion (127 million).

“This cut raises concerns about its potential impact on the continuity and scope of this policy, which has enabled thousands of young people to enroll in public institutions of higher education,” said Salamanca.

The budget also cut the budget for the war crimes tribunal JEP, which could endanger the future of the peace process with the FARC and is opposed by the government.

World.title: De la Espriella announces “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism”
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella announced an “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism” as part of his “cultural counterrevolution.”

During a visit to the Culture Ministry, De la Espriella described wokeism as “an ideological paradigm that aims to transform moral, cultural, and social foundations in the West, perverting values, family tradition, and national identity.”

According to the president, Culture Minister Paola Holguin was a general in the “cultural counterrevolution.”

Culture has an enormous capacity to shape society, and that is why the State has a moral, inescapable, and political duty to prevent cultural spaces from being taken over by social communism, which is atheist and an enemy to the fundamental values upon which the nation of Colombia is built. This is where that cultural counterrevolution will begin. President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella said that Holguin, the daughter of a reported money launderer, would lead the “Culture War” against the “extreme left,” which has “permeated all parts of society, particularly the cultural and academic spheres.”

I want to be clear about this: we are going to wage an open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism, which is nothing more than an ideological movement that aims to transform the moral, cultural, and social foundations of the West, corrupting values, family tradition, and national identity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Earlier in the day, the National Museum removed all references to members of the exterminated Patriotic Union party, slain guerrilla leader and presidential candidate Carlos Pizarro, and the struggle for the rights of Colombia’s LGBT+ community.

References to Colombia’s former guerrilla movements was “terrorism apology, which is “exactly what we have come to confront” in an attempt to “recover pride for Colombian culture.”

Atheists, the Pizarro family and gay rights activists rejected the president’s attempts to remove them from mainstream culture.

World.title: Colombia’s first lady promises transparency over earthquake donations
World.content:
Colombia’s first lady, Ana Lucia Pineda, vowed to reveal how much money she collected and spent in response to the August 10 earthquake that affected hundreds of thousands of people.

Amid mounting public pressure about where the money had gone, Pineda went on the morning program of public television channel Nuestro Caribe to promise that her foundation, Luz y Sonrisas, will take its finances public on Friday.

Carrying a white folder, the wife of President Abelardo de la Espriella stressed that “in the foundation’s accounts rest all, absolutely all of the monies from the donations we received during the ‘Colombia One Single Heart’ campaign” that was announced on August 12.

“A lie is not going to tear down the truth of who I am or what I represent, or how my children recognize me,” said Pineda.

Luz y Sonrisas was one of three NGO’s that were promoted by the De la Espriella government to collect contributions for victims of the earthquake.

Pineda’s foundation was the only one that could receive contributions from abroad.

Earlier in the week, news program Noticias Uno revealed that her foundation that was founded on July 7 lacked the tax exemption that would allow it to accept donations, a process that usually takes months.

In a press statement, tax office DIAN subsequently said that it had granted the tax exemption to the first lady and that she could legally accept financial contributions.

Pineda did not say how much money she had received, but said that she stopped supporting the initial relief efforts “because the humanitarian aid was sufficient, it was huge.”

The first lady vowed she had saved the donations for the reconstruction phase “because I have also taken the initiative to build and return to the victims a house that is durable for the families who lost everything.”

World.title: Colombia’s opposition takes to the street to protest De la Espriella
World.content:
Despite intimidation attempts by the national government and the police, tens of thousands of people took to the streets throughout Colombia to protest the far-right government of President Abelardo De la Espriella.

The protest had been organized by social organizations, labor unions and the country’s largest opposition party, the Historic Pact.

Opposition leader Ivan Cepeda, who joined the protests in Bogota, told a reporter that the government is “exercising a mafia-style rule in the service of the worst elements of Colombian politics—the drug trade.”

Contrary to what De la Espriella is saying, this is not a government that opposes drug trafficking; it is a government that supports the drug trafficking cartels, the paramilitaries, and the ultra-conservative forces that want to destroy people’s rights, the democratic advances made by President Gustavo Petro, and the progress achieved by the popular movement over the past four years. Senator Ivan Cepeda

“That’s why we’re here; we won’t allow people’s rights to be violated or trampled upon,” said the senator.

Hours ahead of the protest, the president signed off on a decree that changed the police response to protests and accused the organizers of being “instigators of evil” who “seek to once again cause chaos.”

Human rights organizations denounced that the security forces put snipers on the roofs of buildings in Bogota and in Cali, a helicopter flew over the heads of the protesters.

The protests sought to test the waters for an even larger “national strike” that is set for November and shut down parts of the country in 2021.

“We are only warming up,” warned Cepeda, who has yet to recognize De la Espriella as Colombia’s legitimate president after losing the elections in July.

World.title: Colombia’s national strike organizers “are instigators of evil,” claims De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella called labor unions and social organizations who organized anti-government protests for Wednesday “instigators of evil” who “seek to once again cause chaos.”

In an address to the nation, De la Espriella stressed that the security forces were instructed to allow peaceful protests, but warned the protesters that “if they intend to set Colombia ablaze, they will face the determination of the tiger and his government to do what is lawfully required—which is to defend the lives, honor, and property of all Colombians.”

Wednesday’s protests are a preparation for a national strike that is set to take place in November and is supported by the country’s political opposition to the far-right government.

According to the president, “those who are promoting the strike and seeking to use it to once again cause chaos and destabilize the government are the very same people who left the country bankrupt, on the brink of a blackout, with the healthcare system in intensive care, energy sovereignty compromised, and public resources plundered and looted.”

“They are instigators of evil, not fighter for freedom,” said De la Espriella.

If they intend to set Colombia ablaze, they will face the determination of the tiger and his government to do what is rightfully required—which is to defend the lives, honor, and property of all Colombians. President Abelardo de la Espriella

The president stressed that he would be signing a decree that regulates public protests in an attempt to avoid the chaos that erupted during massive strikes in 2019 and 2021 an killed 80 people.

De la Espriella additionally is expected to present an “anti-terrorism stature” to Congress, which could see the prosecution of protest organizers on terrorism charges, according to opposition leaders and security experts.

World.title: Colombia declares official start of El Niño, warns of strong impacts
World.content:
Colombia’s meteorological institute IDEAM officially declared the arrival of El Niño, and warned that the climate phenomenon could trigger water shortages and forest fires.

In a press statement, the IDEAM said that its “confirmation reflects the sustained warm conditions in the Pacific Ocean, which, according to the latest measurement, broke records, reaching a sea surface temperature anomaly of +3.49°C.”

The meteorological institute said it expected that this year’s “Godzilla El Niño” could continue to disrupt local climate patterns until March next year.

Initially, the weather phenomenon is expected to reduce rainfall between October and December, which is normally the rainy season in large parts of the country.

“Given this situation, and in light of the alerts issued since the beginning of the year, the national government launched an interagency response,.. with specific instructions for the responsible agencies to have their contingency plans formulated and activated by November 30 at the latest,” said the President’s Office in a statement.

The National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) coordinates response capabilities across the country and enhances the monitoring of wildfires using satellite technology. For its part, the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development is taking steps to protect strategic ecosystems, water sources, and the most vulnerable areas. President’s Office

The Mining Ministry “is implementing an emergency plan aimed at ensuring the country’s energy security by strengthening thermal power generation, securing fuel supplies, and implementing efficiency and conservation measures,” according to the President’s Office.

EPM, the local utilities firm in Medellin, has been testing the effectiveness of water rations as they fear the lack of rain could affect the hydro-electric power plants that provide the northwest of Colombia much of its energy.

Before leaving office on August 7, former President Gustavo Petro ordered the mass purchase of solar panels to reduce the pressure on the electric grid.

World.title: Colombia’s draft counterterrorist statute “creates foundations of dictatorial and inquisitorial regime:” opposition
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella’s antiterrorist statute would criminalize political opposition, social movements, and social protest, and essentially form a dictatorial regime, said opposition leader Ivan Cepeda on Wednesday.

In a video, Cepeda said that the true purpose of the bill that was leaked earlier seeks “to advance in the formation of essentially a dictatorial regime,.. which, moreover, has such a regime prostrate to drug trafficking.”

“The true objectives of this statute are to wage a crusade against the political opposition, social movements, and social protest, which is a legitimate right of citizens,” said the Senator of the Historic Pact party.

“Most of the articles in this draft are devoted to provisions that seriously undermine civil liberties, human rights, and the right to protest—not to illegal armed groups,’ according to Cepeda.

The broad legal definition of the word terrorism would allow the government to prosecute protest organizers on terrorism charges if any clashes occur between protesters and police.

This law could serve to intensify the persecution already underway in Colombia against journalists, judges, students, teachers, union members, peasants, indigenous people, people of African descent, LGBTIQ+ individuals—in short, any person or group that criticizes the citizen Abelardo de la Espriella, his government, law enforcement, or any state institution. Such a person could be taken to prison—without even prior warning—and subjected to abuse and torture. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Furthermore, the creation of a National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors would allow the government to criminalize citizens based on an administrative rather than a legal basis, and “grants extraordinary powers to the president to regulate a statutory judicial procedure, specifically the expedited preventive detention proceeding,” said the opposition leader.

The aim is to criminalize social protest; the alleged crime of “manipulating the civilian population” punishes anyone who promotes, finances, organizes, or leads crowds—this is the language of the draft statute—and this is nothing less than the institutionalization of political persecution and the criminalization of free speech. Senator Ivan Cepeda

The antiterrorism statute will be facing opposition when the government tries to push the legislation through Congress, Cepeda said.

“The Historic Pact rejects this and will do whatever is necessary to ensure that the opposition’s rights and guarantees are respected,” said the opposition leader.

World.title: De la Espriella announces first $309M in aid for earthquake reconstruction
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella announced that his Miracle Fund received COP1 trillion ($309 million) for the reconstruction of western Colombia, which was hit by a 7.4M earthquake on August 10.

The announcement followed announcements by the press, which reported that the Finance Ministry allocated ($192 million) COP625 billion to the fund almost two months after the disaster.

Thank you for your patience, but please understand that the government’s bureaucratic inertia and the situation we’ve inherited are extremely complex. However, we’re working to resolve the issue, and the Milagro Fund is now up and running, thanks to God and the efforts of all the officials in this administration. President Abelardo de la Espriella

“In November, the government will move forward with contracting another COP2.7 trillion ($835 million),” Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo told Caracol Radio.

The money is the first of an estimated COP30 trillion ($9.3 billion) that would be needed to rebuild the damage to airports, roads, hospitals and other public works.

The fund will be managed by De la Espriella’s general secretary, Carlos Rios, and a handful of businessmen with ties to the administration.

The announcement followed increased unrest about the government’s lack of response to the earthquake, which affected more than 400,000 people in the Valle del Cauca and Choco province, and the coffee region.

The government’s initial response was delayed because De la Espriella suspended the process to transfer power a month before he took office on August 7.

World.title: Argentina and the UK to face off in Hamburg on November 10 over Falklands oil
World.content:
Argentina and the UK to face off in Hamburg on November 10 over Falklands oil

21st Wednesday, October 2026 - 01:46 UTC Full article

Argentina submitted its request on October 13, pending the constitution of the arbitral tribunal under Annex VII of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea will hold hearings on November 10 and 11 on Argentina’s request for an order requiring the United Kingdom to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands. The dates were set by the tribunal’s president, Judge Maurice K. Kamga, in an order dated October 20.

The case, officially named the Case concerning hydrocarbon exploitation in the South-West Atlantic Ocean (Argentina v. United Kingdom), will be heard in the main courtroom of the Hamburg-based tribunal. The hearing will be public and broadcast live on its website, where verbatim records will later be published. The detailed schedule of sittings will be announced later.

Argentina submitted its request on October 13, pending the constitution of the arbitral tribunal under Annex VII of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. It seeks four provisional measures, including that the United Kingdom prevent the commencement or continuation of hydrocarbon exploitation through Sea Lion and refrain from granting new permits. To prescribe them, the tribunal must consider that the arbitral tribunal would have prima facie jurisdiction over the dispute and that the situation is urgent.

The United Kingdom has said it will take part in the proceedings, challenge any attempt to use them to settle sovereignty over the archipelago and regard any provisional measures prescribed as binding. Sea Lion, operated by Navitas Petroleum and Rockhopper Exploration, expects first oil in 2028.

World.title: A Russian satellite shadows a US one for days in an unprecedented manoeuvre
World.content:
A Russian satellite shadows a US one for days in an unprecedented manoeuvre

20th Tuesday, October 2026 - 16:10 UTC Full article

The Russian craft carried out “a series of deliberate manoeuvres” around Iceye-X36 between October 15 and 19, alternating between positions ahead of and behind it

A Russian military satellite, Kosmos-2612, manoeuvred for several days at close range to a commercial satellite operated by a US company that supplies images to Ukraine, coming within less than five kilometres, in what space-tracking specialists describe as an unprecedented approach between active satellites belonging to different owners.

According to orbital tracking company LeoLabs, the Russian craft carried out “a series of deliberate manoeuvres” around Iceye-X36 between October 15 and 19, at an altitude of about 540 kilometres, alternating between positions ahead of and behind it. It came within five kilometres on October 16 and then withdrew in a controlled manner; it is now more than 100 kilometres away. LeoLabs says it had never before observed a deliberate approach of this kind sustained over several days.

Short time-lapse of part of this morning’s first pass of ICEYE-X36 (59103) and COSMOS 2612 (68762) over South America under partly cloudy skies. https://t.co/t8RhwmKcV4 — s2a systems (@s2a_systems) October 18, 2026

“This looks like an unprecedented step by Russia, if correct,” wrote astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell, a specialist in tracking space activity, for whom it would be the first known encounter in low Earth orbit between two active satellites without the consent of one of their operators. The head of Germany’s Space Command, Michael Traut, said the Russian satellite was “chasing” the US one and warned that such manoeuvres force satellites to adjust their orbits, consuming fuel and shortening their working lives.

Iceye-X36 belongs to the US subsidiary of Finnish company Iceye, which builds radar satellites capable of imaging at night or through cloud and has worked with Ukraine since 2022. “We are aware of the situation and are monitoring it closely,” the company said. Russia has not explained the mission of Kosmos-2612, launched in April with three other satellites that, according to the US Space Force, approached a Western spacecraft in May.

The episode comes a month after US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink acknowledged that the United States has “space control weapons in orbit”. The 1967 Outer Space Treaty prohibits placing weapons of mass destruction in orbit but not conventional weapons.

World.title: Milei calls Lula a “leftist thief” and says he hopes he will not “steal” Brazil’s election
World.content:
Milei calls Lula a “leftist thief” and says he hopes he will not “steal” Brazil’s election

20th Tuesday, October 2026 - 15:29 UTC Full article

It is not the first time Milei has called Lula a “thief”. On October 7 he posted an image of the Brazilian president with that word on Instagram

Argentine President Javier Milei attacked his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva again on Tuesday, accusing him of a “dirty campaign” and saying he hoped Lula would not try to “steal” Sunday’s presidential runoff, in which he faces Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, whom Milei has publicly backed.

“Progressive male chauvinists… Then they go around accusing all their opponents of misogyny… The mask is slipping on these criminals… I hope his latest dirty campaign trick doesn’t include stealing the election… Leftist thief,” Milei wrote on X. The message was accompanied by a clip from a television interview in which Lula defended the shorter working week, approved last week by the Senate, arguing that “a woman cannot work six days a week and rest one, because on that day she has to clean the house”.

It is not the first time Milei has called Lula a “thief”. On October 7 he posted an image of the Brazilian president with that word on Instagram, and in July he called him a “jailbird” and a “thief”, prompting Brazil to recall its ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations, according to the EFE news agency. Lula was convicted of corruption in the Lava Jato investigation and spent 580 days in prison, but the Supreme Federal Court annulled his convictions in 2021, restoring his political rights. The Brazilian government had not commented on the new message.

On Sunday, in the first runoff debate, Lula asked Bolsonaro whether he intends to apply “Milei’s chainsaw” to cut public spending. Bolsonaro won the first round with 47.03% of the vote against Lula’s 45.16%, and polls show a statistical tie.

Brazil is Argentina’s main trading partner, and the two countries are Mercosur’s largest economies.

World.title: Meta races the clock to prove to Brazil’s electoral court it treats Lula and Bolsonaro equally
World.content:
Meta races the clock to prove to Brazil’s electoral court it treats Lula and Bolsonaro equally

20th Tuesday, October 2026 - 10:09 UTC Full article

The company unilaterally extended the 72-hour deadline it had been given to five days, cited “technical difficulties”, submitted untranslated reports in English and provided out-of-context documents

The 24-hour deadline given by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court to Meta to show that its algorithms and artificial intelligence treat President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro equally expires on Tuesday, five days before the runoff. If the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp fails to show compliance, the daily fine will double from 500,000 to one million reais.

Judge Marco Aurélio Bellizze issued the order on Sunday, as the candidates held their first debate, after deeming unsatisfactory Meta’s response to an earlier ruling, which the full court upheld unanimously on Friday. According to the judge, the company unilaterally extended the 72-hour deadline it had been given to five days, cited “technical difficulties”, submitted untranslated reports in English and provided out-of-context documents. He now requires detailed reports in Portuguese and that, by Wednesday at the latest, Meta restore advertising paid for by Lula’s campaign that was not delivered, or state that none is pending.

The order, in force until the October 25 vote, bars Meta from unequally reducing the reach of candidates’ posts, limiting recommendations or restricting search results in favour of either. It stems from a complaint by Lula’s campaign, which says the reach of his profiles was reduced and that Meta’s artificial intelligence tool refused to generate images supporting the president while doing so for his rival. Bolsonaro’s campaign has also gone to the court, saying Meta allowed negative ads against the senator and the circulation of AI-made Lula campaign material without the mandatory label. The judge admitted it to the case.

Meta regretted the ruling and said it “complies with Brazilian electoral rules”. “We will share with the court additional information on technical aspects that may not have been fully considered in its decision,” a spokeswoman said. The company had warned that some requirements, such as prior human review of ads, would force it to suspend all political advertising.

Polls show a statistical tie between the two candidates, who will debate again on Friday on TV Globo.

World.title: Argentina awaits the Supreme Court after the YPF case is closed at first instance
World.content:
Argentina awaits the Supreme Court after the YPF case is closed at first instance

20th Tuesday, October 2026 - 09:52 UTC Full article

Preska’s judgment, which exceeded US$18 billion with interest, was the largest ever imposed on a state by a US court

New York federal judge Loretta Preska has vacated her 2023 judgment ordering Argentina to pay more than US$16 billion over the expropriation of oil company YPF and formally closed the case at first instance. Its future now depends on whether the US Supreme Court agrees to review it, as litigation funder Burford Capital requested in early October.

Preska’s order incorporates the ruling by the Second Circuit Court of Appeals, which overturned the judgment on March 27. Sources at Argentina’s Treasury Attorney’s Office told the newspaper Infobae that it was a “merely procedural” step the government had expected. In their decision, judges Denny Chin and Beth Robinson, with José Cabranes dissenting, held that Argentine expropriation law precludes claims such as the plaintiffs’ and that a company’s bylaws do not constitute a contract giving rise to such damages. They also vacated the order requiring Argentina to hand over its YPF shares. In June, the full court declined to rehear the case.

Burford, which funds the litigation and acquired the rights of former minority shareholders Petersen and Eton Park, described the appeals ruling as “gravely mistaken, wholly unprecedented and of exceptional importance”. The Supreme Court is not obliged to take the case: it receives between 7,000 and 8,000 petitions per term and usually accepts about 80, and has no deadline to decide. Burford has also brought proceedings before the World Bank’s International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes.

Preska’s judgment, which exceeded US$18 billion with interest, was the largest ever imposed on a state by a US court. The litigation stems from the expropriation of 51% of YPF in 2012 under the government of Cristina Fernández de Kirchner. “We will continue to defend the interests of the State,” official sources said.

World.title: Milei arrives in Madrid mid-campaign and will meet Ayuso but not Sánchez
World.content:
Milei arrives in Madrid mid-campaign and will meet Ayuso but not Sánchez

20th Tuesday, October 2026 - 09:47 UTC Full article

Milei has clashed sharply with Sánchez since 2024 and has made his alliances with conservative leaders a hallmark of his foreign policy

Argentine President Javier Milei flew to Madrid on Monday night on his third visit of the year to Spain and his seventh since taking office, in the middle of the campaign for the snap general election on November 29. His agenda includes a meeting with the president of the Madrid regional government, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, of the People’s Party, but, as on previous visits, no meeting with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

On Wednesday, Milei will give a lecture on economics at the Nueva Economía Forum and meet economist Jesús Huerta de Soto, a leading figure of the Austrian School, before speaking at the launch of a master’s programme on that school of thought at Rey Juan Carlos University. In the afternoon he will meet the Disenso Foundation, linked to the Vox party, and be received by Ayuso. Unlike on other visits, no meeting is planned with Vox leader Santiago Abascal. The trip, which ends on Thursday, includes a small delegation headed by Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno and presidential spokesman Adrián Ravier.

Milei has clashed sharply with Sánchez since 2024 and has made his alliances with conservative leaders a hallmark of his foreign policy. Sánchez called the early election amid a social crisis over access to housing.

The Argentine government presents these trips as part of its strategy to attract investment in sectors such as energy and mining. The opposition questions their cost and usefulness. Spain is the president’s second most frequent destination, after the United States, which he visited last week for the twentieth time.

World.title: Alberta overwhelmingly rejects starting the path to an independence referendum from Canada
World.content:
Alberta overwhelmingly rejects starting the path to an independence referendum from Canada

20th Tuesday, October 2026 - 08:01 UTC Full article

The question did not ask directly about independence, but whether the provincial government should begin “the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution”

Voters in the Canadian province of Alberta on Monday overwhelmingly rejected having their government begin the process of calling a binding referendum on independence from Canada, according to preliminary results. With more than half the votes counted, around 76% chose for Alberta to remain a Canadian province, against about 24% who backed starting down the path to separation. Official results will be known on Thursday.

The question did not ask directly about independence, but whether the provincial government should begin “the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution” to hold a binding referendum on separation. Public broadcaster CBC projected victory for the remain option shortly after polls closed.

“Albertans made a clear choice. They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other. Above all, Albertans chose Canada,” said Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, of the United Conservative Party, welcomed voters’ support for “a stronger Alberta in a united Canada”. Smith had said before the vote that, with this outcome, there would be no separation referendum while she was in office.

Separatist leaders, however, struck a defiant tone. “Our movement isn’t stopping and we’re continuing to move forward,” Calgary lawyer Jeffrey Rath told the BBC, describing the vote as a “first step”. Asked whether they would keep pushing for votes until they got the result they wanted, he replied: “Why not?”

Albertans also voted on nine other questions, five on immigration, such as whether the province should take more control over it or restrict non-citizens’ access to some social services, and four on constitutional reform. The separatist movement draws on frustration with the federal government over the sharing of the province’s oil wealth and over provincial powers. Quebec held two independence referendums, in 1980 and 1995; the second was lost by a narrow margin.

World.title: The Role of Map Statistics in CS2 Match Analysis | Guide
World.content:
The Role of Map Statistics in CS2 Match Analysis | Guide

20th Tuesday, October 2026 - 00:44 UTC Full article

Predicting matches before a competition in Counter-Strike 2 requires a very fine and nuanced analysis. Knowledge of the teams competing, their playing style (team habits/teams preferences), their comfort level or preference for maps, and their competitive history is required for both analysts and the Tactical Staff. Analysis will look at current competitive data for each team in the current competitive landscape to determine the strengths and weaknesses of team compositions for future competition.

Tactical Frameworks and Veto Dynamics in Championship Play

Map selection is where tactics and execution are tested in major events. No team is likely to be very strong on all 7 maps in the active duty rotation. So veto picks are a huge part of pre-event strategy. On the CS2 betting sites there are quite sophisticated systems in place that track the number of picks and bans there are in various regions and at varying levels of competition. Just by looking at whether a team tends to go early ban on high-variance maps such as Nuke or whether they tend to pick maps they are very comfortable with, such as Mirage, you can get a pretty good idea of the level of tactics the team employs. Regional variances also play a large part in the variety of maps that a team will utilise. Asian/East Asian teams (also teams from Mongolia such as The Mongolz) have historically utilised faster maps such as Anubis or Inferno to a higher degree than the average EU team.

Global CS2 Map Pool Statistical Breakdown

Map Name CT Win Rate (%) T Win Rate (%) Average Rounds Ancient 54.2 45.8 21.4 Anubis 48.1 51.9 22.1 Dust II 51.5 48.5 21.8 Inferno 52.8 47.2 22.6 Mirage 50.9 49.1 21.9 Nuke 55.4 44.6 20.8 Vertigo 51.1 48.9 21.6

Core Statistical Metrics in CS2 Map Evaluation

Team performance on a map can't just be boiled down to win/loss. Instead, data can be segmented by time or by team to better reflect actual performance.

- CT Win Rate vs T Round Gain - Some maps have inherent imbalances that persist even through the continuous balance updates. Looking at the conversion rate of CT side wins to T side round gains can show how a team plays, whether they play a very static defence or a more dynamic playing style.

- Pistol Round Conversion - Every half starts with a pistol round. Winning this round gives the team an early in-game economy. Teams that have a high conversion rate in pistol rounds tend to create an early in-round safety that in turn affects the speed of gameplay on a map.

- Buy Type Efficiency - Performance in eco rounds, force-buy rounds and full-buy rounds can show economic awareness as well as performance under economic stress.

- First Kill Conversion Rate - First kills can significantly shift the chances of round possession. Entry conversion stats on a map can show how well a team can use team size to their advantage.

Economic Management and Utility Impact Across Different Map Layouts

An economy will have a large impact on map control and site takes. On large maps like Ancient and Dust II, range-capable equipment (snipers) and utility used at specific points on the map allow for significant amounts of money to be spent to provide defence against advancing enemies. Coaches (such as Andrey “B1ad3” Gorodenskyi from Natus Vincere) encourage the use of utility to open up more predictable opportunities for their team to perform actions in order to gain rounds and ultimately a tournament. This is achieved by opening up areas of the map to be softened up by utility.

Utility damage per round (UD/R) tracking can give a good indication as to how well a team is at disabling opponents prior to physical combat. Beyond disabling opponents via utility, the effective placement and deployment of grenades in defensive-dominated maps (Nuke) on the main and ramp can also stall the offence and cause the attacker to make inferior decisions during a short time period while attempting a site take.

Impact of Game Updates and Meta Shifts on Map Pool Viability

Regular game updates make it difficult for players to develop consistent strategies by changing maps in terms of layout, weapons, and/or economic factors. The company continually changes some map elements such as geometry, how high the “skybox” can be raised and/or how much light is allowed into choke points, which forces tactical coaches to reset their statistical baselines because winning percentages based on previous versions of a map will no longer apply.

The teams that are able to adjust quickly to an evolving map meta typically have a significant advantage at the beginning of major tournaments. When an update to a map favours aggressive middle-of-the-game pushes or alters the default hold position, the team that adapts first has time to take full advantage of this shift while their opponents try to create an effective counter- strategy. With tracking post-patch performance data from small samples, analysts are able to identify new strategic patterns before they become widely known through coverage of large international events.

Predictive Modeling and Long-Term Performance Trends

Modern-day esports analytics are now utilising predictive modelling using previous game history, each individual player's rating, and their situational performance. Using machine learning, a model can go through thousands of past games to find a hidden pattern that is difficult to see by simply looking at it manually. Algorithms will use weights from the previous games based upon a variety of factors including bias from one side, how well an opponent has performed recently against other elite opponents, and how many times they have been able to convert clutch plays. The analytical tools will then create a statistical probability for each upcoming match in a given tournament series.

While there is no doubt that computer-based forecast models continue to become sophisticated, human tactical evaluation continues to be essential. Computer programs can never provide a complete picture of what may happen because they cannot predict unannounced changes in tactics, unexpected lineup adjustments during the middle of the tournament, or mental toughness during extremely intense playoff matches. When trying to accurately determine who will win the most competitive CS2 tournaments in the world, combining your quantitative map data (such as K/D ratio) with your qualitative structural data (i.e., team strategy), you will get the best possible results.

World.title: Mexico suspends chicken imports from Brazil over Newcastle disease outbreak
World.content:
Mexico on Monday suspended chicken imports from Brazil, the world’s largest chicken meat exporter, following reports of a Newcastle disease outbreak in that country.

Mexico’s National Service for Agrifood Health, Safety and Quality (Senasica) halted imports of chicken meat, all live birds and fertile eggs to prevent the spread of Newcastle disease to Mexico, a measure that will apply to commercial imports and products carried in by tourists.

Newcastle disease is a highly contagious respiratory infection in birds that can cause neurological disorders, reduced egg production and high mortality rates, according to the World Organization for Animal Health. It poses no serious risk to humans.

Brazilian authorities first detected an outbreak of the disease at a commercial turkey farm in southern Brazil on Sunday, Brazil’s public news agency reported.

Brazil’s Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock then confirmed the presence of the disease at a commercial broiler chicken farm in the municipality of Nova Itaberaba, Santa Catarina state, on Monday.

The agency reassured the public that the facility had been closed and that measures had been implemented to control and eradicate the outbreak.

Brazil exports a massive 30% of its chicken production, according to official figures, and, in 2025, Mexico was Brazil’s seventh-largest poultry buyer.

This is the second time in 17 months that Mexico has suspended the import of poultry products from Brazil. In May and June 2025, Mexico, China, the European Union and other Latin American countries halted imports of Brazilian chicken due to an outbreak of avian influenza.

The last outbreak of Newcastle disease in Brazil occurred in July 2024 in Santa Catarina’s neighboring state of Rio Grande do Sul. During that period, chicken exports fell by about 25%, or 100,000 metric tonnes, according to estimates by analysts at JPMorgan. However, trade quickly rebounded as markets reopened.

The current outbreak is not expected to cause lasting damage to Brazil’s poultry industry so long as authorities can contain it quickly, according to analysts.

With reports from Noticias DW and Reuters

World.title: Mexico’s economy grew 3.7% last month, compared to September 2025
World.content:
Mexico’s economy grew 3.7% year over year in September, according to preliminary seasonally adjusted data published on Tuesday by the national statistics agency INEGI.

The annual growth rate is the highest of any month so far this year, exceeding July’s 3.3% expansion and a 3.2% estimated increase in August.

INEGI also published preliminary data on Tuesday that showed that Mexico’s economy grew 0.1% on a month-over-month basis in September. That growth rate is significantly lower than the 0.5% month-over-month expansion in August, according to INEGI’s latest estimate.

Both the annual and month-over-month growth rates for September are subject to revision. Final data for the month will be published in late November.

Services sector growth hits 4%

INEGI’s preliminary data shows that Mexico’s tertiary, or services, sector recorded 4% year-over-year growth in September, up from a 3.7% expansion in August.

The secondary sector — which includes manufacturing, construction, mining and electricity generation — expanded 3.6%, according to the preliminary data, on par with the growth rate in August.

INEGI didn’t publish preliminary data for the primary sector.

Analyst: Annual growth in Q3 could exceed 3%

In an X post on Tuesday, Banco Base’s director of economic analysis, Gabriela Siller, wrote that GDP data for the third quarter of 2026 “could show” quarter-over-quarter growth of 0.99% and annual growth of 3.04%.

En México, el PIB del tercer trimestre podría mostrar un crecimiento trimestral de 0.99% y anual de 3.04%, de acuerdo a las cifras del indicador oportuno de la actividad económica (IOAE). Esto se debe a que el IOAE de agosto fue revisado al alza, de un crecimiento mensual de 0.14% a 0.47%. Por su parte, en septiembre el IOAE mostró un crecimiento mensual de 0.09%. — Gabriela Siller Pagaza (@GabySillerP) October 20, 2026

An annual growth rate of 3.04% would represent a significant improvement from the expansions recorded in the first and second quarters of the year. Mexico’s economy grew 0.4% in annual terms in Q1 and 1.9% in Q2.

On a quarter-over-quarter basis, Mexico’s economy contracted 0.6% in Q1 and grew 1.4% in Q2.

Annual GDP growth in 2025 was just 0.8%.

In a separate X post on Tuesday, Siller wrote that there are “three factors that support greater economic growth in Mexico this year.”

Those factors, she wrote, are “the downward revision of GDP in the second quarter of 2025” as well as “greater public spending on physical infrastructure, which has a multiplier effect on the economy,” and “the high growth of computer equipment exports, reaching 209.75% annually in the cumulative total through August.”

Earlier this month, the International Monetary Fund revised its 2026 growth forecast for Mexico’s economy to 1.5% from a previous prediction of 1.2%.

World.title: Music, masked dancing and Afro-Mexican coastal traditions took center stage at Oaxaca’s first Afro Guelaguetza
World.content:
Twelve delegations brought music, masked dancers and coastal traditions to Oaxaca’s first Afro Guelaguetza on Monday, celebrating Afro-Mexican heritage and highlighting communities that officials said had long lacked recognition.

La Rejunjuneada — loosely meaning “the get-together” — took place in Chacahua Isla, a community on Oaxaca’s Pacific coast that has a predominantly Afro-descendant population. It lies in the Costa Chica, a coastal region spanning Oaxaca and Guerrero and a historic heartland of Afro-Mexican culture.

The festival marked Oaxaca’s Afro-Mexican People’s Day, an Oct. 19 observance established in 2013. A procession along the lagoon and through local streets preceded performances on a stage beside Chacahua Lagoon.

Afro-Mexican communities already participate in Oaxaca’s better-known July Guelaguetza, which showcases traditions from across the state. For example, Collantes, an Afro-Mexican town on Oaxaca’s coast, sent its Dance of the Devils delegation to this July’s festival.

The distinction is the focus: La Rejunjuneada gave those Afro-Mexican traditions and others their own dedicated festival rather than only a place in the broader statewide celebration.

Oaxaca Gov. Salomón Jara Cruz said recognizing communities’ histories must also translate into rights, justice and opportunities.

Villa de Tututepec Mayor Eder Muñoz Peña described the municipality’s Chatino, Mixtec and Afro-Mexican roots, saying the celebration represented historical justice as well as cultural pride.

The host delegation opened with the Fandango de Varitas. Another community performed the Turtle Dance, plus there were two interpretations of the Dance of the Devils — a highly representative expression of Afro-Mexican culture, with dancers wearing horned masks stomping and leaping to the music.

Enid Azucena Torres Agustiniano also participated. This summer, she was the first Afro-Mexican woman ever chosen as Goddess Centéotl — the main Guelaguetza’s cultural ambassador.

In Mexico’s 2020 census, 8.6% of Guerrero residents and 4.7% of Oaxaca residents identified as Afro-Mexican or Afro-descendant, compared with 2% nationwide, according to figures from Conapred, the federal anti-discrimination agency.

With reports from Quadratin and La Razón

World.title: Man arrested at Oaxaca International Airport with more than US $366K in undeclared cash
World.content:
Federal agents at the Oaxaca International Airport seized US $365,865 and nearly 6,000 pesos ($326) that a passenger arriving from Dallas, Texas, was carrying in his luggage.

Personnel from the National Customs Agency of Mexico (ANAM), the Navy Ministry, the National Guard and the federal Security Ministry (SSPC) participated in the operation.

➡️ En el Aeropuerto Internacional de Oaxaca, autoridades detuvieron a una persona procedente de Dallas, Estados Unidos, que transportaba sin declarar más de 365 mil dólares y 5 mil 900 pesos mexicanos. https://t.co/cjasoLY581 — IMER Noticias (@IMER_Noticias) October 20, 2026

The unidentified passenger stated to customs officials that he had nothing to declare, but the detection dog “Cinta” alerted its handler to the man’s baggage.

As a result, customs personnel carried out a physical inspection of the four suitcases and a backpack the traveler was toting, eventually locating several packages with dollar bills and national currency hidden among the contents.

In a press release, ANAM said that given the possible commission of a crime, the National Guard was notified and their agents seized the cash and carried out the count.

The Navy and the SSPC then arrested the suspect and informed him of his rights, after which he — and the seized money — were placed at the disposal of the Federal Attorney General’s Office, which will determine his legal status.

The newspaper Milenio reported that this was the first significant incident involving undeclared cash at a Mexican airport since members of the National Guard seized 16 million pesos (then worth about US $750,000) and arrested two at the Mexico City International Airport more than six years ago.

On Feb. 24, 2020, National Guard personnel found 14 million pesos in a suitcase and a backpack after an X-ray inspection, while 2 million pesos were confiscated from another passenger’s hand luggage after a routine inspection uncovered envelopes containing hundreds of peso notes of varying denominations wrapped in transparent plastic.

Visitors to Mexico are permitted to enter the country with cash totaling less than US $10,000 (or the equivalent in other currencies) without declaring it. However, customs officials must be notified upon arrival if carrying more than that.

With reports from El Universal, Línea Directa and Milenio

World.title: Morena is the clear favorite in Mexico’s 2027 midterm elections, say the (very) early polls
World.content:
Mexico’s midterm elections are set for June 2027, and the ruling party Morena has a commanding lead in national electoral preferences with 46% of voter intention, according to an Oct. 19 poll by the newspaper El Financiero.

In the poll, which measures generic party preference and not individual races, the National Action Party (PAN) is a distant second with 8% of respondents saying they would vote for the party. Although it may be more meaningful to give second place to “no preference,” which accounted for 31% of the responses, leaving room for some preference shifts down the line.

Following the PAN’s 8% are the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) with 6% and Citizens’ Movement (MC) with 5%. Meanwhile, the Green Party (PV) and Labor Party (PT), both allied with Morena, received 2% and 1% of voter intention, respectively.

The two new parties — PAZ and Somos — are still stuck in neutral, each garnering less than 1%.

In addition to measuring voting intention, the poll asked respondents for their opinion of each party. Here, Morena swept again. Not only did it record the highest favorable rating at 55%, but its two electoral partners finished second and third with 31% (PV) and 29% (PT).

The PAN earned a positive opinion from just 26% of eligible voters and the PRI 21%. More significantly, those two parties — the previous two to hold power before Morena — are burdened with negative ratings of 64% and 70%.

The 17 governor races are not all so cut-and-dry

A recent report by Político MX measured party support in the 17 state governorships up for election in 2027, using a variety of early polls. Here again, the results favor Morena but not quite as decidedly as the national poll.

Poll data is shaky at this point, but here’s the picture so far:

In Baja California, Guerrero, Tlaxcala, Campeche, Colima, Nayarit, Quintana Roo and Zacatecas, candidates from Morena or its allied bloc lead comfortably across all the polls reviewed, often by double digits.

In Sinaloa and Michoacán, Morena’s lead is less solid. One poll even showed the upstart candidate Grecia Quiroz, widow of the slain mayor of Uruapan, in the lead.

The northern states of Baja California Sur, Chihuahua, Sonora and Nuevo Léon, are toss-ups, with the PAN in the first three and the PRI and MC in Nuevo León challenging Morena.

In three El Bajío states, Morena could be the underdog. Querétaro and Aguascalientes are leaning toward the PAN, and in San Luis Potosí the incumbent PV has split from Morena and will run its candidate against its former electoral partner.

With reports from El Financiero and Político

World.title: UN chairman brings missing persons crisis in Mexico before General Assembly committee
World.content:
A U.N. committee responsible for monitoring the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance again pressed the General Assembly to take up the issue of disappearances in Mexico.

The chairman of the Committee on Enforced Disappearances on Tuesday presented the annual report to the General Assembly’s Social, Humanitarian and Cultural Committee (Sochum), reiterating its assertion that the situation in Mexico ought to be categorized as crimes against humanity, a proposal that Mexico has rejected.

Mañana compareceré ante la Tercera Comisión de la Asamblea General de la @ONU_es para presentar el informe anual del Comité contra la Desaparición Forzada @UNTreatyBodies. Esta comparecencia tiene una relevancia particular. Por primera vez desde la entrada en vigor de la Convención, el Comité ha recurrido al artículo 34 para llevar una situación a la consideración de la Asamblea General. Este procedimiento excepcional abre una oportunidad para movilizar la cooperación internacional en materia de búsqueda, investigación, esclarecimiento de la verdad y protección de las víctimas. También informaré sobre los avances de nuestro trabajo y las graves consecuencias que la crisis financiera de las Naciones Unidas está teniendo para el cumplimiento de nuestro mandato. En un momento especialmente difícil para el sistema internacional de derechos humanos, resulta fundamental que los mecanismos de protección puedan cumplir eficazmente las responsabilidades que los Estados les han confiado. 📅 Martes 20 de octubre, 15h00 (Nueva York). 🔴 Transmisión en vivo:

https://t.co/GLbxtfZ0Ax #UNGA81 #CED — Juan Pablo Albán (@JuanPablo_Alban) October 19, 2026

Sochum is one of six permanent U.N. committees that include representatives of all 193 member states.

“[G]iven the existence of well-founded indications that enforced disappearances have been and continue to be perpetrated in [Mexico],” Juan Pablo Albán Alencastro of Ecuador, the chairman of the Committee on Enforced Disappearances (CED), urged the General Assembly to formally take up the matter.

This marks the first time since the entry into force of the International Convention against Enforced Disappearances (CPED) that the committee in charge of monitoring compliance has recommended that the situation in a specific country be examined by the General Assembly. Albán had initially brought the issue to the Assembly’s attention in April.

The submission of CED’s annual report does not mean a resolution has been issued regarding Mexico, however, nor does it imply that a judgment has been made.

“This exceptional procedure opens an opportunity to mobilize international cooperation in the search for the missing, the investigation of cases, as well as truth-telling and protection of victims,” Albán said.

The goal, Albán said, is to provide support “for the adoption of preventive measures that will enable Mexico to tackle the crisis effectively.”

On Friday, Mexico’s Interior Ministry presented the U.N. with a progress report on the National Strategy for the Search for Missing Persons, while declaring that more than 16,000 people had been located this year.

Mexico also said a group of national and international specialists, with the support of the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, is reviewing the methodologies of the National Registry of Missing and Unlocated Persons.

The International Federation for Human Rights, which requested the U.N. activate CPED procedures, thanked the committee for its actions in a press release.

The decision “acknowledges the existence of international crimes that are emblematic of what victims are experiencing in [Mexico] and seeks to contribute to the adoption of measures aimed at preventing, investigating, punishing and eradicating such conducts,” it said.

With reports from El Universal, Aristegui Noticias and Milenio

World.title: MND Local BCS: Upcoming one-of-a-kind events in Los Cabos
World.content:
A little over two weeks after the return of high season in Los Cabos, the event calendar is already in full swing. Highlights so far include Sammy Hagar’s 36th edition of his annual birthday bash at the iconic Cabo Wabo Cantina in Cabo San Lucas, and Bisbee’s Los Cabos Offshore fishing tournament, with its robust prize pool exceeding US $2.39 million.

Over 100,000 requests were received for the 1,600 available tickets to attend “The Red Rocker’s” 79th birthday celebrations at Cabo Wabo on Oct. 9, 11 and 13. Joining him on stage were long-time collaborators like guitarist Vic Johnson (a bandmate of Hagar’s in The Waboritas and Sammy Hagar and The Circle) and drummer Kenny Aronoff (a bandmate in Chickenfoot) — as well as the always highly anticipated special guests. Notable among the latter category was Jerry Cantrell of Alice in Chains, who joined in on a version of his own band’s hit “Man in the Box,” plus the Van Halen classic “Ain’t Talkin’ ‘Bout Love” during the Oct. 11 show.

Unrehearsed and unpredictable

“That’s part of the charm of the Birthday Bash,” Hagar told Billboard. “It’s not rehearsed, and we never know really what we’re gonna do. I don’t invite people; I just invite kind of a house band, you might say. I’ve got a repertoire of about 400 songs, and if somebody says they know one of them, we throw it together real quick and go out and do it.”

As for Bisbee’s Los Cabos Offshore, over 122 teams competed during the three days of fishing, and there was more than one winner: Team Tikki Perro caught the biggest fish, a 350-pound blue marlin that narrowly beat the 347-pound blue marlin caught by Team Loose Crew on the final day of fishing. Those teams finished first and second in the standings, but due to timing and jackpots, the biggest winner monetarily was the third-place finisher, Team Trixie, who walked away with an oversized check for US $1,589,0007 for reeling in a 334-pound black marlin the day previous, and sweeping all daily jackpots.

But this drama was merely a prelude to the world’s most lucrative fishing tournament, which takes place this week.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bisbee’s Offshore Tournaments (@fishbisbees)

The biggest single event on the Los Cabos sports calendar, Bisbee’s Black and Blue marlin fishing tournament has been a local institution since its founding in 1982. Its impact, however, is global: No fishing tournament on the planet has ever topped the record US $11,651,300 prize pool offered by the Black and Blue in 2022.

As the name suggests, blue and black marlin are the most valuable catches — provided they meet the minimum 300-pound limit. In 2025, three teams earned checks totaling upwards of US $1.7 million for boating blue marlin, with the two largest in excess of 450 pounds.

This year, for the first time, Bisbee’s has added a fourth event to its Baja California Sur schedule: Mag Bay Mania in Bahía Magdalena, Comondú municipality. The format is also novel, with teams given the entire month of November to choose three days to fish, with 100 points each garnered for all virtually verified catches and releases of qualifying billfish (including blue, black and striped marlin, sailfish and spearfish).

The other three events — the East Cape Offshore, Los Cabos Offshore and iconic Black and Blue — all take place in Los Cabos. The prize pool for the 2026 Black and Blue, aka “The Super Bowl of Fishing,” will be announced when registration closes on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

Dates: Oct. 19-24

Location: Boats depart from the Cabo San Lucas Marina, with fishing permitted within a 50-nautical-mile radius.

Cost: Base entry is US $5,000 per team, or US $84,500 “all-in” to include daily jackpots.

Founded by Latitude 38 publisher Richard Spindler back in 1994, this epic annual 750-mile cruisers rally from San Diego to Cabo San Lucas celebrates its 32nd edition in 2026. This year’s sail, however, will be the first without Spindler as “Grand Poobah” of the proceedings, as he stepped down and sold Baja Ha-Ha LLC after last year’s event, citing age as the reason (he’s 78).

San Diego Sailmaker Chuck Skewes is the new Grand Poobah, or “Newbah,” and has stated he plans no major overhauls. A nine-time participant himself, he also has the expertise of longtime Assistant Poobah Patsy Verhoeven, a veteran of 20 Baja Ha-Has, to lean on. Boats will depart San Diego on Nov. 2 following the pre-launch costume party, with two stops planned along the way before scheduled merrymaking in Cabo San Lucas — including the “Can’t Believe We Cheated Death Again” dance party at El Squid Roe on Nov. 13, and an awards banquet at Mango Deck on Nov. 14, with awards given out in categories such as “most miles sailed” and “biggest fish caught” along the way.

Dates: Nov. 2-14

Location: Departs from San Diego, California, and arrives in Cabo San Lucas following stops at Bahía Tortuga and Bahía Santa María.

Cost: Entry fee is US $595.

Fishing and hunting-focused publication Western Outdoor News (WON) has a long history with Los Cabos, dating back to the halcyon days of Baja columnist and “The Sea of Cortez” author Ray Cannon, who helped put the area on the travel map in the 1950s and 1960s — largely because of its superb sportfishing.

The Los Cabos Tuna Jackpot was first organized by WON in Cabo San Lucas in 1999, and by 2019 it had crossed the million-dollar prize pool threshold. Now recognized as the richest tuna fishing tournament in the world, the 2025 prize pool exceeded US $1.4 million (just shy of the 2022 record of US $1,533,800), with Team North Star pocketing a cool US $572,225 for reeling in a 253-pound yellowfin.

But it’s not all about the money, as the tournament motto (“fish hard, party harder”) makes clear.

Dates: Nov. 4-7

Location: Cabo San Lucas Marina, with no off-limits boundary line for fishing.

Cost: Base entry is US $1,000 per team, or US $50,500 to include all daily jackpots.

The only PGA-sponsored golf tournament in Los Cabos — and one of only two in Mexico — returns to the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal course at Diamante for its 20th edition this year (the fourth based in Cabo San Lucas after 16 years on the Riviera Maya).

The last two tournament winners, Austin Eckroat (2024) and Ben Griffin (2025), have both confirmed they’ll return this year. However, since players aren’t required to commit until Oct. 30, the rest of the field is mostly still unknown, outside fan favorite “Cashmere Keith” Mitchell, Mexican invitee Álvaro Ortiz and Mexican qualifiers Alejandro Madariaga and Jorge Villar.

For the first time, both of Mexico’s PGA tournaments — the VidantaWorld Mexico Open in Nuevo Nayarit and the World Wide Technology Championship — will appear back-to-back on the schedule as part of the FedExCup Fall series.

Dates: Nov. 5-8

Location: El Cardonal Golf Course, Diamante, Cabo San Lucas

Cost: General admission tickets are US $139 for the four-day tournament, with daily tickets available from US $35. Access to VIP hospitality areas, however, runs significantly higher. The Skybox overlooking the 18th green, for example, costs US $1,499 for the duration of the tournament.

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.content:

SOUTH AFRICA · TRADE

Key Facts — The country South Africa is Africa’s most industrialized economy, with a large paper industry and a big media and retail sector.

— What happened The South African Revenue Service raised the import duty on newsprint in rolls or sheets from zero to 5%, effective Friday 16 October 2026.

— Who asked for it Sappi, a paper and pulp producer listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, applied to the trade regulator Itac in March 2026.

— The mill at stake Sappi says its Ngodwana Mill in Mpumalanga is the only operating newsprint plant in South Africa and the wider Southern African Customs Union.

— Import sources Canada supplied 47.2% of South Africa’s newsprint imports in 2024/25, ahead of Brazil with 19.8% and Norway with 18.3%.

— The review Itac will review the duty after three years to judge its effect on industry, newspapers and other users of newsprint.

— Still open How much of the 5% publishers and retailers will absorb, and whether a wider paper tariff package follows.

The South Africa newsprint tariff is now in force, a 5% duty on the paper that newspapers and retailers print on. The South African Revenue Service, the national tax and customs authority, applied the new rate from Friday 16 October 2026.

The duty protects Sappi’s Ngodwana Mill, which Sappi calls the region’s only newsprint plant, and it hits foreign suppliers led by Canada. Business Day laid out the findings behind the South Africa newsprint tariff on Wednesday 21 October.

What South Africa Decided on Newsprint

The International Trade Administration Commission, known as Itac, is the government body that advises on import duties and trade remedies. It backed a 5% duty on newsprint in rolls or sheets, which had entered the country free of duty.

The revenue service announced the change on Thursday 15 October in a notice on secondary customs legislation, citing Itac Report 784. The new rate applies from Friday 16 October, and Itac will review it after three years.

Why Sappi Asked for the Duty

Sappi is a paper and pulp producer listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, and it filed its application with Itac in March 2026. Its Southern Africa chief executive, Graeme Wild, warned then that cheap imports threatened the viability of local newsprint manufacturing.

Sappi told the regulator that falling global demand, worldwide overcapacity and low-priced imports were causing sustained losses at its Ngodwana Mill. Rising pulp and energy costs added to the pressure, Business Day reported.

What the Itac Figures Show

Itac found that newsprint imports grew by an average of 13% a year between 2021 and 2025, while domestic production fell by about 11.7%. The local mill’s capacity utilization dropped from 68.5% in 2021/22 to 46.1% in 2024/25.

The domestic producer’s share of the market slid from 60.8% to 51.1% over the same period, according to the Itac report quoted by Business Day. The regulator also cited a significant price disadvantage against imports and falling profitability.

The Ngodwana Mill and Its Jobs

Ngodwana lies in Mpumalanga, a province in the north-east of South Africa, and its newsprint line can make 110,000 tonnes a year. That is about 20% of the mill’s capacity of more than 570,000 tonnes, which also covers pulp, linerboard and packaging.

Sappi says the mill contributed R9.9 billion (about US$604 million) to Mpumalanga’s economy in 2025 and supports 1,500 direct and 5,000 indirect jobs. Sappi’s own website has used lower figures, about 1,100 direct jobs and R5.8 billion (about US$354 million), as BusinessTech reported in March.

Who Sells Newsprint to South Africa

Canada supplied 47.2% of South Africa’s newsprint imports in 2024/25, followed by Brazil with 19.8% and Norway with 18.3%, according to the Itac report. Those three countries together accounted for more than 85% of imports.

The new duty raises the landed cost of their rolls by 5%, a margin that matters in a low-price commodity trade. The South Africa newsprint tariff reaches publishers and retailers that print flyers and inserts first.

What It Means for US Readers

Canada, a North American neighbour, supplies nearly half of South Africa’s imported newsprint, so the duty narrows an export market for mills on this continent. It also shows Pretoria will use tariffs to defend factories, a signal for US exporters of paper and packaging.

The decision sits beside other trade steps, such as the end of support for kit car plants. Investors can read the profiles of the producer Sappi Ltd and the media group Caxton.

Pressure on the Wider Paper Industry

Packaging firm Mpact issued retrenchment notices to nearly 400 workers in its carton board business, Business Day reported, citing cheap imports and a stronger rand. Trade Minister Parks Tau has also told Itac to investigate the whole paper and paper products sector.

The minister said the pulp and paper industry is under strain in uncoated paper, newsprint, packaging and tissue. The industry says it has invested R33 billion (about US$2.0 billion) in the economy over the past seven years.

What Is Not Known

It is open how much of the South Africa newsprint tariff publishers and retailers will pass on to readers and advertisers. The notice also leaves open when the Government Gazette, the official state journal, will print the final text.

Itac has not said whether other paper grades will get similar protection after the sector-wide investigation ends. The effect on Canadian, Brazilian and Norwegian exporters will only show in the trade figures of coming months.

More: South Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the South Africa newsprint tariff?

The South Africa newsprint tariff is a 5% customs duty on newsprint in rolls or sheets, up from zero. It took effect on Friday 16 October 2026.

Who asked for the newsprint duty?

Sappi, a paper and pulp producer listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, applied to Itac in March 2026. It says low-priced imports threaten its Ngodwana Mill.

Which countries sell newsprint to South Africa?

Canada supplied 47.2% of imports in 2024/25, followed by Brazil with 19.8% and Norway with 18.3%. Together they account for most of the market.

How long will the South Africa newsprint tariff last?

Itac will review the duty after three years. The review will weigh the effect on industry, downstream users and the wider value chain.

Will newspapers in South Africa cost more?

The South Africa newsprint tariff raises the import price of newsprint by 5%. How much reaches readers depends on what publishers and printers absorb.

Sources: South African Revenue Service, Tariff Amendments 2026 (newsprint, Itac Report 784), 15 October 2026; Business Day, Can a 5% newsprint tariff save SA’s print industry?, 21 October 2026; Business Day, Sappi seeks 5% tariff on newsprint imports, 23 March 2026; BusinessTech, Ngodwana mill risks shutting down, 24 March 2026.

World.title: Honduras Floods Hit 1,741 in Sula Valley
World.content:
Lake Yojoa in northern Honduras during a rainy season (file photo: Luis Alfredo Romero, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

HONDURAS · FLOODS

Key Facts — The country Honduras is a Central American country of mountains and river lowlands, and its northern Sula Valley around San Pedro Sula sits on the floodplain of the Ulúa river.

— Why it matters River floods in the north damage homes and belongings within hours, and a second wave of rain can hit communities that are still wet.

— Why now The national risk agency Copeco gave the latest count on Tuesday 20 October 2026, and forecasters say a first cold front could arrive between Friday 23 and Sunday 25 October.

— What happened Floods in the Sula Valley have affected 378 families, or 1,741 people, in 13 neighbourhoods, and the Ulúa river is under watch.

— The numbers Water rose above one metre in some communities, the Ulúa read 4.30 metres at the Santa Bárbara stations, and a 48-hour green alert began at 7 a.m. on 20 October.

— What it means for you Travellers to San Pedro Sula, Lake Yojoa or the north coast could face heavy rain and road delays this weekend, and families abroad should wait for official aid channels.

— Still open Whether the Ulúa spills further, whether the cold front arrives, and how many people are affected once the damage count is complete.

Honduras floods have affected 378 families, or 1,741 people, in 13 neighbourhoods of the Sula Valley in the north of the country, Copeco meteorologist Alberto López said on Tuesday 20 October 2026. Copeco is the national risk-management agency, and it is watching the Ulúa river while forecasters warn that a first cold front could bring heavier rain between Friday 23 and Sunday 25 October.

For US readers, the Honduras floods matter to travellers heading for San Pedro Sula, Lake Yojoa or the north coast, and to families in the United States with relatives in the affected towns. None of the reports reviewed mentions deaths or an appeal for international help.

The same rain system hit the area around Lake Yojoa, where a storm before dawn on Tuesday flooded homes and set off landslides, the Honduran fire service said. Beyond the Honduras floods, our earlier coverage of the country, including Honduras Remittances Top US$10 Billion, shows how closely households depend on relatives abroad.

What Copeco Says About the Honduras Floods

López said Copeco has 378 families, with 1,741 people, on its register across 13 neighbourhoods of the Sula Valley, the Honduran lowland around San Pedro Sula. In some communities the water rose above one metre, and some residents lost all of their belongings, he told Hondudiario.

First humanitarian aid was delivered in the sectors known as Valle de Sula 1 and Valle de Sula 2, and Cabañas was due to receive help on Tuesday, Infobae reported. Officials are still registering damaged homes to decide which communities come first.

Hondudiario reported that the risk agency, formally the Secretariat of Risk Management and National Contingencies, issued a green alert for 48 hours from 7 a.m. on Tuesday 20 October. Green is a precautionary level below the yellow and red alerts that Copeco has used in earlier floods.

The alert covers low-lying and riverside areas of Pimienta, Villanueva, Potrerillos, San Manuel, El Progreso, Santa Rita, El Negrito, Ramal del Tigre in Tela and La Lima. It also applies to the Central District around Tegucigalpa and the zones next to Lake Yojoa, Hondudiario said.

The Ulúa River Is Under Watch

Hydrologist Luis Dacosta of the Centre for Studies and Development of the Sula Valley told Infobae that monitoring stations in Santa Bárbara recorded a flood level of 4.30 metres on Tuesday. He expects the river’s flow to move down toward the Sula Valley in the coming hours.

That surge could flood the buffer areas that absorb river water and raise pressure on communities on low ground, Dacosta said. The sectors under special watch are the low zones of Potrerillos and Pimienta and the right bank of the Ulúa.

Infobae noted that the evolution of the emergency depends on how the rivers behave, with the Ulúa the main concern. Our reading is that the 4.30-metre figure is a single reading from one set of stations, and the sources reviewed do not give the river’s flood stage for comparison.

Rain Also Hit Lake Yojoa and Its Surroundings

Proceso Digital reported that a strong storm in the early hours of Tuesday left homes flooded and caused landslides in several sectors of Santa Cruz de Yojoa, in Cortés department, according to the fire service. A landslide made access difficult on the road to the village of Buena Vista, and in the village of Los Naranjos three homes were found flooded with no one inside.

Separately, Infobae reported late on Tuesday, citing a specialist at the national weather centre Cenaos, that about 190 families, more than 700 people, remain affected by water around Lake Yojoa. The sources do not say whether those people are included in the Sula Valley count, so we do not add the two figures together.

A Cold Front Could Bring More Rain This Weekend

Cenaos, the national centre for atmospheric, oceanographic and seismic studies, said in its extended forecast that the first cold front of the season could arrive between Friday 23 and Sunday 25 October. If it forms, it could bring heavy rain, electrical storms and a moderate drop in temperature, Proceso Digital reported, and the forecast is subject to change.

The cold-front season normally runs from late November to March, so this one would come early, according to the same forecast. For now a trough in the middle atmosphere keeps afternoon and night showers going in Cortés, Santa Bárbara, Yoro, Atlántida, Copán and northern Comayagua, Infobae reported.

If the front arrives, Infobae said, urban flooding is a particular risk in San Pedro Sula, El Progreso, Villanueva, Choloma, Puerto Cortés and Omoa. Mountain communities near slopes face landslide risk, the same report said.

What It Means for You

Travellers should check road and flight conditions before heading to San Pedro Sula, Lake Yojoa or the Caribbean coast on 23 to 25 October, and follow Copeco notices. Our guide Honduras for Expats: Homicide Falls to 26.2 per 100,000, but Location Decides Safety covers how conditions differ by region.

Families in the United States who want to help should wait for official channels, because the sources reviewed name no public donation account. Remittances, which our report on Honduras Remittances Top US$10 Billion covers, are how many households recover after a disaster, though no source here links the two.

For wider context, our explainers Honduras Explained 2026, Honduras and Its Neighbours in Central America and Honduras Geopolitics Explained 2026 show how the country works. There is no city guide for San Pedro Sula on our site yet.

What Is Not Known

The Copeco bulletin itself could not be opened for this article, because the agency’s website did not publish one. The figures rest on Hondudiario, Infobae and Proceso Digital, which quote Copeco, Cenaos and the fire service and agree on the main numbers.

None of the reports reviewed gives a death toll, a count of injured people or a figure for economic damage. The sources do not say how many homes are destroyed, how many people are in shelters, or whether the Sula Valley and Lake Yojoa counts overlap.

It is not known whether the Ulúa will spill beyond the zones under watch, or whether the alert will be raised from green. The cold front is a forecast only, and Cenaos itself says it is not confirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people have the Honduras floods affected?

Copeco counts 378 families, or 1,741 people, in 13 neighbourhoods of the Sula Valley as of Tuesday 20 October 2026. A separate Infobae report cites about 190 families, more than 700 people, around Lake Yojoa.

Which river is being watched?

The Ulúa, which flows toward the Sula Valley, is the main concern. A hydrologist said monitoring stations in Santa Bárbara read 4.30 metres on Tuesday.

What does the green alert mean?

It is a precautionary alert that began at 7 a.m. on 20 October and lasts 48 hours. It covers low-lying and riverside areas in the Sula Valley, the Central District and the zones next to Lake Yojoa.

Is a cold front coming to Honduras?

Cenaos says the first cold front of the season could arrive between Friday 23 and Sunday 25 October. It is a forecast subject to change, and the season normally starts in late November.

Should US travellers change plans for Honduras?

The US State Department already lists Honduras at Level 3, Reconsider Travel, and says the country is vulnerable to heavy rains and flooding from June to December. Heavy rain could slow roads and flights in the north this weekend, so travellers should follow Copeco notices and check with airlines and hotels.

Sources: Hondudiario, 20 October 2026; Infobae Honduras, 20 October 2026; Infobae Honduras, 21 October 2026; Proceso Digital, 20 October 2026; Proceso Digital, 20 October 2026 (Cenaos forecast); U.S. State Department, Honduras Travel Advisory; Copeco, risk-management agency of Honduras.
