Cyberattacks on Armenian government agencies

Several Armenian government agencies have come under cyberattack, according to Citizen Lab, a Canadian organisation that researches cybersecurity and digital censorship and works to protect human rights.

Information security expert Samvel Martirosyan said the attacks were targeted rather than random.

The targets included specific individuals and organisations, notably the office of Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, the Central Bank and the Central Election Commission.

Investigators have identified the Israeli company Candiru as responsible for the cyberattacks. In 2021, the same company targeted Armenia, infecting computers with malware.

At the time, Candiru acted on behalf of Azerbaijan. Samvel Martirosyan says he cannot determine which country, if any, stands behind the latest cyberattack.

“My guess is that either Azerbaijan, Israel itself, or both countries are behind this. I don’t think any other interested party could afford to buy these services. Carrying out attacks of this kind requires authorisation from the Israeli military,” the expert said.

It remains unclear what data or information the hackers wanted to obtain and what they managed to access in the attacks.

Commentary

According to information security expert Samvel Martirosyan, the Canadian organisation Citizen Lab identified attacks similar to those recorded in the past. However, the earlier incidents did not involve exploits that require no user interaction, known as “zero-click” exploits.

He recalls that the Israeli company Candiru has previously carried out cyberattacks against Armenian government agencies.

This time, however, the attackers also infected devices through online s:

“They reached an agreement with an advertising network. Websites often use software from advertising networks to display ads, while the site owners receive a share of the revenue. In this case, a major advertising company effectively partnered with Candiru, using these ads to infect users.”

According to Martirosyan, the attacks targeted Windows computers as well as mobile phones. It remains unclear whether the hackers collected detailed, in-depth data from the phones. However, Martirosyan suspects they may use this information later to carry out “other types” of attacks.

“The attacks were widespread. Most infections occurred through the mamul.am website. Under no circumstances should anyone assume that the website itself had any involvement in what happened. The only issue was that it displayed banners from this advertising network. The ads appeared around one million times, and investigators classified 100,000 of those instances as targeted and malicious. The attackers used them to collect data or launch an attack.”

Martirosyan stressed that Candiru’s cyberattack was not the only incident of its kind in recent days.

Cybersecurity firms Cisco Talos and Recorded Future published a report describing an attack on Armenia by another hacking group.

Based on the group’s tactics, its interactions with other hacking groups and its time zone, the companies investigating cyber threats suspect that the attack originated in Kazakhstan.

“These hackers speak Russian. They may actually be based in Russia, but are trying to disguise their origins by posing as actors operating from Kazakhstan,” the expert said.

According to Samvel Martirosyan, Kazakhstan is an “unusual actor” in cases of this kind. He suspects that “other forces attempting to operate under the flag of Kazakhstan” may be behind the attack. In early 2026, the same hacking group attacked Armenia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade.

However, Armenia is not its only target. The group also operates against targets in Tajikistan, Belarus and Russia.

“These are not sophisticated tools that work on a ‘zero-click’ basis, without user interaction. The hackers use phishing and then try to install malware on computers,” the expert added.

World.title: Georgia’s party ban: Court to begin hearing government case against opposition on 21 October
World.content:
At noon on 21 October, Georgia’s Constitutional Court will begin hearing on the merits a case brought by the ruling Georgian Dream party, which is seeking to ban five opposition parties and political groups. The hearings will take place in Batumi and continue on 22 and 23 October.

Four of the five parties intend to defend their positions in court, while the fifth will boycott the proceedings. Some opposition groups also plan to hold protests in Batumi and Tbilisi alongside the hearings.

The Constitutional Court’s full bench will hear the case, meaning all its sitting judges. The court has nine seats, but only seven judges currently serve on it, with two vacancies. On 13 October, Manana Kobakhidze, one of the founders of Georgian Dream, left the court. She had previously asked to recuse herself from the case, but the court rejected her request. Kobakhidze said she had made the decision to leave the court independently and for personal reasons.

Georgian Dream MPs Archil Gorduladze, Giorgi Kakhiani, Tengiz Sharmanashvili and Tornike Cheishvili will represent the party in court.

Under the law, the court must deliver its ruling by 24 June 2027.

Why is Georgian Dream seeking to ban the parties?

The claimants — 88 Georgian Dream MPs — argue that all five parties have violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits political parties that aim to overthrow or forcibly change the constitutional order.

According to information released by the court, the claimants cite alleged human rights violations between 2004 and 2012, when one of the parties, the United National Movement (UNM), was in power. They also point to the parties’ current refusal to recognise Georgian Dream’s legitimacy. The claimants say the parties have rejected the government’s legitimacy since 2016 and are pursuing a common goal.

The claimants also accuse the parties of attempting to overthrow the government. In the case of the United National Movement, they further allege that it undermined the country’s independence and territorial integrity, citing the August 2008 war.

The opposition parties reject all these accusations.

What do the parties facing a ban plan to do?

United National Movement

The party will attend the court hearings, said Irakli Pavlenishvili, chair of its governing council. He called on members of the public to gather outside the courthouse in Batumi on the days of the hearings.

The UNM’s jailed founder and Georgia’s third president, Mikheil Saakashvili, has also demanded that he attend the proceedings. In a statement released on 17 October, he said he wanted the authorities to bring him to Batumi so he could “fully expose this so-called court and its master for their historic betrayal”. Much of the case against the parties concerns Saakashvili’s time in power, from 2004 to 2012.

The party’s leader, Levan Khabeishvili, who is also in prison, has likewise demanded permission to attend the hearings.

The UNM belongs to the opposition alliance and takes part in its protests.

What is the Opposition Alliance? The Opposition Alliance “Unity for Victory” was formed by nine pro-Western Georgian parties on 2 March 2026, following months of negotiations. Its members are the United National Movement, Ahali, Girchi – More Freedom, Droa, the Federalists, European Georgia, Strategy Aghmashenebeli, Freedom Square and the National Democratic Party. The alliance says its goals are to end the rule of Bidzina Ivanishvili, founder and honorary chairman of Georgian Dream, restore Georgia’s Euro-Atlantic course, release political prisoners and form a coalition government after Georgian Dream loses a free election. The parties retain their ideological independence but have agreed on a joint strategy for protests and communications. The alliance’s largest rally to date took place in Tbilisi on 26 May 2026, Georgia’s Independence Day. Two other major opposition parties, Lelo and For Georgia, led by Giorgi Gakharia, have not joined the alliance. Lelo chose to operate independently, while For Georgia rejected an alliance with the United National Movement and parties that split from it.

Coalition for Change

The coalition will also take part in the hearings. Its member parties — Ahali, Girchi – More Freedom and Droa — also belong to the Opposition Alliance. On 15 October, Nika Gvaramia, leader of Ahali, announced the launch of a joint campaign by the alliance.

Gvaramia said their struggle would not be confined to the courtroom. “We will be everywhere, including on the streets of Tbilisi,” he promised.

Strong Georgia – Lelo

Lelo will attend the hearings and has asked the Public Defender (ombudsman) to submit a legal opinion on the case. As of 19 October, the ombudsman’s office had not responded.

Lelo is not a member of the alliance. The party’s political council says it has several scenarios and an action plan ready in case the court approves the ban.

For Georgia

The party announced in a statement on 20 October that it would take part in the proceedings. However, it insists that the court consider the case against it separately, rather than together with the other parties.

The party of former Georgian prime minister Giorgi Gakharia does not belong to the Opposition Alliance. It was the only one of the five parties that refused to surrender its parliamentary mandate in protest and nevertheless entered parliament.

The Federalists

The party has decided not to attend the hearings, saying it does not want to lend the proceedings a veneer of legal legitimacy.

According to party leader Tamara Chergoleishvili, the Federalists will travel to Batumi but protest against the court proceedings outside the courthouse rather than in the courtroom.

Why does it matter whether the parties attend the hearings?

The parties’ attendance could affect their chances of appealing the verdict to the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) in Strasbourg.

Sandro Baramidze, a lawyer with Transparency International Georgia, explains that the ECHR requires applicants to raise and document their arguments through domestic legal proceedings first. If a party does not attend the hearing, its application to the court in Strasbourg could therefore be declared inadmissible.

Who is organising the protests?

As Georgian Dream seeks to ban the parties listed above, the Opposition Alliance has announced a protest campaign.

The first demonstration will take place at 11:00 on 21 October in Batumi, outside the Constitutional Court. Freedom Square, a member of the alliance, is organising the protest.

At 19:00 on 25 October in Tbilisi, outside the first building of Tbilisi State University, the Opposition Alliance will launch a joint campaign aimed at organising a large demonstration in Tbilisi on 28 November.

As of 20 October, Lelo and For Georgia had not said whether they would join the protests.

What is the rest of the opposition doing?

In addition to the parties facing a ban, the Opposition Alliance includes European Georgia, Strategy Aghmashenebeli, Freedom Square and the National Democratic Party. These parties are not named in the lawsuit but take part in all the alliance’s protests.

Levan Tsutskiridze, leader of Freedom Square, believes that banning the parties would create a bigger problem for Georgian Dream itself.

He says a ban will not make the country’s problems disappear. Instead, it will “close off the political path to solving these problems and guarantee an even worse end for Georgian Dream”.

Viktor Kipiani, leader of the party For Georgia First, points to the same risk:

Banning opposition parties through the courts effectively brings the political process to a standstill, while making change through elections virtually impossible.

He believes this will accelerate radicalisation in the country.

The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association has now issued its independent legal assessment of the case for the third time, arguing that the lawsuit aims to eliminate political competition.

What is the European Union saying?

EU institutions have reacted strongly to the Georgian authorities’ attempt to ban opposition parties:

The European Parliament adopted another critical resolution, calling for the immediate withdrawal of the lawsuit and saying it was considering personal sanctions against those who initiated the proceedings.

Christian Wigand, a European Commission spokesman, said Brussels was closely monitoring developments. He said the attempt to abolish leading political forces, alongside the Georgian authorities’ earlier statements and legislative changes, pointed to a worrying instrumentalisation of the justice system. This directly threatens democratic pluralism and fundamental freedoms.

On 20 October, Georgia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded that questioning the legitimacy of the proceedings before the court had even examined the case amounted to an attempt to pressure the court and interfere in the country’s internal affairs. The ministry urged EU representatives to refrain from statements that prejudge the proceedings.

What happens if the court upholds the lawsuit?

If the court upholds the lawsuit, the five parties will legally cease to exist. According to official figures from the Central Election Commission, a total of 784,820 voters backed the five parties in the 2024 parliamentary election.

Under current legislation, the court may also, at the claimant’s request, ban people associated with the dissolved parties from engaging in political activity. The law also provides a 14-day procedure for banning a successor party.

The hearings scheduled for 21–23 October mark the first stage in the proceedings. It remains unclear how long the case will take or when the court will deliver its ruling.

World.title: Armenia considers restricting regional cars from entering Yerevan
World.content:
Cars from regions banned from Yerevan

A statement by Yerevan Deputy Mayor Suren Grigoryan has sparked widespread debate in Armenia. He said that one of the city administration’s strategic goals was to create car parks at the entrances to Yerevan, where drivers arriving from other regions could leave their vehicles and continue their journeys by public transport.

The proposal has prompted heated discussions among both experts and residents.

Traffic experts suggest increasing parking fees in the capital rather than restricting vehicle access. Meanwhile, residents have raised concerns that the initiative could limit freedom of movement and lead to discriminatory measures.

People are also questioning how they would navigate Yerevan using public transport if travelling with young children or elderly relatives, or bringing a family member to the capital for medical treatment.

What else did deputy mayor say?

Deputy Mayor Suren Grigoryan said the city administration had no plans to introduce restrictions immediately. He explained that creating car parks and expanding the public transport fleet would take time. Grigoryan did not specify when a possible ban on cars from other regions entering Yerevan might come into force.

According to him, the number of cars in Armenia has doubled from 500,000 in 2014 to one million. Meanwhile, the number of vehicles in Yerevan is increasing by around 15,000 or more each year.

The deputy mayor also addressed plans to purchase new vehicles for public transport. He said the city planned to acquire 171 new buses in the near future.

However, Grigoryan acknowledged that he could not say with certainty whether all residents of Armenia’s regions would be able to switch from private cars to public transport.

Clarifications following statement

Following a wave of outrage on social media, the deputy mayor issued further clarifications. He stressed that he had been referring not to a measure that would be introduced immediately, but to a strategic goal that would be implemented gradually.

“There has been a misunderstanding. Some citizens assumed that vehicles from the regions would be banned from entering Yerevan. I said nothing of the sort,” Suren Grigoryan emphasised.

He attributed the confusion to the headline of his interview:

“It had nothing to do with the actual content of the interview. This is a clear example of what happens when people judge a news story solely by its headline.”

Expert opinion

Traffic expert Artak Gaboyan believes that banning private cars from Armenia’s regions from entering the capital would make little sense:

“Nowhere in the world do authorities simply tell people they are banned from entering a city. Instead, they create conditions that make leaving a car outside the city a more convenient and financially attractive option.”

To ease congestion in central Yerevan, Gaboyan suggests increasing parking fees to 1,000 drams ($2.60) per hour, roughly three times the current rate.

“In addition, free shuttle buses should operate near the car parks [at the entrances to the city], taking drivers to the nearest transport hub, metro station or interchange where they can transfer to regular public transport services heading in different directions,” he explained.

Gaboyan also believes that implementing his proposal would require ensuring the “uninterrupted movement of public transport”.

As an example, he cited Isakov Avenue, one of the capital’s busiest roads, where one lane is reserved exclusively for public transport.

Social media reactions

“Are you now dividing society into Yerevan residents and people from the regions? How long will you continue dividing society? Instead, ease congestion in the capital and sort out the traffic problems.”

“This violates people’s right to freedom of movement. The current city administration has already made life unbearable for us.”

“And what about the fact that many people are simply too lazy to travel one or two stops by public transport and prefer to use their own cars?”

“We come to Yerevan with small children and loads of bags. How does he expect us to get around on public transport?”

“Why not simply ban people from the regions from entering Yerevan unless they carry an ID card, an income declaration, a CV and at least three letters of recommendation? And then, why not require people from the regions to obtain police permission before leaving their villages?”

“The deputy mayor could start setting an example today: take public transport home, use it to get to work tomorrow, take his children to school and then go to the doctor. All by public transport. In short, let him try living like that for at least a week, and then we’ll see.”

“According to the deputy mayor, implementing this idea would require building car parks at the entrances to the capital and introducing dedicated public transport lanes. Given that over the past eight years the city administration has made no progress beyond a single dedicated lane on one avenue — failing to establish a proper network of such lanes or make progress in expanding the metro system — expecting them to resolve the issue of restricting cars from the regions from entering Yerevan is simply wishful thinking.”

World.title: South Ossetia’s new authorities seek to crack down on illegal trade in ‘award’ weapons
World.content:
The new president of South Ossetia, Marat Kambolov, has ordered an investigation into the legality of the circulation of civilian, service and military firearms, as well as bladed weapons.

The Prosecutor General’s Office is carrying out the president’s order. Kambolov’s fellow villager, Soslanbek Kozhiyev, was recently appointed first deputy prosecutor general.

A smuggled ‘award’

The authorities will pay particular attention to a practice that took hold under previous presidents: handing out Glock and Beretta pistols left, right and centre under the pretext of awarding them as honours. Smugglers brought the pistols into South Ossetia from Georgia.

Officials often used these supposed “awards” as a cover to sell the weapons to members of the criminal underworld or simply to anyone who wanted one. And plenty of people in South Ossetia want a gun “just in case”. However, Kambolov believes this “tradition”, which dates back to the 1990s, has run its course. He says that civilian gun ownership no longer serves a relevant purpose and that real security risks no longer justify it.

“Today, South Ossetia leads a peaceful life and is building a state governed by the rule of law. In a peaceful state, the law — not tradition, personal merit, official position or private arrangements — must determine the right to own a gun.

The republic has suspended all awards of weapons until the investigation ends. The state must know exactly where each weapon is, to whom and on what grounds it was issued, how it was registered and who is responsible for it,” the president said.

At the same time, he proposes extending permits to possess and carry most types of civilian firearms to ten years, while retaining mandatory checks and periodic permit renewals:

“This approach will allow us to bring order to the firearms register without imposing excessive bureaucracy on law-abiding owners. The republic’s Security Council will make the final decision on this matter, following a proposal from the prosecutor general.”

A rifle as a gift

These measures come amid criminal proceedings against former Interior Minister Erislav Mamiyev and his first deputy, Atsamaz Sagkayev.

Investigators suspect that Sagkayev “gifted” his boss, Mamiyev, a sniper rifle and an assault rifle in 2025 and 2026.

Authorities have opened two criminal cases against Sagkayev on suspicion of “abuse of official powers for personal gain or other personal motives”, an offence under the Criminal Code.

Some Telegram channels claim that over those two years, Sagkayev used the pretext of awarding weapons to sell 400 firearms to unknown buyers.

Both Sagkayev and Mamiyev lost their jobs at the Interior Ministry in August 2026, when Marat Kambolov, then prime minister, launched the first stage of a purge of South Ossetia’s security agencies.

The roots of the problem

Many consider Erislav Mamiyev a close friend of local crime boss Alexander (Alik) Gagloyev, the brother of former president Alan Gagloyev.

Social media has also circulated claims that Alan Gagloyev and his team planned to use his gangster brother and their friends, armed with weapons presented as “awards”, to hold on to power by force if he lost the 2027 presidential election.

But that scenario never materialised. In mid-2026, the Kremlin itself ousted Gagloyev from the presidency and effectively installed its own envoy, Marat Kambolov, in his place.

The new president is now trying to clean up his predecessor’s “legacy” and deliver on his promise to restore order, a pledge he repeatedly made to the people of South Ossetia over the past several months.

However, Alan Gagloyev was not the only former president involved in illegal arms trafficking. His predecessor, Leonid Tibilov, also had a record of such activity. One case came to light relatively recently, in autumn 2025. The major scandal that erupted at the time also implicated former Interior Minister Akhsar Lavoyev and Russian debt collector Eduard Budantsev, alongside Tibilov.

It emerged that back in December 2015, Budantsev and several former colleagues had exchanged gunfire in central Moscow using award weapons from South Ossetia. He had acquired the weapons through Tibilov and his inner circle.

“The trade in Glocks and Berettas in South Ossetia became a well-oiled operation under Tibilov and his associates. Gagloyev and his people simply continued the lucrative business,” a local expert said on condition of anonymity.

World.title: TV host gets 30-day detention in Georgia over Facebook post: reactions
World.content:
Journalist jailed over Facebook post in Georgia

Popular Georgian TV host Vakho Sanaia was sentenced to 30 days’ administrative detention on 19 October over social media posts deemed insulting to government officials.

The lawsuit was filed by the Department for Monitoring Hate Speech and Aggressive Statements, which recently became part of the Interior Ministry. Sanaia was accused of insulting Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili and MP Vladimir (Lado) Bozhadze in his Facebook posts and videos.

This is the third sentence handed down to the Formula TV host on similar charges since July this year, and his second term of detention.

Vakho Sanaia

Sanaia did not attend the court hearing, saying that prosecuting him for his posts was absurd. Police arrested him at his home.

“They want to force society into silence, but society will never be silent. We will overthrow this regime, however long it takes. This will certainly end in our victory,” Sanaia said as he was being arrested.

Why was Vakho Sanaia punished

The case centres on three social media posts about parliament speaker Shalva Papuashvili and ruling-party MP Vladimir Bozhadze.

The posts included censored profanities referring to the two politicians.

In a post on 22 July, shortly before he was detained in an earlier case, Sanaia wrote: “For 14 days, don’t call Shalva [Papuashvili] and Lado [Bozhadze] [censored insult] – when I get out, I’ll deal with that.”

In another post on 5 August, he referred to his earlier remarks, writing: “I wrote that you shouldn’t call Papuashvili and Bozhadze [censored insult], and they arrested me.”

On 24 September, Sanaia published a video address whose title also contained a censored profane reference to Papuashvili. Sanaia has described the proceedings as an attempt to restrict freedom of expression.

The case is being brought under Article 173¹⁶ of Georgia’s Code of Administrative Offences, which penalises insulting a political office-holder. The provision allows for a fine of 2,500 to 6,000 lari ($930–$2,220) or administrative detention for between five and 60 days.

This is the third administrative case against Sanaia. In July, he was fined 6,000 lari and sentenced to 14 days in detention over earlier posts involving the same two politicians.

The government agency that monitors social media

The Interior Ministry’s Division for Combating Hate Speech began operating on 1 June. It monitors public statements, including social media posts, and refers cases to court. Local media report that the unit often acts without a complaint from the person allegedly insulted. Cases brought by the division have led to dozens of fines and several detentions.

The case comes amid deteriorating relations between Georgia and the West. In November 2024, the government halted EU accession talks until 2028, triggering mass protests. Georgia has also fallen to 135th place out of 180 countries in Reporters Without Borders’ 2026 Press Freedom Index, down from 77th in 2022.

Sentence draws criticism in Georgia and abroad

European Commission spokesperson Christian Wigand has commented on the arrest of Vakho Sanaia:

“We have been very vocal in our criticism of Georgian Dream’s actions aimed at suppressing the political opposition, journalists and activists. Unfortunately, they continue to restrict civic space. The Georgian authorities must immediately release all unjustly detained politicians, journalists and activists and repeal repressive legislation.”

The Georgian Charter of Journalistic Ethics described the sentence as unjust, saying the authorities are using legislation and the courts to silence critical voices and restrict independent media.

“Through legislative amendments and, subsequently, the way these amendments are enforced, Georgian Dream has abandoned its obligation to tolerate criticism,” the charter said.

The Media Advocacy Coalition said the third case brought against the same journalist points to a pattern of persecution targeting critical media and dissenting voices. The coalition also expressed solidarity with the Formula TV team.

PEN Georgia called for the detention ruling to be overturned immediately. “In a country where journalists and citizens are jailed for criticising the government, and free speech becomes grounds for punishment, democracy no longer exists,” the organisation said.

Transparency International Georgia said Sanaia was being punished for exposing billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili, founder of Georgian Dream and widely seen as Georgia’s shadow ruler, and for supporting the country’s European future.

Parliament speaker: “Obscenity is not freedom of expression”

Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili said obscene language in public was unacceptable and could carry legal consequences.

“Obscenity has nothing to do with expressing an opinion and is not protected by freedom of expression,” he said.

Papuashvili said he did not follow individual cases. According to him, the Interior Ministry’s unit operates automatically, and those targeted often learn about decisions only after they have been made.

He also cited Germany, saying people can face criminal charges for insulting others on social media, including following a personal complaint by the chancellor.

Papuashvili also criticised the EU ambassador, claiming that “he himself promotes hatred” and that “some people may try to win his favour.”

“If he has the audacity to use obscene language in public, he should also have the courage to face the consequences,” Papuashvili said of Sanaia.

News in Georgia

World.title: Opinion: ‘Irakli Bzhinava’s arrest in Russia is blow to freedom in Abkhaz society’
World.content:
Abkhaz Foreign Minister Oleg Bartsits discussed the fate of Abkhaz lawyer Irakli Bzhinava, who has been in a Russian prison since February 2026, with his Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov.

Irakli Bzhinava

Irakli Bzhinava holds dual Abkhazian and Russian citizenship and lives in Russia. The initial grounds for his arrest stemmed from a social media post he published on 23 December 2022, in which he criticised an agreement to transfer a famous state-owned holiday residence in Abkhazia to Russia. Russian authorities accuse Bzhinava over the post of “criminal intent to make public calls for activities directed against the security of the Russian Federation”.

In mid-September 2026, Russia’s Investigative Committee opened a second criminal case against Bzhinava, accusing him of “publicly justifying terrorist Shamil Basayev on the internet”.

According to Oleg Bartsits, Abkhazia’s Foreign Ministry remains in regular contact with the Russian side and also liaises with Bzhinava’s relatives and lawyers. The Abkhaz consul in Russia recently visited Irakli Bzhinava, and the authorities also arranged a meeting between him and his mother.

Bartsits adds that some issues remain unresolved, but they fall under the jurisdiction of Russian law enforcement agencies, and the Abkhaz side respects this. Since Bzhinava is a Russian citizen, Abkhazia’s authorities have limited scope for action, although members of the public are urging them to do everything possible to help their compatriot.

Prominent Abkhaz public figure Akhra Bzhania explains in his blog why Irakli Bzhinava’s case matters so much to Abkhaz society. In his view, by punishing Bzhinava for his dissenting views, Russia is trying to intimidate all Abkhaz people who share his position. And there are many of them.

Most Abkhaz people oppose agreements under which Russia seeks to take something from Abkhazia or derive some benefit from it. The issue of Shamil Basayev is also controversial: he received the title of “Hero of Abkhazia” for his participation in the 1992–93 Georgian-Abkhaz war. In short, many other Abkhaz people could have made — and have made — the statements that led to Bzhinava’s arrest.

Akhra Bzhania: “An effective state is possible only when society is free and responsible. Society acts as a reservoir, supplying the state with everything it needs: personnel, money and a worldview. It also holds the state to account through the press and political institutions.

This model works wherever society is free and confident in its natural rights. To a large extent, it works in Abkhazia too. Our society delegates power to the authorities not as a sacred function, but to represent its real interests. When the authorities begin to disregard those interests, a correction follows: the government resigns, and the overall political course returns to a path guided by our own sovereign interests.

A free and politically active society is what makes us strong, allowing us to advance our own agenda under the most difficult circumstances. Our freedom is our immunity against everything that threatens us — a fence that marks where other people’s interests end and ours begin.

Irakli Bzhinava’s arrest is an attack on this very immunity.

I do not believe there are any naive people in Abkhazia who think the charges against our compatriot are purely personal. Almost our entire society could face the same accusations on entirely legitimate grounds, because the overwhelming majority of us think exactly as he does.”

Therefore, Bzhinava’s arrest and the extremely harsh conditions of his detention aim not to counter his personal views, but to control the ideological climate in Abkhazia.

From now on, anyone who dares to criticise agreements between Russia and Abkhazia must consider the possibility of arrest on charges of “making public calls for activities directed against the security of the Russian Federation”.

We must respond appropriately to this, if only out of an instinct for self-preservation, not to mention civic solidarity. This applies to everyone: political parties, public movements, creative unions and parliament. In this case, the strength of our response will determine the extent of our freedom. We must defend Irakli Bzhinava not for his sake, but for our own.”

World.title: Heydar Aliyev Foundation VP Leyla Aliyeva attends opening of World Summit on Investing in Children’s Well-being in Samarkand (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. Leyla Aliyeva, Vice-President of the Heydar Aliyev Foundation, attended the opening ceremony of the World Summit on Investing in Children’s Well-being: A Path to Sustainable and Equitable Development for Future Generations, and the Second International Congress on Childhood Cancer in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on October 21.

Prior to the opening ceremony, First Lady of Uzbekistan Ziroat Mirziyoyeva welcomed Leyla Aliyeva and the other participants. The attendees subsequently posed for a group photo.

The events, taking place on October 21–22, have brought together representatives from more than 100 countries.

Initiated by Uzbekistan, the summit was jointly organized with the UN Special Representative of the Secretary-General on Violence Against Children, UNICEF, the World Health Organization and the World Bank.

The summit is expected to conclude with the adoption of the Samarkand Declaration.

World.title: EU firms show growing investment interest in Karabakh and East Zangezur
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. EU firms show a growing investment interest in Karabakh and East Zangezur regions of Azerbaijan, reads the EU Business Climate Report Azerbaijan 2025/26.

This eighth edition of the report, funded by the European Union and prepared by VM Europe Consortium, presents an updated assessment of Azerbaijan's economic and business environment from the perspective of European companies active in the market.

The survey results indicate considerable interest among European companies in Karabakh, East Zangezur and Nakhchivan as potential investment destinations.

“The comparison between the 2024 and 2025 surveys indicates a clear increase in European companies' active engagement with Karabakh and East Zangezur, alongside continued interest in future investment. The share of companies reporting that they have already started working in the regions increased substantially, from 8% in 2024 to 19.4% in 2025. At the same time, the share of companies preparing or waiting for a suitable investment opportunity remained broadly stable. This suggests that some of the investment interest observed in the previous survey may be translating into actual business activity,” reads the report.

However, as the authors of the report say, the comparison should be interpreted with some caution because the corresponding question in 2025 also includes Nakhchivan, whereas the 2024 question covers only Karabakh and East Zangezur. The survey results indicate that European companies have a particularly high level of interest in doing business in Nakhchivan.

“Although the reconstruction has not directly affected most European companies, it has had a positive indirect effect on the broader economy and increased demand for logistics services. Most construction work is carried out by Turkish firms, while European companies are mainly involved in freight transport from Europe. Very few EU companies participate directly in reconstruction projects, and those that do are often subcontractors introduced by Turkish counterparts, typically operating as second-or third-tier contractors,” reads the report.

The authors believe that finance companies could benefit from informative, business-oriented visits to better assess local opportunities, while vocational training and business capacity-building linked to actual business development are considered necessary to support asset-building before business credit can become meaningful.

World.title: Middle Corridor boosts Azerbaijan’s role as transit hub
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. The Middle Corridor has reinforced Azerbaijan’s importance as a regional transit hub, says the EU-backed report.

The eighth edition of the EU Business Climate Report Azerbaijan 2025/26, funded by the European Union and prepared by the VM Europe Consortium, provides an updated assessment of Azerbaijan’s economic and business environment from the perspective of European companies operating in the country.

“Transport and logistics have become increasingly prominent in the assessment of Azerbaijan's economic potential. The development of the Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor has reinforced the country's importance as a regional transit hub, and businesses broadly acknowledge the strategic significance of Azerbaijan's investments in rail, port, and customs infrastructure. At the same time, interviewed companies also point to bottlenecks related to corridor efficiency, operational coordination, and logistics costs. Further progress in this area will be essential if Azerbaijan is to fully capitalise on its transit role and strengthen its position in regional and international value chains,” reads the report.

The authors point out that Azerbaijan continues to occupy a strategically important position at the intersection of Europe and Asia, with energy cooperation and transport connectivity remaining central pillars of EU-Azerbaijan relations.

“At the same time, the country is pursuing a broader economic transition aimed at reducing its dependence on hydrocarbons and strengthening the role of the non-oil economy. This process has gained further relevance in light of changing geopolitical conditions, shifting trade routes, and increasing international focus on regional resilience, energy security, and diversified supply chains,” reads the report.

According to the interviewed European companies, Azerbaijan's geographic location, expanding transport infrastructure, and relatively stable operating environment remain among the country's most important assets.

“At the macroeconomic level, Azerbaijan has demonstrated resilience, although growth dynamics have become more moderate and remain influenced by fluctuations in hydrocarbon revenues, public spending patterns, and external developments,” the report says.

The investment climate is generally assessed as satisfactory. European businesses point to positive developments in infrastructure, energy availability, and market accessibility.

The report also highlights the growing importance of sustainability and green transformation on the country's economic agenda.

“Azerbaijan has taken visible steps to promote renewable energy development, improve energy efficiency, and position itself as a future green energy partner. However, according to European businesses, the transition remains at an early stage in many sectors, and stronger incentives, clearer frameworks, and improved access to green finance will be needed to accelerate uptake and create a more enabling environment for sustainable investment,” reads the report.

World.title: EU recommends direct passenger rail link to Azerbaijan’s Alat FEZ
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. EU recommends Azerbaijan to construct a direct passenger railway line to the Alat Free Economic Zone (AFEZ) to improve its accessibility for workers and investors, reads the “Trade Study Report – Trade Sector Development in Azerbaijan: Policies, Constraints and Opportunities”, issued by the EU.

The report’s authors point out that the establishment of AFEZ is a positive and strategic step for Azerbaijan’s economic development, attracting investment, and creating new business opportunities.

At the same time, as the report says, it is important to take into account a number of key factors to fully realize AFEZ’s potential and ensure its long-term competitiveness.

“One of these factors is ensuring the accessibility of the zone for investors, workers, and businesses. International experience shows that, alongside a favourable geographical location, effective connectivity with major urban centres and transport hubs plays an important role in shaping the competitiveness of special economic zones. Alat is located approximately 65 km from the city centre and currently has no direct metro, ferry, or suburban passenger rail connection with central Baku. However, the successful operation and long-term development of AFEZ also depend significantly on ensuring the accessibility of the zone for investors, workers, and businesses. To this end, establishing a connection with Absheron Railway Station, which is only 7 km from Baku Central Railway Station, and then developing the existing railway connection from Heybat to Alat for passenger transportation could significantly improve Alat’s accessibility,” reads the report.

The Alat Free Economic Zone (AFEZ), established by the Presidential Decree dated May 22, 2020, is located adjacent to the Baku International Sea Trade Port and at the intersection of international transport corridors. Alat Free Economic Zone gives preference to investors engaged in high-value-added and export-oriented manufacturing, using innovative technologies and approaches to work, in accordance with best international standards.

World.title: Azerbaijan could establish ExImBank to support SMEs, EU says
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. The European Union (EU) recommends Azerbaijan to establish ExImBank targeting small and medium-sized enterprises, reads the “Trade Study Report – Trade Sector Development in Azerbaijan: Policies, Constraints and Opportunities”, issued by the EU.

According to the findings of the study, a significant proportion of both goods and services exporters suffer from the limited availability or inaccessibility of trade finance services. Yet, the report shows that financial institutions such as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Islamic Development Bank, World Bank, Asian Development Bank, and Black Sea Trade and Development Bank provide trade finance instruments to Azerbaijani exporters.

“Since trade-finance resources allocated by international financial institutions are administered through commercial banks, there is a possibility that these funds may be diverted to purposes other than export financing. To this end, strengthening monitoring of the appropriate use of trade finance funds and organizing awareness-raising programs for exporters in this area would be beneficial. In the context of the transformation of KOBİA and AZPROMO, it would be beneficial to establish a financial instrument in the form of an Azerbaijan Export Credit Insurance and Factoring Fund or an ExImBank,” the report reads.

The authors of the report believe that this fund could provide export contract insurance, pre-export financing, and factoring services at low interest rates to SMEs exporting non-oil products and services.

World.title: Breaking: Putin announces release of imprisoned US citizen during meeting with Witkoff
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has said that Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old US citizen held in Russian custody since 2022, had been freed and was at Pulkovo Airport in St Petersburg.

Mr Putin did not give further details in comments published by Russian state media on Wednesday, local time.

He made the announcement during a meeting with US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg.

Mr Hubbard, a retired schoolteacher from Michigan, had been serving a nearly seven-year prison sentence in Russia after being convicted of mercenary activity at a closed-door trial.

He was arrested in April 2022 in the eastern Ukrainian city of Izyum, where Russian prosecutors alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint.

Russian state media reported he pleaded guilty to the charges. But his US-based lawyer, Martin De Luca, previously told Reuters Mr Hubbard had said the charges were false and that he was not part of any combat or military unit.

At the time of his release, Mr Hubbard was the only US prisoner held by Russia who was designated by Washington as "wrongfully detained".

Mr Witkoff thanked the Russian president for the gesture of goodwill.

The talks in St Petersburg, the ninth time that Mr Witkoff has met Mr Putin in person, are intended to review new ideas on ending the war in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War II.

The meeting comes amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications.

The latest talks came more than two years after US President Donald Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours.

Mr Witkoff flew into Russia's second city on Wednesday morning, a day after conducting what a US official called "constructive" talks in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the leaders of Finland and Norway and European and NATO representatives, as Mr Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing".

World.title: Man arrested for allegedly making threats at WA MP's office with nunchucks
World.content:
Police have arrested a man after he reportedly made verbal threats while armed with "nunchucks" at state MP Hannah Beazley's electoral office in the inner-city Perth suburb of Victoria Park.

In a statement, police said they responded to reports of a man causing a disturbance at the electorate office on Albany Highway in Victoria Park about 1:15pm today.

They said he was armed with nunchucks — a weapon used in martial arts made of two short sticks connected by a short chain.

Police found the 56-year-old man in nearby Bentley, where he was apprehended. He is assisting police with their inquiries.

No-one was injured in the incident.

Man 'demanded to see MP'

Speaking outside parliament, Ms Beazley said the man had allegedly demanded to see her.

She said he was asking for her by name and "demanding access" to her while brandishing "home-made" nunchucks.

"But apart from that, when he was escalated, [they] couldn't actually understand what he was saying," she said.

Ms Beazley said it was especially concerning due to the "heightened environment" following the alleged attack on Helen Haines in Victoria.

Hannah Beazley's electorate office is in the inner-city suburb of Victoria Park. (ABC News: Madigan Landry)

"I immediately jumped to concerns for [my staff], and to be honest concerns of getting home and being able to have a conversation with my kids before they found out from anyone else," she said.

"Often times my local police say to me I should be calling them more often with some of the stuff we see in the electoral office.

"I'm a highly accessible member of parliament, I love that … every time I walk down the street I'm stopped for a conversation — I do not want to see that change at all."

Earlier, Ms Beazley described the incident as a "confronting situation".

"I have spoken to my staff, who are understandably shaken and upset by what took place," she said in a statement.

"At this time, I do not know the motivation behind what occurred today."

Ms Beazley is the daughter of former federal opposition leader Kim Beazley, who was also a former US ambassador and WA governor.

Witness heard screaming

Olivia Nelson witnessed the incident from a business across the road.

"We heard some screaming, and that's not uncommon here along this strip," she said.

"But we heard it pretty prevalently so we went out there.

"And this guy was just screaming, cussing, going crazy."

Olivia Nelson said she heard screaming, which she described as "scary stuff". (ABC News: Madigan Landry)

Ms Nelson said the incident was different from what she ordinarily might witness along the highway.

"It was scary stuff," she said.

"He was much louder than the usual crowd that we see."

Safety discussion

The incident comes just two days after an attack on the federal member for Indi Helen Haines, who remains in a critical condition in hospital after being run over outside her electoral office.

Leaders of the state's political parties are due to meet with representatives from government, police and the parliament tomorrow to discuss safety issues in the wake of the attack on Ms Haines.

Roger Cook said safety at electorate offices is under discussion. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

Premier Roger Cook said yesterday it would offer an opportunity to talk about recent improvements, as well as "what further actions can be taken to improve the security arrangements".

"There's three elements here: there's the parliamentary precinct, where we're already undertaking significant upgrades in security," he said.

"There's electorate offices, and they've changed significantly since I was an electorate officer back in the 1990s, and obviously there's people's homes as well."

World.title: 18yo charged over alleged Alice Springs hit-and-run that left man dead
World.content:
Police have charged an 18-year-old man with dangerous driving causing death five months after an alleged hit-and-run that killed a 57-year-old man in Alice Springs.

In a statement this afternoon, an NT Police spokesperson said the man was arrested at Alice Springs police station today. He was also charged with hit-and-run "and multiple other offences relating to the fatal crash".

Police have previously said the 57-year-old was found unresponsive on Len Kittle Drive at about 9:30pm on May 20 and was "believed to have suffered head injuries consistent with a vehicle strike".

"The 57-year-old male victim received catastrophic injuries and died at the scene," the spokesperson said.

A week later, police announced a taskforce had been formed to investigate the man's death involving major crash and regional crime detectives after he was captured on dash cam footage walking south near the BMX track.

"It is believed he was struck and killed by a vehicle about 350 metres south of this location, near the Men’s Shed building at Blatherskite Park," the spokesperson said at the time.

In the statement today, the spokesperson said the investigation had involved "a coordinated effort by specialist police units from across the Northern Territory".

"Police acknowledge and appreciate everyone who came forward and assisted investigators," they said.

The 18-year-old man has been remanded in custody to appear in the Alice Springs Local Court tomorrow.

World.title: Data centre gas plant could be mothballed after two years, court told
World.content:
A gas-fired power station proposed for the NSW Southern Highlands could be mothballed once the grid can meet the energy demands of an onsite data centre, a court has heard.

The NSW Land and Environment Court is considering an appeal by developers Nakar Property, after Wingecarribee Shire Council refused its development application for a 16-megawatt power station and battery energy storage system in Moss Vale.

The station is one of three planned to power a data centre campus on site proposed by Sydney company Cloud Carrier.

Barrister James Smith, acting for Nakar Property, told the court the power plant was needed to provide constant power for customers using the centre.

"[Cloud Carrier's] investment in computers is circa a $1 billion; the fundamental requirement is firm supply," Mr Smith said.

"It's akin to enrolling your child in school without any teachers; Cloud Carrier can't sell any product unless there is firm supply."

The proposed gas-fired power plant would be used to run Cloud Carrier's data centre campus. (ABC Illawarra: Penny Burfitt)

The second day of hearings before Commissioner Nicola Targett came after the court travelled to Moss Vale to inspect the site of the $23 million project on Tuesday.

In his opening submissions, Mr Smith said developers would stop using gas power as soon as a reliable supply of energy from the grid could be secured.

"The cost savings per year via connecting to the grid is approximately $14 million per year," he said.

"There is clear financial incentive to use the grid when that power becomes available. The issue is there is not sufficient supply."

Referencing expert reports, Mr Smith said the power plant was projected to emit less greenhouse emissions than if it were powered by the grid until approximately 2029.

Grid touted as a 'panacea'

Addressing Commissioner Targett, barrister Michael Staunton, for Wingecarribee Shire Council, said that power supplied by the grid had been touted as a "panacea" to the project, but not investigated thoroughly.

"All of that work and investigation should have been done, and you'll find when you get to the documents, it hasn't been," Mr Staunton said.

After an adjournment, Wingecarribee Shire Council tendered draft conditions of consent in the middle of the hearing.

These included a new requirement that canopy trees be planted across approximately 40 per cent of the development site.

Expert air-quality, electrical and engineering consultants appeared as witnesses for cross-examination about reports they had prepared for the project.

Mr Staunton argued during cross-examination that the project would not have the secure power needed to fill the full capacity of servers in the proposed data centre for two years, when an upgrade of a nearby power substation operated by Endeavour Energy would be completed.

"You've got no firm supply for two years," Mr Staunton said.

"That time could be spent negotiating with Endeavour Energy while you wait for the permanent connection."

The matter will return to court on Thursday for a third day of hearings.

World.title: Seven people charged over deadly alleged pack attack in Melbourne's west
World.content:
The final moments of a 24-year-old allegedly hacked to death in a pack attack in Melbourne's south-west have been revealed as three boys and four men face charges almost two years after the ambush.

Lino Atem was allegedly stabbed 26 times as he drank and listened to music with his friends at a reserve Haines Drive in Wyndham Vale on January 10 last year.

A children's court heard 18 youths stormed the park in what prosecutors described as a riot with weapons as Lino's group was preparing to leave, attacking the group before fleeing in cars.

Lino died at the scene, while a friend and one of his brothers were also injured.

Police previously said the attack may have been a case of mistaken identity. (ABC News: Leanne Wong)

Police previously said they believed the "ferocious" and "targeted" ambush on Lino may have been a case of mistaken identity.

Three 17-year-old boys and four men, including two 18-year-olds, a 20-year-old and a 21-year-old, were charged with manslaughter on Wednesday morning after raids across Melbourne.

The 17 and 18 year-olds all fronted a children's court, where prosecutors said they would probe DNA on a machete found at the scene and a beer bottle located inside a car connected to the accused young men.

The court was told some DNA collected from the scene matched one of the co-accused, and one of the co-accused is on bail for unrelated drug offences.

The court was told CCTV and items of clothing would also be central to their case.

Two of the 17-year-old boys are expected to apply for bail on Thursday.

Prosecutors told the court they had not ruled out additional suspects, and that the investigation was continuing.

Charges come nearly two years after death

The slew of charges laid on Wednesday comes almost two years after Lino's death and is the most significant breakthrough in the investigation since police arrested 13 youths over the fatal attack last year.

They were all without charges pending further inquiries.

Police estimated that more than 160 detectives across the Homicide Squad, Crime Command and the north-western region were involved in those raids, which spanned 15 properties.

Lino's death followed the shooting death of his brother Atem at their Wyndham Vale home in February 2023.

Atem was allegedly followed home and shot, along with his friend Ayuel Akuei and the family dog.

The boys' father Deng Atem told the ABC he could not comprehend losing two of his sons following Lino's death.

"My son called me … he said, 'I can't believe it. Lino is dead like Atem two years ago'," Mr Atem said at the time.

"I want justice."

The 20 and 21-year-old men charged over Lino's death were due to appear in the Melbourne Magistrates' Court later on Wednesday night.

The accused youths will return to court for a committal hearing next month.

World.title: Hundreds rally at parliament against proposed university merger
World.content:
More than 300 university students and staff have marched on Parliament House to protest a controversial plan to merge three of Western Australia's four public universities.

The government last week announced a steering committee to investigate the merits of combining the University of Western Australia, Curtin and Murdoch to create Australia's largest university with more 100,000 students.

More than 300 university students and staff joined the protest. (ABC News: Lucy Murray)

The move was immediately slammed as expensive and wasteful by both Murdoch and Curtin universities, while UWA Vice Chancellor Amit Chakma praised the "aspiration" of the plan and its desire to improve the sector.

Students chanted "I repeat, I say, no merger in WA" and "say it loud, say it clear, we don't want a merger here," as members of the three student guilds spoke to the crowd.

Students attending the protest questioned the benefits of the proposed merger. (ABC News: Lucy Murray)

Parallels to France protests

Curtin University guild president Dylan Storer said students would not back down.

"Our universities belong to the people of Western Australia, and we deserve a say in their future," he said.

"Right now, our state government has an opportunity. An opportunity to invest in affordable student housing. To invest in better teaching, better facilities and better student support … you cannot fix a cost-of-living crisis with a corporate restructure."

Dylan Storer said students would not allow politicians to decide the future of universities. (ABC News: Lucy Murray)

Incoming UWA guild councillor Rojin Didari described the actions of protesters in France as "heroic" and urged WA students to "take a leaf" out their book.

Protests over poor classroom conditions have turned into riots in the European country, with widespread violence and looting.

Rojin Didari described the students protesting in France as "heroic". (ABC News: Lucy Murray)

But speaking after the protest Mr Storer distances himself from those comments, saying he did not agree and most people in attendance would "deplore that kind of violence".

Minister not in attendance

Tertiary Education Minister Tony Buti said he would not address the rally because he had only been invited yesterday, and would be introducing an overhaul of the state's discrimination laws to parliament at the same time.

Tony Buti is asking students and academics to keep an open mind about the merger. (ABC News: Keane Bourke )

Dr Buti repeated the government's concerns about students receiving a sub-par education and said money spent on executives should instead benefit them.

"All I ask students, all I ask academics ... let's re-imagine [university] education," he said.

WA's university merger explained The University of Western Australia, Murdoch University and Curtin University could be merged under a WA government proposal. What's behind the plan, how will it work and what comes next?

Dr Buti said he could understand why students were concerned about the proposal but accused guild presidents of cherry picking the information they give to them.

He said no commitment had been made and a merger would only proceed if the business case stacked up.

Numbers in parliament

But the merger may be in trouble before the business case even begins, with doubt over whether Labor has the numbers to get the legislation through parliament.

The Liberal party room voted on Tuesday to reject the proposal, regardless of the business case, and the Greens are also strongly opposed to the idea.

It means Labor would need the support of at least three members of the cross bench to pass its bill.

Opposition education spokesman Liam Staltari said it was "the wrong proposal, flat out".

Liam Staltari says WA's universities need more investment, not a "forced triple-mega-merger". (ABC News: Lucy Murray)

"Have we ever seen this government commission a business case that at the end of the process doesn't end up with a glowing view of their own pet project?" he said.

"What they haven't counted on is the opposition of students and the community saying they won't just roll over and accept a forced mega merger."

World.title: Man who allegedly threatened to 'blow up' unit block given bail
World.content:
A teenager who allegedly yelled racist insults and threats to "blow up" a Morningside unit block has been ordered to wear an electronic monitoring device while out on bail.

Harley Adams, 19, appeared in Brisbane Magistrate's Court on Wednesday, charged with hate crime offences, after he allegedly threatened a family in the early hours of Monday morning.

Police prosecutor Sergeant Matt Kahler described the alleged incident as an "extraordinary racist outburst".

Sergeant Kahler alleged Mr Adams wrongfully believed the victims of his outburst had made a complaint which led to his eviction.

They noted Mr Adams was apologetic once he was told no such complaint had been made.

Police allege other residents within the unit complex have been breaking leases and moving out on account of Mr Adams' behaviour, the court heard.

Magistrate Peter Saggers cautioned Mr Adams that the courts take violent claims seriously.

"When you say you're going to do things then the court will proceed on the basis of that's what you mean," he said.

"If you say you're going to blow yourself up and blow everybody up with you then there's no point in shaking your head because that's what I accept."

Mr Adams was granted bail, on the basis he wears an electronic monitoring device, stays away from the unit complex and its residents, and reports to the local police station three times a week.

His matter was adjourned to November 16.

World.title: Husband of Helen Haines says critically injured MP is a 'fighter'
World.content:
The husband of Helen Haines has spoken publicly for the first time since Monday's attack on his wife, confirming her second leg had been amputated due to her injuries.

Joined by Governor-General Sam Mostyn, Phil Haines said his wife's recovery would be "long and difficult" after she was struck by a car outside her Wangaratta electorate office in Victoria's north-east.

"But we know she is a fighter, she is a determined person to do her best, with our support and love, to recover," he said.

"And that is what we hope for."

Mr Haines became emotional during his address at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne, where doctors are working to save his 65-year-old wife from critical injuries.

Helen Haines and her husband Phil live on a farming property in the King Valley. (Supplied: Helen Haines)

"What took place on Monday was a horrendous incident, and as you know, it's caused Helen significant injuries," Mr Haines said.

"As a result of that, Helen's left leg was amputated on Monday.

"We had been hoping her right leg would be saved, but as of this afternoon or this morning, the surgeons also had to remove her right leg."

Mr Haines, a farmer and agricultural scientist, married Ms Haines in 1986 and the couple are set to celebrate their 40th wedding anniversary next month.

"Her heart is huge — she is a very compassionate, caring, loving person, incredibly supportive of all around her," he said of his wife.

"And her mind — she has the sharpest intellect. She has always had the most intense desire to learn, to read, to synthesise and to understand what's going on.

" We are grateful and thankful that, at this stage, both her heart and her mind are in good shape. "

The governor-general confirmed King Charles had been given updates on Ms Haines's medical situation and urged Australians to "disagree well" and exercise their "muscle of decency."

"We don't have to all agree, but we can wrestle the issue, not the person," Ms Mostyn said.

"Words matter, whether spoken or in written form, increasingly in the virtual world."

Sam Mostyn has urged Australians to follow Helen Haines's example by conducting political debate with greater civility. (ABC News: Tara Whitchurch)

McGowan urges voters to 'call out bad behaviour'

Former independent MP Cathy McGowan represented the seat of Indi before Ms Haines, breaking the Coalition's 82-year hold on the seat in 2013.

Speaking to Fran Kelly on ABC's Radio National Hour, she called on Australians to be the best version of themselves ahead of the Victorian state election in six weeks.

Cathy McGowan (left) endorsed Ms Haines to be her successor in 2019. (ABC News)

"Let's take Helen's legacy of being our best selves, of being transparent and open and honest, but good to this election," she says.

"And let's just see if we can't, from a community like Indi, really be the change we want to see.

" Call out bad behaviour, stop the violence. "

Loading...

Locals still grappling with the attack on Helen Haines are gathering for a vigil in Wodonga tonight.

Ms McGowan said she hoped the orange cockatoos worn by supporters of the beloved Indi MP could symbolise a community moving forward.

"We've got a lot of cockatoos flying around and they come together in groups and they make a lot noise, but they're very supportive of each other as flocks," she said.

"That's our symbol tonight of us coming together as a community … We're not going to let violence win."

World.content:

Executive chef Alejandro Saravia has crafted a flavour-packed itinerary across Latin America, right in the heart of Martin Place. First stop: Mexico. Slices of raw swordfish and crisp cucumber are rested in a cold, citrusy broth that hints of winter melon. The bluefin tuna belly tostada is a smoky and spicy affair with fiery salsa macha tempered by roasted avocado cream.

Next up is Argentina, with a well-charred and attentively seasoned Black Market Denver steak, melting gracefully on the palate and paired with tangy chimichurri.

A quick journey to Brazil calls for hearty, coconut-scented moqueca, the stew loaded with cod, prawn, scallop and squid, paired with steamed rice and toasted cassava flour.

The elegant dining room may be inside the heritage-listed former Sydney General Post Office, but with such a roving menu, and a wine list that follows the brief, you could well be in Buenos Aires.

Must-order dish: Black Market Denver steak with chimichurri.

World.title: Ciro’s
World.content:
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Judging by the flocks of locals loading up with Ciro’s takeaway boxes, Thirroul residents are quite aware their town has some of the best pizza in the state. The base is thin, blistered and subtly sour, and you can also have it in flatbread form to run through stracciatella with pistachio vinaigrette, or whipped ricotta underneath charred butternut pumpkin.

A pizzeria is only as good as its margherita, of course, and this one has the ideal balance of San Marzano tomato sweetness and creamy dollops of fior di latte. The white-sauced pizzas are just as good, including the garlicky, earthy “Shroom” number, which goes great guns with a house orange wine made by co-owner Joel Mucci’s label Benson and Mooch.

House-made limoncello also feels essential, and if you’re in the market for something more protein-heavy, ask about the wood-fired rice with confit chicken.

Good to know: On Mondays, only pizzas are available, but all of them are $20.

World.title: No wonder exam results are on the slide
World.content:
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

David Prest of Thrumster writes: “When I started my Mechanical Engineering Certificate in 1975, I was forced to get a calculator as the rest of the class were worried that my use of logarithm tables and slide-rule (C8) wouldn’t be fast enough during the exam. I still have that calculator but the logarithm table book and the slide-rule have since gone.”

Perhaps Valerie Bray of East Killara can help: “I still have my old slide-rule and book of logarithm tables. The problem is, I’ve forgotten how to use them.”

“I once sat for an exam with an array of jelly beans (for sugar),” says Pasquale Vartuli of Pennant Hills. “I noticed an examiner looking at them to see if I had inscribed any messages on them. ”

Ian Nicholls of Baulkham Hills makes a good point “Years ago, during an engineering lecture, the topic of exam nerves came up. Our stern old school professor said self-control was important and went on to tell us that when he had a panic attack during an exam, he had to stab his hand with his pair of compasses to regain control.”

Edward Loong of Milsons Point (C8) has a fair bit to unpack regarding his new-found fame: “No, Graham Lum, I ain’t Edmund – he’s my older brother! Loong story. But, yes, Maureen Lysaght, Nancy is my older sister. Small world, indeed.”

Matt Shea October 21, 2026 Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Finally, Alfi Eatery & Bar is here. This Mediterranean-influenced venue in the Everton Plaza precinct was intended to open in the winter. Given its ginormous size, though – 350 seats spread across 800 square metres – 80 or 90 days doesn’t seem so bad, especially when Ghanem Group only just came off the launch of the similarly large-format Hotel Terminus on Fish Lane. Alfi opens Thursday in Everton Park. Markus Ravik “There are elements that get easier about opening these venues, and elements that remain challenging,” managing director Nehme Ghanem says. “You can’t expect it to be smooth sailing ... But it also gets a little easier in some ways – back when we opened Byblos [in 2006], I was literally sleeping there, working 20 hours a day.” “We’re definitely more versed in what to expect now,” Nehme’s brother and co-director, Adonis Ghanem, adds. “You learn something with every opening and that experience helps, but every venue has its own challenges, team and audience, so you can never assume what worked somewhere else will automatically work again.”

You can see it in the shrewd location in the middle of a suburb going through a significant demographic shift, and the Amalfi-inspired treatment, which flows effortlessly from a low-key, airy bistro into an expansive drinks garden. World.title: ‘Don’t let violence win’: McGowan’s plea as Haines fights for life
World.content:
PoliticsFederalHaines attack ‘Don’t let violence win’: McGowan’s plea as Haines fights for life Rob Harris Updated October 21, 2026 — 8:13pm ,first published 7:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Former independent MP Cathy McGowan has warned that the attack on Helen Haines has struck at the heart of Australian democracy, revealing that women across the electorate fear for their safety and question whether they can enter public life without facing violence. In an emotional address to hundreds of residents gathered at a community vigil in Wodonga on Wednesday night, McGowan said the assault on her Indi successor had left north-east Victoria grappling with grief, shame and the confronting reality that one of its own had been attacked in the community she represented. Former independent member for Indi Cathy McGowan embraces a community member. Eddie Jim Haines, 65, remains in a critical but stable condition in hospital, having had both legs amputated after a vehicle drove into her outside her Wangaratta electorate office on Monday afternoon. Brendan Nugent, 43, of Tarrawingee, near Wangaratta, made no application for bail when he appeared before Wangaratta Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday morning over the incident.



“That this happened in our town, [allegedly] by one of our community members, to one of us. In the attack on Helen, it is an attack on all of us,” McGowan said. “It’s so very hard to get our minds around.” Loading A message of hope from Governor-General Sam Mostyn drew an emotional response from the crowd. “We now know that Helen’s heart and head are good. She is going to get better, and she is going to come back fighting.” McGowan said the community was confronting something far more profound than the shocking violence inflicted on a much-loved local MP.



Flowers lined the front of Haines’ second electoral office, in High Street, Wodonga, on Wednesday, with handwritten well wishes from the community. The city’s water tower was illuminated in her honour. Related Article Haines attack Helen Haines attack as it happened: Indi MP has both legs amputated, husband confirms; alleged attacker charged “There is another level of grief, different and deeper from the actual violence, from the sorrow, the shame and the hurt,” McGowan said. “It’s about Helen in her role as our elected representative – in attacking her, we intuit that this is an attack on our political system, on our democracy.” McGowan, whose historic 2013 election victory helped launch the modern community independents movement, said the attack had shaken the grassroots political culture that had defined Indi for more than a decade. She said many of those who had helped elect Haines were struggling to comprehend how the democratic process they had worked to strengthen could become the target of such violence.



Locals held cardboard cockatoos in tribute to Haines. Eddie Jim Orange cockatoos, emblems of McGowan’s campaigns which have also come to represent Haines, were being handed out by volunteers at the vigil. They were designed by a local artist and made with recycled corflutes. In a show of cross-party solidarity, state MPs Tim McCurdy, Bill Tilley, Cindy McLeish and Annabelle Cleeland joined nine local mayors from across north-east Victoria to condemn the growing wave of intimidation targeting public officials. In a joint statement, the regional leaders warned that threats and violence “have absolutely no place in our democracy or in our communities”. Civic leaders from Alpine, Benalla, Indigo, Mansfield, Murrindindi, Strathbogie, Towong, Wangaratta and Wodonga declared that while robust disagreement was essential to democracy, targeted harassment abandoned basic humanity. Refusing to let hostility undermine civic participation, the group pledged that “decency still outweighs division” as they urged the public to reject political hatred and safeguard the standards of public service. Michael Gobel, mayor of Wodonga, told the crowd that it was a nation, region and community united in shock.



“We are neighbours, we are friends, and we are colleagues. And while we may not always agree, we share a deep connection to this region and to each other,” he said. McGowan said conversations across Indi since Monday had exposed the deeper scars left by the attack, particularly among women already living with the threat of violence. Helen Haines with her predecessor in the seat of Indi, Cathy McGowan. Alex Ellinghausen Many women are scared for their own safety and the safety of women in public positions, she said. She acknowledged the anguish of Haines’ family and staff, the Wangaratta locals who intervened during the attack and the medical teams working to save the MP’s life.



She urged residents not to allow their grief to harden into fear or retreat from political participation and instead challenged the community to make next month’s Victorian election a demonstration of the democratic values that had been threatened. Related Article Analysis

Haines attack Helen Haines once said she had no mortal enemies. That remark hangs heavily over this town “Let’s make it the best ever, not only here in [the electoral district of] Benambra but across Victoria,” she said. McGowan said the response to Monday’s attack must be to strengthen, rather than surrender, the democratic culture campaigners had helped build. “My ask, in closing, is that we don’t let violence win, that we ensure the legacy of this attack on Helen will be a stronger, more vibrant and effective democracy,” she said. “And from a personal perspective, all candidates and especially women, know they can run for office and be safe.”

World.title: Man arrested after entering WA MP’s electorate office with ‘nunchucks’
World.content:
NationalWACrime Man arrested after entering WA MP’s electorate office with ‘nunchucks’ Hannah Murphy and Hamish Hastie October 21, 2026 — 7:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items.
